title: Typing-indicator KV prefetch for hibernated chat sessions
idea: When a response finishes, the server spills that session's KV cache to NVMe/CXL flash. It prefetches the cache back into HBM when the client sends a 'user started typing' or 'tab focused' event. This jumps from the nanosecond scale of HBM to the 5-60 s of human think time between turns, which hides a 10-200 ms restore completely.

physics.key_insight: Client typing/focus events give 2-20 s of lead time, against <1 s from scheduler hints. An 8k-context 70B KV (2.7 GB) then streams SSD-to-HBM directly, removing the host-DRAM KV tier.
physics.killer_doubt: NAND wear: append-only spill of ~3 GB/s new KV per 8-GPU node is ~280 TB/day, ~9 drives at 1 DWPD. Workaround: spill-on-evict, FP8/MLA KV (4-10x fewer bytes).
physics.decisive_experiment: Instrument an open chat front-end to log focus/typing lead times. Replay the traces on one 8xGPU vLLM+LMCache node with SSD-only against host-DRAM tiers; report TTFT p99, resident sessions/GB and NAND TB/day. <$100k.
physics.prior_art: CachedAttention/AttentionStore (ATC'24) scheduler-aware disk prefetch (via search snippet); Mooncake, LMCache, Dynamo KVBM. Client-signal prefetch not found.

innovation.key_insight: Human think time (5-60 s) exceeds NVMe restore (~1-2 s for a 10 GB, 32k-token 70B KV), so flash can replace the DRAM/CXL KV tier with no visible TTFT cost.
innovation.killer_doubt: Aggregate flash bandwidth: 200 sessions per node, each turning every ~40 s at 10 GB, need ~50 GB/s, about half of eight Gen5 drives. False-positive prefetches multiply that.
innovation.decisive_experiment: vLLM+LMCache with an NVMe-only KV tier (no DRAM tier). Replay multi-turn chat traces plus a 50-user typing-signal study. Measure TTFT, prefetch hit and false-positive rates, and DRAM saved against a Mooncake-style DRAM tier. About $80k.
innovation.prior_art: CachedAttention (2024) prefetches from disk at queue entry; LMCache, Mooncake and Cake tier KV to disk. Typing-signal trigger: none found (via search snippet).

title: Diode-steered capacitor stack: one transistor, sixteen bits per pillar
idea: IFR: one switch serves a whole tower of bits. Deposit 16 plate-electrode/dielectric tiers around one vertical storage pillar, with a thin oxide Schottky diode in each tier between plate and capacitor, so a plate-line pulse forward-biases only the selected tier onto the shared pillar node, read through a single access transistor; tiers come from deposition and one hole etch.

physics.key_insight: DRAM analog of Intel/Kepler 1T-nC FeRAM: a per-tier oxide Schottky diode replaces ferroelectric coercivity as plate-line selector; clamp-write works one-way; nodes use floating-gate 3D-NAND recess process.
physics.killer_doubt: 0.27 fF tiers share onto a ~1.5 fF pillar (~75 mV signal), forcing a gain-FET read; a ~60 nm hole makes density 2-4x at 16-32 tiers, not 24x.
physics.decisive_experiment: University-fab 4-tier stack in 100-200 nm holes (TiN plates/ZrO2/recessed node/IGZO-RuOx Schottky/pillar): measure clamp-write, read charge, reverse leakage (<20 aA/tier at 85 C), unselected-tier disturb. ~$600k.
physics.prior_art: Intel EP4016625 3D-FRAM plate lines; Kepler Computing 1TnC stacked ferroelectric pillar capacitors (via search snippet); diode-steered linear-capacitor version not found.

innovation.key_insight: Per-tier oxide Schottky diodes plus plate-line selection replace 15 of 16 access transistors: a linear-capacitor DRAM analogue of 1T-nC FeRAM, built with the 3D-NAND recess flow, no EUV.
innovation.killer_doubt: 0.2-0.9 fF tiers read destructively through a one-way diode: ~15-60 mV. Reverse leakage must stay <2e-17 A at 85 C (barrier >=1.0 eV). 3x 1-beta needs >=48 tiers.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Make a planar BEOL test chip in a university fab: one access FET, 4 MIM capacitors, each steered by a Pt/IGZO Schottky. Measure 85 C retention, read signal, disturb over 1e9 plate pulses, diode endurance to 1e12. ~$300k.
innovation.prior_art: 1T-nC stacked FeRAM (plate-selected, shared node; Sogang 2026 thesis, stacked-FE patents) (via search snippet). Diode-steered linear-DRAM version: none found.

title: ESCO shared-savings contracts for reclaiming cold DRAM pages
idea: Like energy-service companies paid from a client's utility savings, a vendor installs a page-temperature profiler and transparent tiering agent that moves cold pages to compressed or CXL far memory, and is paid a fixed share of the DRAM purchases the customer avoids.

physics.key_insight: Tiering is free and proven (Meta TMO saves 20-32% of memory), but enterprise fleets skip it for risk and effort. Payment from avoided DRAM buys at 4x prices aligns incentives.
physics.killer_doubt: Savings are counterfactual: purchases are avoided only at 4-6-year refresh, so the baseline is gameable. VMware already compresses memory; adopters may save ~10-20%, only ~2-4% of world bits.
physics.decisive_experiment: Pilot on 200-500 servers at 3-5 enterprise customers (~$400k): profile cold pages at a 2-minute threshold, enable zswap or CXL tiering, track resident-memory cut and p99 latency for 6 months, and trial an IPMVP-style baseline.
physics.prior_art: Meta TMO (ASPLOS'22); Google zswap far memory (ASPLOS'19); MemVerge, Kove software tiers; VMware memory compression. Shared-savings memory contracts: none found.

innovation.key_insight: Negabytes: zero-capex, savings-shared reclaim targets the non-hyperscale fleets that never deployed TMO/zswap; pulling the freed DDR5 and reselling it at 4x prices makes savings metered and adds compatible supply.
innovation.killer_doubt: VMware's NVMe memory tiering went GA in VCF 9.0, June 2025 (via search snippet), inside existing licenses; below ~15% p99-safe reclaim, the savings share cannot cover service costs.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Three 90-day enterprise pilots (VMware, KVM, Kubernetes): DAMON/esxtop coldness profiling, then zswap/NVMe/CXL tiering under a p99 SLO guarantee. Measure GB freed, pull or swap DIMMs, and test a third-party M&V baseline. ~$300k.
innovation.prior_art: Energy ESCOs/IPMVP; Meta TMO (ASPLOS 2022); Google far memory (ASPLOS 2019); VMware VCF 9 tiering (via search snippet). Shared-savings memory contracts: none found.

title: Drum-era SOAP placement makes shift-register memories act random-access
idea: Revive the IBM 650's Symbolic Optimal Assembly Program, which placed each next instruction where the rotating drum would be when needed: a compiler/controller lays out tensors, KV-cache pages and weights in shift-register arrays (CCD strings, racetracks, delay loops) so the next word reaches the read port just in time, with out-of-order prefetch hiding the rest.

physics.key_insight: LLM decode reads every weight and KV byte once per token in fixed order, so a ~33 ms loop fits. Per-lap regeneration doubles as refresh. Shifts cost ~86 fJ/bit.
physics.killer_doubt: It needs serial arrays that exist: imec IGZO CCDs show CTE ~98%, and a 64-stage lap needs >=0.999. Unpredictable 20-40% of traffic sees ~10 us without a front tier.
physics.decisive_experiment: Trace-driven simulator ($150k) of decode, prefill and training traces on a serial-string array (shift rate, CTE, lap length) with an SRAM front buffer. Report the bytes served within 30 ns-equivalent and pJ/bit vs HBM.
physics.prior_art: IBM 650 SOAP; 1970s CCD/bubble major-minor loops; ShiftsReduce racetrack placement (Khan et al., TACO 2019) (via search snippet); none found for LLM-sweep timing.

innovation.key_insight: LLM traffic is mostly predictable: weights stream in fixed order and KV caches are append-then-scan. A just-in-time placement controller lets us-latency shift strings (CCD, racetrack) serve it.
innovation.killer_doubt: A 64-bit string at imec's ~6 MHz takes ~10 us per rotation; averaging under 40 ns needs misses below ~0.2%. Data-dependent top-k attention and batch churn may break that.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Trace-driven simulator (~$80k): replay vLLM/SGLang decode and training traces against a parameterized shift-string memory (length, clock, ports). Report the fraction of bytes served within 40 ns versus clock rate. This sets I-10793's clock target.
innovation.prior_art: IBM 650 SOAP (1950s); ShiftsReduce, TU Dresden, ACM TACO 2019, shift-minimizing racetrack placement (via search snippet); SanDisk/SK hynix HBF serves weights at flash latency.

title: Fairchild CCD memory reborn as vertical IGZO buried-channel CCD
idea: 1970s CCD memories died from serial access and silicon dark current that filled potential wells within ms when hot. Stack 64-128 gate tiers 3D-NAND-style around a vertical IGZO channel, store electron packets under alternate gates and shift a few stages to a top sense node. IGZO has no holes to invert the channel and a ~3.1 eV gap, so thermal generation stays negligible at 125 C and packets last seconds or more.

physics.key_insight: Charge shifts through a semiconductor channel, so wear is gate stress only (imec >1e10 cycles). A buried IGO/IGZO heterochannel keeps packets off interface traps, the main CTE loss.
physics.killer_doubt: imec reports CTE >98% at ~4-6 MHz; ~120 transfers need >=0.999 each (89% survives). A 60-stage shift at 4 MHz takes 15 us, ~300x DRAM tRC.
physics.decisive_experiment: University-fab planar 3-4 phase CCDs, surface versus buried IGO/IGZO heterochannel with fat-zero bias (~$300k): CTE versus clock 4-200 MHz at 25-125 C. Go if >=0.999 at >=50 MHz.
physics.prior_art: imec IEDM 2024 planar and IMW 2026 vertical IGZO CCD; buried-channel oxide CCD: none found (via search snippet); in-study I-10793, I-01064.

innovation.key_insight: A buried heterochannel keeps packets off interface traps. CTI is mostly modelable deferred charge, so decision feedback at the string-top sense node could relax CTE ~0.9999 toward ~0.999 (estimate).
innovation.killer_doubt: Trap kinetics, not mobility: transport over a 30 nm gate is ~15 ps at 10 cm2/Vs, yet imec shows CTE >98% at 4-6 MHz. ~120 transfers need >=0.999 each.
innovation.decisive_experiment: University-fab planar 4-phase CCDs, surface vs buried IGO/IGZO heterochannel (~$300k): CTE and deferred-charge profile vs clock 5-500 MHz at 25-125 C, replayed through a DFE corrector. Go if corrected loss <1e-3/transfer at >=100 MHz.
innovation.prior_art: imec IGZO CCD buffer memory (IEDM 2024; IMW 2026); LSST deferred-charge correction (Snyder 2021, via search snippet). Buried-channel or DFE-corrected oxide CCD memory: none found.

title: Zero-helium wafer cooling with low-pressure hydrogen backside gas
idea: Ideal: etch/deposition chucks that need no helium. Closest achievable: run electrostatic-chuck backside cooling on 5-15 Torr H2 (thermal conductivity 0.18 vs 0.15 W/m-K for He) from on-site PEM electrolysis, with flow-limiting orifices and an N2-purged plenum so any leak stays below the flammability limit after exhaust dilution.

physics.key_insight: H2 beats He at both limits: continuum conductivity 0.18 versus 0.15 W/m-K, and ~1.2-2x free-molecular transfer per Torr. Its higher Paschen minimum (~270 versus ~150 V) also cuts backside arcing.
physics.killer_doubt: H2 thermal accommodation on real, film-coated wafer backsides is unmeasured (~0.1-0.3); at the low end gap transfer drops ~2x. Plus NFPA 55/SEMI S2 qualification in every chamber.
physics.decisive_experiment: Swap He for H2 at 5-30 Torr on one 300 mm etch chamber. Map wafer temperature with thermocouple wafers under 2-5 kW bias, measure HAR oxide etch rate and selectivity drift, and log exhaust H2 against the 4% LFL. ~$300k.
physics.prior_art: ESC patents list hydrogen beside He/Ar/N2; vendors moved to N2/Ar despite arcing limits (via search snippet). No production H2 backside use found.

innovation.key_insight: Free-molecular gap conductance scales as (g+1)/(g-1)/sqrt(m): H2 gives ~2x helium per unit accommodation, and its Paschen minimum (~270 V vs ~155 V) lowers backside-arc risk.
innovation.killer_doubt: Unverified share of fab helium that is backside cooling (A2 flags it), and plasma impact of ~0.5-2 sccm H2 leaking into fluorocarbon HAR etch; H2 LFL is 4%.
innovation.decisive_experiment: University ICP etcher with thermocouple wafers: wafer temperature with He versus H2 at 5-15 Torr under 1-3 kW bias, plus HAR etch rate, selectivity and profile with 0-2 sccm H2 bleed. ~$250k.
innovation.prior_art: None found (one search): ESC patents name He, N2 or Ar backside gas (via search snippet). H2 is already a W CVD and epi gas.

title: Gen-10.5 display-glass panels stacked with twenty tiers of oxide-TFT DRAM
idea: Ideal: memory sold like window glass. Closest: use Gen-10.5 display lines (~9.9 m2 panels) to build 2T0C/1T1C tiers from In-free ZnSnO TFTs, Mo/Al lines and planar Al2O3/TiO2 caps (TFT off-current ~1e-21 A/um makes small caps adequate), 4-5 masks per tier with panel nanoimprint at F~0.25 um, 20 tiers stacked at <=350 C.

physics.key_insight: Oxide-TFT leakage makes planar caps enough: 0.25 um2 of 10 nm TiO2/Al2O3 (k~30) holds ~6 fF. 20 tiers give ~5 TB/m2 at a cost per m2 ~100-1000x below DRAM wafers.
physics.killer_doubt: No panel tool images 0.25 um at ~50 nm overlay: FPD steppers resolve ~1.5 um with ~0.3-0.5 um overlay. And 100 patterning steps (20 tiers x 5 masks) compound defects.
physics.decisive_experiment: Build two tiers of ZnSnO 1T1C arrays at F=0.25 um on 200 mm glass with a commercial step-and-repeat imprinter. Measure overlay, killer defects/cm2 per mask, Vt sigma and 85 C retention, then feed a panel-maker cost-per-mask-m2 model. ~$600k.
physics.prior_art: Phase B B2-19 panel 3D oxide memory; SEL CAAC-IGZO DOSRAM; R16 DROP of 2 um display-glass memory (I-03879); Canon NIL; large-area wire-grid imprint.

innovation.key_insight: Display fabs process ~170x more area per month than a DRAM fab at under half the capex; transistor-written oxide gain cells need no HAR capacitor, EUV, W, Hf or He.
innovation.killer_doubt: Economics need F<=0.3 um with ~8F2 cells over 20 tiers. Gen-10.5 FPD steppers resolve ~1.2-1.5 um, giving ~37 GB/m2 and ~$13/GB, worse than DDR5's $1.48/GB cost.
innovation.decisive_experiment: On Gen-2/3.5 glass at a display R&D line: two-tier ZTO 2T0C arrays by step-and-repeat NIL at F=0.3-0.5 um; measure tier overlay after 350 C cycles, Vt sigma and 85 C retention. ~$700k.
innovation.prior_art: Phase B N-38 panel-level oxide memory; SEL DOSRAM/NOSRAM CAAC-IGZO memory on silicon; no DRAM on display panel lines found (one search).

title: ECC-paid capacitor: let the code, not the capacitor, carry the last 4 sigma
idea: Today's ~50 mV sense budget exists so that every one of ~1.7e10 cells reads correctly at ~7 sigma of sense-amp (SA) offset and coupling noise, with only on-die SEC as backup. Re-centre the array on a raw BER target of 1e-4 per read. A t=8 BCH code (80 check bits per 512 data bits) in the memory controller or HBM/CXL logic base die absorbs the errors; optionally the SA fires two extra comparator thresholds to hand one soft-information bit per cell to a NAND-style soft decoder. With dV_min of 26 mV instead of 50 mV, the ZrO2/TiN pillar storage node can hold ~2.7 fF instead of 5.4 fF on the same 512-cell bitline: ~640 nm tall instead of 1,300 nm. An SA's offset is static, so codewords run along the row (each bit through a different SA), and outlier SAs are fused out at test like today's column repair. The same rule gives a 0.6 fF cell on a 64-cell local bitline in a 3D tier.

physics.key_insight: SA offset is static, so row-wise codewords make offset errors near-iid; t=8 BCH at 1e-4 raw BER fails ~2e-17 per read, halving capacitor height (AR 62 to 30).
physics.killer_doubt: Row-correlated errors share one codeword: half-margin cells may flip at ~2x fewer hammer activations (~500); a 13 fA tail cell droops 0.31 of 0.5 V in 64 ms.
physics.decisive_experiment: DRAM Bender/SoftMC on DDR5: emulate half charge with truncated tRAS restore; map BER versus margin, temperature and hammer count; test whether errors along rows are iid. ~$100k, six months.
physics.prior_art: Hi-ECC (Wilkerson et al., ISCA 2010); DDR5 on-die ECC; NAND soft-decision LDPC; approximate DRAM. Capacitor redesigned around ECC margin: none found.

innovation.key_insight: Static SA offset lets row-wise codewords spread each SA's errors. A t=8 BCH at raw BER 1e-4 halves capacitor height (AR 62 to 30); 3D tiers need only ~0.6 fF.
innovation.killer_doubt: Non-iid errors (VRT, pattern coupling, SA-offset drift) may burst past t=8 per 512 b. Check bits add 9-21 points of area against a 2x shorter pillar; ~8,800-electron cells are softer.
innovation.decisive_experiment: DRAM Bender/FPGA on 20-50 DDR5 dies: emulate half signal with a cut tRAS restore and lowered VPP, then log error positions per 512 b codeword across 1e12+ reads and 45-95 C. Fit burst tails against t=8. ~$150k.
innovation.prior_art: DDR5 on-die ECC and the LPDDR6/HBM4 ECC trend; Hi-ECC (ISCA 2010); NAND LDPC soft sensing; ECC(552,512) gain-cell refresh study (arXiv 2607.16042, via prior snippet).

title: SSD-controller playbook: 28nm CXL controller with page-level LDPC
idea: Adapted from NAND flash, which became cheap by pairing weak cells with smart controllers: a 28 nm CXL memory controller built in existing mature logic fabs applies 4 KB-codeword LDPC, with an on-chip SRAM write-combining buffer for read-modify-write, to unmodified commodity or lower-grade DRAM, exposing a byte-addressable device that tolerates raw BER ~1e-4.

physics.key_insight: Page-level codes turn the retention tail into a parity budget. At raw BER 1e-4, a 4 KB BCH needs ~1.5% parity (t~30), buying 4-16x refresh relaxation with no new fab.
physics.killer_doubt: DDR5 runs in-DRAM TRR inside REF commands, so 8x fewer REFs means 8x fewer hammer-mitigation slots at HC~1k; RFM/PRAC is needed. Self-refresh cannot be stretched.
physics.decisive_experiment: Build an FPGA CXL/DDR5 controller with 4 KB BCH/LDPC. Run commodity and retention-reject DIMMs at 0.25-2 s refresh, 45-85 C, with RFM on. Log raw BER, VRT and hammer flips for 3 months. ~$500k.
physics.prior_art: Hi-ECC (ISCA 2010): strong BCH cut eDRAM refresh 93% (via search snippet); Morphable ECC (DSN 2015); patent US10691532; triage N-62/N-63.

innovation.key_insight: NAND playbook for DRAM: a mature-node CXL controller with strong ECC makes rejects and relaxed refresh usable, and gives new oxide/3D cells a raw-BER-1e-4 landing zone (N-62).
innovation.killer_doubt: 4 KB codewords make each random 64 B write a 4 KB read-modify-write (64x traffic) unless the SRAM buffer coalesces; VRT may push raw BER past 1e-4 at 8x tREFI.
innovation.decisive_experiment: FPGA CXL card with BCH/LDPC over commodity and reject DDR4/DDR5 DIMMs at 4-8x tREFI, 85 C: log raw-BER tail incl. VRT for weeks, post-ECC errors past 1e15 bits, bandwidth on real traces. ~$400k.
innovation.prior_art: Hi-ECC (2010), ArchShield (2013), LOT-ECC (2012); X-PPR recycled-DDR4 CXL repair (2025, via search snippet); Microchip/Astera CXL controllers. LDPC plus relaxed refresh: none found.

title: Erasure-flagging sense amps: weak decisions marked, not guessed
idea: Limit: accept a raw bit error rate of 1e-4. A second, time-delayed sample in each SA flags bits that resolved slowly (small |dV|) as erasures, and a short per-burst erasure code corrects up to 4 flagged bits per 64 B with little overhead, since known-location errors cost half the parity.

physics.key_insight: Slow SA resolution marks near-threshold bits as erasures. Known-location errors cost half the parity: 4 erasures per 512 bits need only a d=5 code (~20 bits, 3.9%).
physics.killer_doubt: Fully leaked junction/GIDL tail cells read confidently wrong and unflagged. If >50% of errors at 2-4x tREFI are confident, gain falls to ~15% parity. Flag latch: ~3-7% die.
physics.decisive_experiment: DRAM Bender on DDR4/DDR5: read each row at reduced and nominal tRCD and treat mismatches as erasure flags. Measure the flagged fraction of retention and low-margin errors at 2-8x tREFI. ~$80k.
physics.prior_art: NAND soft-decision LDPC; Razor delayed-sample timing detection (MICRO 2003); XED on-die error flags (ISCA 2016); FLY-DRAM; Phase B N-62.

innovation.key_insight: SA resolution time encodes |dV|; flagging slow decisions turns margin errors into erasures at half the parity cost, so ECC-paid capacitors (N-62) shrink further or refresh stretches 2-4x.
innovation.killer_doubt: If most raw errors at 1e-4 are confident flips (VRT, fully leaked cells) rather than small-|dV| ones, under ~50% get flagged; a per-SA flag latch adds ~3-5% die.
innovation.decisive_experiment: DRAM Bender on 50 DDR4/DDR5 chips: read rows at nominal and reduced tRCD as a flag proxy, then at stretched refresh measure the fraction of errors flagged. Pass: over 80%. ~$60k.
innovation.prior_art: Static weak-cell erasure maps (US 8,898,544); Solar-DRAM reduced-tRCD weak profiles (via search snippet); NAND soft-decision LDPC; IBM chipkill chip marking.

title: Minify $/m2 3000x: roll-to-roll nanoimprinted memory foil
idea: Run steel or polyimide foil webs through R2R UV-nanoimprint at ~100 nm half-pitch with sputtered IGZO channels and anodized-aluminum high-k capacitors, making 0.4 um2 gain cells on kilometers of foil, then laminate and slit into memory ribbons.

physics.key_insight: Transistor-written IGZO gain cell passes the endurance wall; DRAM cost parity is ~$440/m2 at 300 GB/m2, and one 1 m R2R line (~5e6 m2/yr) could make ~1.5 EB/yr.
physics.killer_doubt: Multilevel 100 nm overlay on foil: PI moves 10-20 ppm/K plus humidity, and 10 ppm over 1 cm is 100 nm; realistic $150-300/m2 gives ~$0.5-1/GB, not $0.1.
physics.decisive_experiment: SAIL-style single multilevel stamp on PI-on-glass or steel foil (~$400k, university NIL tool): 1 Mb IGZO 2T gain-cell array at 100-200 nm; map overlay, killer defects/cm2, Vt sigma, retention at 85 C.
physics.prior_art: HP Labs SAIL R2R oxide TFTs, ~15 cm2/Vs (via search snippet); PragmatIC FlexIC/FlexRV IGZO at ~0.6-0.8 um. Sub-micron R2R oxide memory array: none found.

innovation.key_insight: An active-matrix display backplane is already a 1T1C DRAM refreshed at 60 Hz. SAIL-imprinted IGZO at ~100 nm on a web gives ~200 GB/m2, a ~$100M line and no EUV.
innovation.killer_doubt: SAIL is proven only near ~1 um. At 100 nm, resist steps must hold ~10 nm across a metre-wide web. At $100-200/m2, not $20-40, cost is $0.5-1/GB.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Imprint a 4-level SAIL mask on polyimide-on-glass to make a 64x64 IGZO 1T1C/2T0C array at 100-150 nm. Measure Ioff, Vt spread, cell yield and 85 C retention. Then run one roll-to-roll pass at 500 nm to map distortion failures.
innovation.prior_art: HP Labs SAIL roll-to-roll a-Si TFTs; a-IGZO SAIL TFTs (IEICE 2018) (via search snippet); Thin Film Electronics printed memory; PragmatIC IGZO FlexICs; project N-38.

title: LLNL ZFP arrays, fixed: lossy compression as a page attribute
idea: ZFP fixed-rate lossy floating-point compression saw low adoption because codes had to be rewritten around compressed-array classes. Put a ZFP engine in the memory controller and let the OS mark pages 'fp64 lossy, 16 bits/value', so unmodified HPC codes get 4x compression with bounded error.

physics.key_insight: Fixed-rate lossy coding gives a guaranteed 4x with none of the page fragmentation that hurt lossless capacity compression. A CXL expander serving 'lossy fp64' NUMA pages eases adoption.
physics.killer_doubt: A 64 B writeback read-modify-writes a 4^3 block (512 B to 128 B), re-quantizing 56 untouched values. Drift over 1e4 timesteps may break bounds, and the controller needs array shape.
physics.decisive_experiment: Run LULESH, an AMReX hydro code and HPCG for 1e4 steps on a userfaultfd page emulator (ZFP rate 8-24, RMW buffer); compare drift against full precision. Then an Agilex CXL Type-3 FPGA prototype for latency. ~$400k.
physics.prior_art: zfp compressed arrays (LLNL), FPGA ZFP codecs (DE-ZFP), lossy-truncation memory-controller patents; no inline ZFP capacity controller found (via search snippet).

innovation.key_insight: Fixed rate makes compressed memory addressable by arithmetic (no metadata, no fragmentation), so a CXL Type-3 'lossy fp64' NUMA node gives unmodified HPC binaries a guaranteed 2-4x.
innovation.killer_doubt: A 64 B writeback re-quantizes a whole 4^3 block (56 untouched values); drift over 1e4 timesteps at 16 bit/value may break solver bounds. HPC is ~5% of server DRAM.
innovation.decisive_experiment: userfaultfd page emulator running LULESH, an AMReX hydro code and HPCG for 1e4 steps at ZFP rates 8-32 with an RMW buffer, measuring drift versus FP64; then an Agilex CXL FPGA prototype. ~$250k.
innovation.prior_art: AVR (ICPP'19) and MemSZ lossy LLC/memory compression (Chalmers); zfp compressed arrays (LLNL); lossy-controller patent US 11347650. No inline ZFP NUMA device found.

title: Genome Project biologist: open atlas of real memory contents
idea: Biology took off once the genome was sequenced. An opt-in agent samples hashed, entropy-profiled page snapshots (never raw data) from volunteer fleets and publishes a 'memory atlas': the share of zero pages, duplicates, near-duplicates, compressible types, pointer density and cold data by workload. About $800k.

physics.key_insight: Outside three hyperscalers, nobody has published memory contents by workload. An on-host-aggregated atlas would calibrate the S-score of every compression, dedup and tiering idea in this study for under $1M.
physics.killer_doubt: It saves nothing by itself. It needs >=1,000 non-hyperscale hosts across >=10 workload classes, and raw page hashes enable confirmation attacks, so only on-host aggregates may leave the host.
physics.decisive_experiment: Ship an eBPF/DAMON agent with on-host zero/dup/entropy/coldness histograms (no hashes leave the host) to 3 partner fleets (university HPC, a mid-size SaaS, a CDN) for 90 days, then publish v0.1. ~$300k.
physics.prior_art: Google far memory (ASPLOS'19), Meta TMO (ASPLOS'22), Microsoft Pond (ASPLOS'23) publish single-fleet statistics; no open cross-fleet atlas found.

innovation.key_insight: Outside hyperscalers, nobody publishes what DRAM holds by workload. An on-host-aggregated atlas calibrates every compression, dedup and tiering idea here, and wedges into reclaim tooling at 4x prices.
innovation.killer_doubt: It saves nothing itself. It needs >=1,000 non-hyperscale hosts in >=10 workload classes, page hashes allow confirmation attacks, and hyperscaler data may already bound reclaimable memory at 20-50%.
innovation.decisive_experiment: eBPF/DAMON agent emitting only on-host zero/dup/entropy/coldness histograms, run 90 days on 3-5 partner fleets (university HPC, mid-size SaaS, AI inference). ~$250k. Advance if any class differs >1.5x from hyperscaler figures.
innovation.prior_art: Meta TMO, Google far memory/zswap, Microsoft Pond; Meta reports 10-20% zero pages among swapped pages (via search snippet). No public cross-fleet content atlas found.

title: All-IGZO monolithic memory: n-only periphery in the same tiers
idea: TRIZ #33 Homogeneity: build sense amps, decoders and drivers from the same IGZO transistors as the 2T0C array, using bootstrapped n-only (pseudo-CMOS) circuits, so each BEOL tier is a complete memory with no CMOS underneath. The whole stack can sit on any logic die's metal stack.

physics.key_insight: 1970s NMOS DRAMs proved n-only periphery; 2T0C cells give >1e3 read-current ratios, so 100-300 mV TFT offsets still sense. Memory on any logic BEOL, no Si periphery.
physics.killer_doubt: IGZO PBTI and hydrogen drift of ~50-100 mV over 1e10+ periphery cycles at 85-105 C, and ~3-5x Si periphery area per tier, may cut array efficiency to ~25-35%.
physics.decisive_experiment: University BEOL IGZO run (~$400k): 4-16 kb 2T0C macro with bootstrapped n-only decoders and auto-zeroed latch sensing; measure 50-100 ns access, offset and drift after 1e10 cycles at 105 C.
physics.prior_art: 1970s NMOS DRAMs; IGZO gate-driver-on-array; SEL DOSRAM uses Si periphery; no all-oxide-periphery macro found (via search snippet); Phase B N-35, N-27.

innovation.key_insight: A tier carrying its own oxide periphery needs no FEOL. Passive interposers, glass and any logic BEOL then become DRAM hosts. I-11198 and the display ideas silently assume this enabler.
innovation.killer_doubt: Oxide-TFT Vt sigma of ~30-100 mV rivals a ~100 mV bitline signal, so n-only latches need offset cancellation. Mobility of ~10-30 cm2/Vs may make periphery 3-10x larger than in Si.
innovation.decisive_experiment: On an IGZO BEOL shuttle or university line, tape out a 1 kb 2T0C array with bootstrapped n-only decoders and auto-zeroed sense amps. Measure read time, margin, energy and Vt drift at 85 C (~$400k).
innovation.prior_art: No all-oxide DRAM periphery found (via search snippet). PragmatIC Flex-RV NMOS-only IGZO processor (Nature 2024); SEL CAAC-IGZO logic; display gate-on-array drivers.

title: Negative-capacitance bitline: electrophysiology's capacitance neutralisation applied to the DRAM sense path
idea: A small amplifier per bitline (or a pre-phase folded into the existing sense amplifier) senses the bitline and drives a feedback capacitor Cf with gain A > 1. That injects a current equal to -Cn*dV/dt, with Cn = (A-1)*Cf. For the 1-2 ns of charge sharing, the bitline's effective capacitance becomes Cbl - Cn; then the neutraliser switches off and the normal latch fires. At Cn/Cbl ~0.7 the cell can shrink 3.3x for the same signal. Amplifier offset is auto-zeroed during precharge.

physics.key_insight: Active neutralisation needs no new device: a per-bitline gain stage cancels ~50-70% of Cbl during 1-2 ns charge sharing, so Cs can fall 2-3x on today's 512-cell bitline.
physics.killer_doubt: Stability needs Cn below capacitance to static nodes; BL-BL coupling (assume 20-30% of Cbl) follows neighbour data, so worst patterns may cap Cn/Cbl near 0.5 (2x, not 3.3x).
physics.decisive_experiment: 28-65 nm MPW ($150-300k): 64 emulated 35 fF bitlines with 1-5 fF MIM cell stubs and per-line neutralisers; measure signal, offset and oscillation under all-0, all-1 and checkerboard data, beside N-04 charge-transfer pre-sense.
physics.prior_art: Electrophysiology headstage capacitance neutralisation; clamped-bitline sense amp (Blalock, IEICE). No DRAM bitline neutraliser found (via search snippet).

innovation.key_insight: Positive-feedback neutralisation cuts the effective load of an unchanged 512-cell bitline ~3x, so a ~1.1 fF (~260 nm) capacitor suffices. That is small enough for a 3D-tier capacitor.
innovation.killer_doubt: Noise and residual offset scale 3.3x at Cn/Cbl=0.7: 3 mV after auto-zero becomes ~10 mV of a 50 mV budget. Needs ~8k >=1 GHz amplifiers at 2F pitch per activation.
innovation.decisive_experiment: 28-65 nm MPW: 512-cell emulated bitlines with 1-5 fF MOM cells, each with a per-bitline neutraliser and auto-zero. Measure gain spread, stability across mats at Cn/Cbl 0.5-0.8, energy, and error rate vs Cs. ~$400k.
innovation.prior_art: SRAM negative-capacitance bitlines (Mostafa et al., IEEE TVLSI); US 8872938 NC sense amp (via search snippet); electrophysiology headstage neutralisation. No DRAM version found.

title: Sandwich stack: Smart-Cut single-crystal sense layers every 16 oxide tiers
idea: Build oxide-channel 3D DRAM tiers (horizontal or vertical-channel 1T1C or 2T0C) in groups of 16, then bond a ~50 nm single-crystal Si layer on top by Smart Cut (H-implanted donor, low-temperature bond, split) and build n- and p-channel transistors in it at <=400 C, as CEA-Leti showed with full 2.5 V n&p SOI MOSFETs at 400 C (IEDM 2025, nanosecond laser anneal plus solid-phase regrowth). That layer holds the local sense amps, tier decoders and muxes for the 16 tiers below; the next 16 tiers go on top. Each vertical bitline is only 16 cells tall (~2-4 fF), so a 1T1C cell needs only ~0.3-0.6 fF, which fits in a ~30-60 nm lateral capacitor inside the tier, shrinking the per-tier footprint from A1's ~0.03 um2 base case to ~0.01 um2. Global bitlines run up to a bonded or top-level periphery.

physics.key_insight: A 16-cell vertical bitline (~2-4 fF) decouples capacitor size from tier count. At EOT ~0.45 nm (~77 fF/um2), 0.3-0.6 fF fits a 30-60 nm lateral capacitor.
physics.killer_doubt: Signal is ~0.5 V x 0.45/(0.45+3) ≈ 65 mV, which needs offset-cancelled SAs. Four Smart Cut c-Si layers (SOI donor plus a FEOL-lite pass each) may add ~$8-16k per wafer.
physics.decisive_experiment: Build 4-tier IGZO 1T1C with 30-60 nm lateral caps and measure retention at 85 C. Then apply a 400 C bond/split thermal and hydrogen sequence with an Al2O3 barrier and remeasure (go: Vt drift <20 mV).
physics.prior_art: CEA-Leti CoolCube 400 C sequential CMOS; layer-transfer DRAM patents; M3D DRAM periphery tier (arXiv 2008.11367). No interleaved SA layer found (via search snippet).

innovation.key_insight: Capping vertical bitlines at 16 cells (~2-4 fF) cuts the needed Cs to ~0.3-0.6 fF, shrinking the 3D capacitor ~10-20x: the reading-is-solved insight applied inside the stack.
innovation.killer_doubt: Each 16-tier group adds a bonded donor layer and ~15-25 low-temperature CMOS masks, perhaps ~$3-6k per wafer for 4 groups. <=400 C FETs and implant hydrogen threaten IGZO tiers.
innovation.decisive_experiment: With CEA-Leti or a Smart-Cut university partner, bond and split c-Si over a 4-tier IGZO TFT stack with an Al2O3/SiN barrier. Measure IGZO Vt shift (<20 mV target), Ioff, and the quality of ns-laser n/p FETs. ~$700k.
innovation.prior_art: Samsung 16-tier VS-DRAM with bonded peri-on-cell (VLSI 2026); CEA-Leti CoolCube and 400 C sequential CMOS; Monolithic 3D Inc. ion-cut 3D-memory patents [training knowledge].

title: Carrier-is-memory: the mandatory carrier wafer of backside-power logic becomes a DRAM wafer
idea: In backside power delivery the finished front-side BEOL is flipped and bonded to a carrier wafer, the original substrate is ground away and power is wired in from the back, so the front-side signal wiring ends up facing the carrier. Replace that blank carrier with a full DRAM wafer (1-beta-class 1T1C or an oxide-cell wafer) whose die map matches the logic reticle, and make the bond a Cu-SiCN hybrid bond at 1-2 um pitch instead of a plain dielectric fusion bond. The memory die keeps its sense amps and bank logic but drops pads, PHYs and TSVs; commands, data and memory power cross the bond. The memory wafer stays thick and becomes the heat-spreading side of the stack (pair with B3-03). For a wafer-scale engine, the same move puts a whole 300 mm DRAM wafer (~3.9 TB) under the compute wafer.

physics.key_insight: BSPDN already forces a face-to-face bonded wafer onto every leading-edge logic die; making it DRAM gives ~45 GB at ~0.3 pJ/bit with no TSVs, PHYs or interposer.
physics.killer_doubt: All logic heat (~125 W/cm2, hotspots ~1 kW/cm2) crosses the DRAM: Si cells at 95-105 C need ~16-32 ms refresh, and W2W compound yield scraps ~10% of good logic.
physics.decisive_experiment: Hybrid-bond finished DRAM wafers face-down onto a dummy logic wafer with SiGe etch stop, thin to <1 um, run 400 C backside metal; map retention tail, bond-pad yield and overlay distortion before and after.
physics.prior_art: imec proposed face-to-face memory-on-logic in a BSPDN stack (via search snippet); UniIC SeDRAM W2W hybrid-bonded DRAM-on-logic; Graphcore Bow power-carrier wafer.

innovation.key_insight: BSPDN already forces a bonded carrier onto the signal side; making it DRAM adds ~45 GB at ~0.3 pJ/bit interface, with no TSVs, PHYs, interposer or extra footprint.
innovation.killer_doubt: BSPDN puts the heat sink on the carrier side, so DRAM sits in the ~1 W/mm2 path at ~95-105 C (2-4x refresh); one bond short scraps a ~$30k logic wafer.
innovation.decisive_experiment: D2W hybrid-bond commercial DRAM test dies face-down onto a heater-and-sensor logic die at 2-6 um pitch with bank-disable sparing (~$300k). Measure bond yield, pJ/bit and retention tails at 85-110 C under 1 W/mm2.
innovation.prior_art: Chip Scale Review 2022: memory wafer replaces BSPDN carrier (via search snippet); UniIC SeDRAM (IEDM 2020); Graphcore Bow functional carrier; AP Memory VHM WoW.

title: Automata Processor fixed: one hard-wired in-DRAM job, KV-cache top-k filtering
idea: Micron's Automata Processor died because nobody wanted to program NFAs and DRAM-process logic was slow. Hard-wire one function with a huge market: each bank's sense-amp stripe computes 4-bit dot products of a broadcast query against the open row of keys and returns only the indices of the top-k matches, so the accelerator fetches just those KV entries through one new command and no programming model.

physics.key_insight: Bank-parallel row buffers give ~8x the external bandwidth (~17 TB/s per stack). Scoring INT4 keys there and returning only indices lets KV live in a DDR/LPDDR tier, not HBM.
physics.killer_doubt: Software top-k (Quest/ShadowKV) already cuts KV traffic ~8-16x. In-memory filtering only removes the low-bit key scan (~1/8 of KV). Bank-PIM cost Samsung ~50% of PIM-die capacity.
physics.decisive_experiment: Trace-driven study (<$150k): Llama-70B-class model on LongBench/RULER, comparing software Quest with in-bank INT4 top-k on a DDR5/LPDDR-PIM tier (Ramulator plus DRAMPower). Add area of the INT4 MAC and top-k in a 3-metal DRAM-like PDK.
physics.prior_art: SK hynix AiM, Samsung HBM-PIM, AttAcc (ASPLOS 2024), CENT CXL-PIM LLM inference (ASPLOS 2025), Micron Automata Processor, SparQ/Quest top-k attention.

innovation.key_insight: Scoring 4-bit key sketches at bank bandwidth (LPDDR5X-PIM is 8x internal) and returning only top-k indices lets long-context KV live in commodity PIM DRAM instead of HBM (~3x wafer/bit).
innovation.killer_doubt: DRAM-process logic is costly: Samsung HBM-PIM dies held half the bits (4 vs 8 Gb). Top-k must cost under ~10% die area and hold RULER accuracy at k~1-2%.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Run sketch scoring plus top-k on UPMEM PIM DIMMs or Ramulator2+DRAMPower. Synthesize a per-bank top-k unit at 28 nm, scaled to 3-metal DRAM. Measure tokens/s, pJ/token and RULER-128k accuracy. About $250k.
innovation.prior_art: SK hynix GDDR6-AiM and Samsung HBM-PIM/LPDDR5X-PIM (dense GEMV); IBM StarC selective token access on PIM; H2EAL hybrid-bonded top-k (via search snippet).

title: Vertical charge-coupled shift strings: memory without per-bit transistors
idea: Ideal: memory with no transistor, capacitor or contact per bit. Closest: in a 3D-NAND-like stack, clock tier wordlines three-phase so charge packets move along a vertical oxide-semiconductor channel like a CCD; each string is a shift register read by one sense amp at its foot, with a regeneration stage every ~32 tiers to cancel transfer loss.

physics.key_insight: Charge moves through a semiconductor channel, not a tunnel oxide, so wear is gate stress only; no per-bit transistor, capacitor or staircase (phases share plates); bits added by deposition.
physics.killer_doubt: imec planar IGZO CCD CTE is >98%; need >=99.99% (0.98^128 keeps 7.5%). imec's 3D clocks >4 MHz, so a 64-stage shift takes ~16 us, not 100-300 ns.
physics.decisive_experiment: University-fab planar 4-phase IGZO CCDs, surface versus buried-channel (IGO/IGZO heterostructure) with fat-zero bias; measure CTE versus clock (4-200 MHz) at 25-85 C. Go if >=0.9999 at >=50 MHz.
physics.prior_art: imec IEDM 2024 planar IGZO CCD (CTE>98%, >200 s retention, >1e10 cycles); imec IMW 2026 vertical 3D CCD (via search snippet); 1970s Si CCD memories.

innovation.key_insight: Deposition-only 3D charge-shift memory with no per-bit transistor or capacitor. Writes stay in a semiconductor channel (imec: >1e10 cycles, >200 s retention). Plausibly 4-8x 1b density as a streaming tier.
innovation.killer_doubt: Charge-transfer efficiency: imec reports >98% per transfer, but 64 transfers need >=0.9999 (0.98^64 = 0.27 kept). Its 6.25 MHz clocks are ~40x below 250 MHz.
innovation.decisive_experiment: University-fab planar buried-channel (bilayer IGZO/IGO) 64-gate CCD string: measure per-transfer CTE versus fat zero at 1-100 MHz and 25-85 C. Then a 16-tier vertical coupon through an imec or NAND-pilot partner. ~$300k.
innovation.prior_art: imec 2024 'High Density 3D Buffer Memory Enabled by IGZO Channel CCD' (CTE >98%, via search snippet); 1970s Intel/Fairchild CCD main memories; Phase B N-08.

title: Advance market commitment for next-generation memory bits
idea: Combine the vaccine Advance Market Commitment model with memory. Governments and hyperscalers pre-commit to buy the first 10 EB of any DRAM-class technology that meets $/GB, latency and endurance thresholds, at a guaranteed premium price that tapers.

physics.key_insight: Memory entrants die in the bust, not the boom (Qimonda 2009, Elpida 2012). A tapered, technology-neutral price floor makes an entrant fab bankable, like a power-purchase agreement.
physics.killer_doubt: 10 EB is ~1/3 of a year's world DRAM bits (~25-30 EB, est.), ~$30-50B. Industry lobbied in July 2026 against market interventions and favors incumbent long-term contracts.
physics.decisive_experiment: Policy pilot (~$500k): term sheet (performance thresholds, 0.5-1 EB, taper, floor price); model entrant-fab IRR with and without it through a 2012-style bust; seek non-binding letters of intent from 3-5 hyperscalers.
physics.prior_art: Gavi pneumococcal AMC ($1.5B); Frontier carbon-removal AMC ($925M); CHIPS grants (Micron ~$6.1B) are supply-side. No memory AMC found (via search snippet).

innovation.key_insight: New DRAM technologies die in the demand-risk valley. A tech-neutral pull commitment pays only for delivered bits that meet $/GB, latency and endurance thresholds, so it backs whichever cell wins.
innovation.killer_doubt: 10 EB at ~$20/GB is ~$200B; a fundable first tranche is ~$1-5B (0.05-0.25 EB). SEMI's July 2026 letter opposes government memory-market intervention and favours long-term contracts.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Draft an AMC term sheet (thresholds, price taper, JEDEC-style qualification) and secure non-binding letters from 3 hyperscalers and 1 federal buyer for a $1B pilot tranche. ~$300k, 12 months.
innovation.prior_art: Gavi pneumococcal AMC (2009) and Frontier carbon-removal AMC (2022) [training knowledge]. No memory AMC found; SEMI urges long-term contracts instead (via search snippet).

title: Phone LPDDR packages reballed onto CXL bridge cards
idea: Po: every phone is a memory mine. Recyclers desolder LPDDR4X/5 packages from end-of-life phones (hot-gas rework plus automated reballing), test them on a fixture, and mount 16-32 of them on a CXL Type-3 card whose controller bridges the LPDDR protocol and masks per-package defects with a remap table.

physics.key_insight: ~1.2B phones/yr at ~5-6 GB is ~7e9 GB, ~15-20% of world DRAM bit output, with zero wafer starts; at 4x prices a $20/GB bounty can raise collection.
physics.killer_doubt: Realistic 15-20% collection x 70% rework yield gives ~1e9 GB (~3% supply); 3rd-4th reflow on MSL-3 PoP parts plus >50 ballout variants could push cost past $5/package.
physics.decisive_experiment: Harvest 1,000 EOL phones (~$150k): measure desolder/bake/reball yield, retention and hammer (HCfirst) bins, all-in $/GB; run 16 packages behind an FPGA CXL Type-3 bridge with remap for 1,000 h.
physics.prior_art: Microsoft GreenSKU reuses retired DDR4 behind CXL; Shenzhen reballed/recycled DRAM trade (often counterfeit). Phone-LPDDR-to-CXL: none found.

innovation.key_insight: At shortage prices harvested phone LPDDR is worth more than the phone; a CXL bridge with defect remap gives OEM-rejected packages a datacenter outlet, zero wafer starts.
innovation.killer_doubt: Chinese phone OEMs already buy harvested DRAM natively; if they absorb >80% of good pulls the bridge sees only rejects, and underfilled-PoP removal yield below ~70% breaks cost/GB.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Buy ~2,000 EOL phones (~$40k), desolder/reball LPDDR4X, test BER and retention at 85 C on an FPGA fixture; build one 128 GB CXL card on an FPGA bridge; report good-GB yield and $/GB.
innovation.prior_art: Chinese OEMs reuse desoldered phone DRAM; Meta (Vistara ASIC) and Google reuse DDR4 via CXL (via search snippet). LPDDR-to-CXL bridge: none found.

title: Retired GPUs become attention-computing KV-cache servers
idea: Combine previous-generation accelerators (HBM2-era parts on non-EUV processes) with attention offload: the new GPU ships query vectors over the network, the retired GPU holds long-context KV in its HBM and returns attention outputs, so only small vectors cross the link.

physics.key_insight: Bandwidth per GB, not FLOPS, sets KV-serving value: V100 (~28/s) and A100-80 (~25/s) scan their HBM nearly as often as H100 (~42/s), at similar or lower W/GB.
physics.killer_doubt: Each token needs ~80 per-layer round trips (~1-2 ms) and ~20 GB/s per H100 at batch 256; V100 lacks BF16/FlashAttention-2; the retired HBM2 pool is likely only tens of PB.
physics.decisive_experiment: Rack 8 used V100 or A100 servers as attention/KV nodes behind 2 H100 nodes over 400G RDMA (~$300k); serve a 70B GQA model at 32-128k context; measure tok/s/$ against H100-only.
physics.prior_art: Lamina attention offloading to cheaper memory-optimized GPUs (2024); MegaScale-Infer and StepFun attention-FFN disaggregation (2025). Retired-fleet sourcing angle: none found.

innovation.key_insight: Attention is bandwidth-bound: an A100 scans 80 GB in ~40 ms (one decode step) at ~200 W per TB/s, like H100. Retired HBM beats CXL DDR as a KV tier.
innovation.killer_doubt: In a 2026 compute shortage, A100/H100s still rent and are not stranded. The 80 serial per-layer round trips (~10-20 us each) add ~1-1.6 ms per token unless pipelined.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Pair 4 A100-80GB with 1 H100 over 400G RDMA (~$150k used or rented), run Lamina-style offload at 128k context, and measure tokens/s/$ and TTFT. Then size the retirable A100/H100 HBM pool from fleet data.
innovation.prior_art: Lamina (Tsinghua 2024) offloads attention to consumer RTX 3090s (via search snippet); MegaScale-Infer and StepFun attention-FFN disaggregation. Retired datacenter GPUs as the tier: none found.

title: Smoke detector: leaky analog charge counters catch row hammer
idea: Smoke builds up in an ionization chamber until the alarm trips. Give each group of 4 rows one tiny capacitor in the wordline-driver strip that gets a fixed charge packet per activation and leaks with a ~64 ms time constant; a comparator trips at ~500 activations' worth of charge and queues a targeted neighbour refresh.

physics.key_insight: Analog accumulators on every 4-row group track all rows with no read-modify-write, so many-sided patterns cannot evade them and PRAC's tRC penalty goes away.
physics.killer_doubt: A designed 64 ms leak on ~1 fF is ~8 fA and drifts ~100x over 25-95 C; packet mismatch ~10%. Workaround: no leak, reset on REF. Micron patents the core.
physics.decisive_experiment: 28 nm MPW: 4,096 analog counters (coupling-cap pump, reset-on-REF, single-transistor trip). Measure trip-count spread, leakage tail and temperature drift at 25-110 C. ~$300k.
physics.prior_art: Micron analog accumulator patents US 10,964,378, US 11,568,918 and US 10,943,636 (via search snippet); JEDEC DDR5 PRAC digital per-row counters.

innovation.key_insight: One leaky analog integrator per 4 rows counts every activation with no counter table, no in-array read-modify-write and no many-sided evasion; ~3T+1C per 4 rows fits the driver strip.
innovation.killer_doubt: A leakage-set 64 ms time constant drifts ~2x per 10-15 C and packet mismatch adds tens of %; trip spread beyond ~2x over 0-95 C breaks a 500-versus-1k margin.
innovation.decisive_experiment: 65 nm MPW with 1k integrators using a bias-referenced (PTAT) leaker; measure trip-count distribution from 0 to 95 C and under pulse-width variation. Pass: 6-sigma spread under 2x. ~$150k.
innovation.prior_art: Digital counters: JEDEC DDR5 PRAC, Graphene, ABACuS; LIRMM decaying 'forgetful' counters; no analog charge-integrator counter found (via search snippet).

title: Open array-to-periphery bond standard for merchant cell wafers
idea: Inverting 'one company makes the whole DRAM die': publish an open hybrid-bond interface (bitline pitch, preamp spec, power and test pads) so array fabs sell bare cell wafers and many periphery designers, including US logic foundries, sell sense/decode dies, like UCIe for memory internals.

physics.key_insight: Every 2026 next-gen DRAM demo already bonds a periphery wafer to the cell wafer. An open per-segment interface lets litho-light cell fabs and US logic foundries split the value chain.
physics.killer_doubt: At 40 nm BL pitch, 128-cell segments need <=0.45 um bonds, beyond production. W2W has no known-good die (0.9x0.9=0.81). Periphery must match each array's Cs, Cbl, ~3 V VPP.
physics.decisive_experiment: Draft an electrical envelope spec. Tape out a 28/22 nm SA plus WL-driver periphery test chip and bond it at 1-2 um pitch to an IGZO or MIM-cap array wafer. Measure sense margin vs bond parasitics. ~$900k.
physics.prior_art: Samsung VCT periphery-under-cell and SK hynix 4F2 VG (in-house bonding); YMTC Xtacking and Kioxia CBA for NAND; UCIe (die-level only). No open bitline-level standard found.

innovation.key_insight: Periphery-under-cell bonding is coming anyway; an open cut at the ~1 um-pitch local-bitline level lets array-only fabs and U.S. logic foundries each make half the die.
innovation.killer_doubt: Bond pitch of 0.4-1 um against ~0.05-0.08 um bitline pairs keeps an 8-32:1 mux on the array wafer (Cbl ~10-12 fF); incumbents have no reason to sell array wafers.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Draft the cut at 64-cell bitlines with 8:1 mux (N-40); tape out a 28 nm periphery MPW die; wafer-bond at ~1 um to a third-party IGZO or MIM array wafer. Measure per-bond yield over 1e6 bonds and sense margin. ~$500k.
innovation.prior_art: YMTC Xtacking, Kioxia CBA (NAND, in-house); UniIC SeDRAM; YMTC bonded-DRAM patents and no open standard (via search snippet); Samsung/SK hynix 4F2 periphery-under-cell.

title: Host-DRAM-lite AI servers decode data shards directly on GPU
idea: IFR: AI-server host memory shrinks to almost nothing. Constraint: adding no new chips means adding no scarce elements, so delete host DRAM's jobs instead: compressed training shards go storage-to-GPU and are decoded by GPU kernels, and checkpoints stream GPU-to-NVMe directly, removing the staging buffers that justify 1-2 TB per node.

physics.key_insight: Host DDR5 per AI GPU (~256 GB on DGX H100/B200) is 1.4-3x the GPU's own HBM bits; much is staging and page cache, removable with GPUDirect Storage and GPU decode.
physics.killer_doubt: Host DRAM is gaining jobs: KV-offload tiers (Dynamo KVBM, LMCache) and in-memory checkpoints; GB200 solders 480 GB LPDDR5X per Grace, so cuts need board changes.
physics.decisive_experiment: Two weeks of DAMON working-set telemetry on a 64-GPU training+inference cluster, then cgroup-cap host memory at 32-64 GB/GPU with GDS checkpointing and SSD-direct KV; report step-time and TTFT p99 deltas.
physics.prior_art: NVIDIA GPUDirect Storage, DALI/nvCOMP GPU decode, checkpoint streaming tools; no fleet-level host-DRAM-diet study found.

innovation.key_insight: AI racks carry as much host DRAM as HBM (DGX H200: 2 TB vs 1.1 TB; GB300 NVL72: ~17 vs ~21 TB). Deleting its jobs is a big lever.
innovation.killer_doubt: Host DRAM is becoming the KV tier and coherent capacity (Vera: 1.5 TB per CPU). Async checkpoint staging needs ~16 B/param, so the real cut may be 2x, not 8x.
innovation.decisive_experiment: On rented 8-GPU nodes, cap host memory with cgroups at 256 GB vs 2 TB. Run training (GDS + nvCOMP data path, GPU-to-NVMe checkpoints) and inference (NVMe KV tier). Compare throughput and TTFT. About $100-150k.
innovation.prior_art: NVIDIA GPUDirect Storage, nvCOMP/DALI GPU decode, DeepSpeed ZeRO-Infinity/FastPersist NVMe paths. No one has published a host-DRAM-minimal AI node specification.

title: Substitute global bitline sensing with local gain transistors from same VCT step
idea: Split each bitline into 16-cell segments; each segment's charge drives the gate of a local gain transistor made in the same vertical-channel-transistor step as the cells (no extra mask), which pulls a ~50 mV current-mode signal onto the global bitline. With a ~1 fF local line, the cell needs only ~1 fF, so the capacitor can be shallow.

physics.key_insight: A 16-32-cell local bitline (~0.6-1 fF) driving a local gain FET swings ~250-300 mV from a 1 fF cell, so the capacitor can be ~5x shorter (AR ~70 to ~15).
physics.killer_doubt: VCT gain-FET sigma-Vt of ~30-50 mV against a ~250 mV end-of-retention signal gives only ~5-6 sigma over 1e10 cells. A buried-bitline-to-gate contact likely costs one critical mask.
physics.decisive_experiment: Run SPICE Monte Carlo on a calibrated VCT model. Then build a university 1T1C-MIM test array of 16-cell segments with 3T local amplifiers, and measure the signal, offset tail and restore. ~$600k.
physics.prior_art: IBM SOI eDRAM micro sense amplifier on 32-cell local bitlines (Barth, ISSCC 2007-08); Phase B N-90, N-40 and N-61 (prior knowledge).

innovation.key_insight: In 4F2 VCT DRAM, the access-transistor step can also build per-segment gain devices. 16-cell local lines cut Cs ~5x and capacitor AR from ~70:1 to ~15:1 with no added mask.
innovation.killer_doubt: Charge sharing stays destructive, so segments need write-back and precharge. IBM used 3T per 32 cells (~20% area at 16), and ~40 mV Vt sigma leaves ~6 sigma.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Tape out a 28-65 nm MPW with 16-cell local lines, 0.5-2 fF cells and 2-3T local amplifiers. Map read BER against Cs and global swing, and add VCT Vt-mismatch TCAD. ~$300k.
innovation.prior_art: IBM eDRAM 3T micro sense amp, ~32 cells per local bitline (Barth, ISSCC 2007/JSSC 2008, via search snippet); Phase B N-04, N-48; R23 I-05154.

title: Series-gated shared read channel: NAND-string gain cells
idea: IFR: many bits, one read transistor. Make 8-16 storage nodes the consecutive gate segments of a single vertical read channel; to read node k, plate lines capacitively boost every other node above threshold so the string current reports only node k's charge, while tiny vertical oxide write devices fill each node.

physics.key_insight: Writes go through a transistor channel (endurance-safe) and reads are non-destructive; one series read channel replaces 8-16 read FETs and contacts, mapping onto NAND-style vertical holes.
physics.killer_doubt: Pass-boost must lift unselected ~0.2 fF nodes >1.5 V (plate coupling >=0.6) without over-stressing 5-8 nm read oxide; ~30 nm-pitch neighbour coupling may eat a 200 mV window.
physics.decisive_experiment: Planar 8-node IGZO string on a university line (~$300k): each floating gate gets its own IGZO write FET and plate line. Measure read margin versus pattern, boost disturb, read time on 50 fF, and retention at 85 C.
physics.prior_art: Japanese oxide-semiconductor NAND gain-cell patents (US8421071, US8750023, US12082391: series cells, floating nodes, OS write FETs) (via search snippet); IMECAS vertical 2T0C.

innovation.key_insight: Storage nodes become floating gates on one shared vertical read channel, written through oxide transistors. No capacitor, no per-bit read contact, non-destructive read, and channel writes avoid charge-fluence wear.
innovation.killer_doubt: Each node still needs its own lateral write FET and write-bitline contact (Fact 2's blocker). With ~3 sublayers per tier and 0.1-0.3 fF nodes, read margin may be <100 mV.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Build a planar 8-node IGZO string in a university fab: series read TFTs whose gates are floating nodes written by IGZO write TFTs, plus coupling plates. Measure read selectivity, disturb, and 85 C retention. About $400k.
innovation.prior_art: No direct match in one search (via search snippet). Nearest: Toshiba NAND-structured DRAM (1990s), imec/IMECAS IGZO 2T0C, NEO 3D X-DRAM 3T0C, Kioxia OCTRAM.

title: Laser interference gratings plus coarse cuts define the whole array
idea: Worse: insist that every array layer needs a $200M scanner and a custom reticle. Flip: expose the purely periodic wordline/bitline layers with maskless two-beam 193 nm immersion interference lithography (a ~$10-20M tool), pitch-split by SAQP, then trim with one low-resolution DUV cut mask. Arrays need periodicity, not arbitrary shapes.

physics.key_insight: With periphery bonded separately, the cell wafer is purely periodic. Dry 193 nm two-beam fringes (~51 nm half-pitch) plus SAQP reach ~13 nm lines with no reticle or projection lens.
physics.killer_doubt: Overlay. A perfect fringe grating cannot follow the 1-3 nm intra-die wafer distortion that scanners correct with high-order models, and array layers need <=2.5 nm overlay.
physics.decisive_experiment: On a Lloyd's-mirror or SBIL tool, print two stacked gratings plus a crossed hole layer on 300 mm wafers with moire phase alignment. Map overlay and LER against a 2.5 nm budget. ~$500k.
physics.prior_art: MIT scanning-beam interference lithography (Nanoruler); Eulitha displacement Talbot lithography; Phase B N-32 is the same idea (prior knowledge).

innovation.key_insight: Lines are already EUV-free via SAQP. The prize is 3-beam hexagonal IL for honeycomb capacitor and landing-pad holes (DRAM's hardest layers), and sub-um array layers on display glass.
innovation.killer_doubt: Rigid fringes cannot follow distortion. DRAM needs ~2-3 nm overlay, and glass at ~3 ppm/K moves ~0.8 um across 2.5 m per 0.1 K, so scanning, phase-corrected IL is required.
innovation.decisive_experiment: On a university IL bench, print hexagonal hole arrays and double them by SADP. Align a DUV cut mask to a scanner-printed prior layer and measure CDU, LER and overlay. ~$300k.
innovation.prior_art: Phase B N-32; Intel/Borodovsky complementary lithography with Multibeam e-beam cuts; Eulitha Talbot lithography; MIT SBIL. IL for DRAM holes: none found (via search snippet).

title: Main memory inside the logic die's own metal stack (monolithic BEOL oxide gain cells)
idea: After the logic metal stack is complete (TSMC has already embedded an oxide-semiconductor-selector memory fully in BEOL above advanced logic), deposit 8-16 tiers of vertical IGZO/ZTO 2T0C cells with 3 bits/cell write-verify, local complementary-oxide sensing (B2-08) and short vias down to SRAM-buffered memory controllers. Oxide cells retain >200 s at 95 C, so they tolerate sitting on hot logic. On backside-power logic, the frontside BEOL is less congested. Capacity is the target, not cache: an 800 mm2 die area carries 76-152 GB.

physics.key_insight: Transistor-written oxide gain cells in the logic die's own BEOL: capacity-class memory at ~0.2 pJ/bit, with no extra wafer, no TSV and no write-endurance limit.
physics.killer_doubt: Yield coupling: 99% unrepairable yield per tier across 16 tiers loses 15% of $500+ logic dies. Each 3-bit level is ~120 e- on a ~0.15 fF node at 105 C.
physics.decisive_experiment: Deposit 2-4 vertical IGZO 2T0C tiers on finished 22-28 nm foundry logic die. Measure 3-bit retention and drift at 105 C over 1,000 h, plus logic Vt and ring-oscillator shift after the <=400 C flow.
physics.prior_art: Stanford/MIT N3XT memory-on-logic; SEL CAAC-IGZO DOSRAM in BEOL; imec IGZO 2T0C; Kioxia/Nanya OCTRAM. From memory.

innovation.key_insight: Even at 1-2 b/cell, 8-16 oxide tiers over an 800 mm2 logic die hold ~25-100 GB at ~0.2 pJ/bit with no extra wafer: HBM-stack capacity without the TSV tax.
innovation.killer_doubt: Memory yield multiplies into a ~$25k logic wafer: 1% loss per tier is ~15% at 16 tiers. 3-bit levels sit ~140 mV apart, near expected 95 C PBTI drift.
innovation.decisive_experiment: 4-tier vertical IGZO/ZTO 2T0C arrays (64 kb) on finished 65-130 nm foundry CMOS wafers. Measure 2-3 b retention and Vt drift at 95-105 C across 1e9 write-verify cycles, plus logic ring-oscillator shift. ~$600k.
innovation.prior_art: TSMC fully-BEOL oxide-selector memory over logic (VLSI 2025); CXMT BEOL multi-layer IGZO DRAM (IEDM 2025); imec BEOL 2T0C IGZO eDRAM; NUS all-BEOL 2T0C.

title: One latent per token regenerates every layer's K/V on demand
idea: Inverts 'each layer stores its own KV cache': DRAM holds a single low-rank latent per token (e.g., 256 dims), and each layer's tensor cores up-project it to K and V just in time inside the attention kernel, spending cheap FLOPs to save scarce bytes. A short distillation pass retrofits existing models so the shared cross-layer latent is trained jointly.

physics.key_insight: Llama-70B KV is ~320 KB/token, while one 256-d latent is 512 B. With MLA-style absorbed up-projection, scoring stays in latent space and the FLOP cost stays small.
physics.killer_doubt: All 80 layers re-read the latent, so bandwidth falls only ~8x unless 64 MB stays on-chip. Retrofits (xKV, MiniCache) stall near 2-7x before accuracy drops.
physics.decisive_experiment: Distil Llama-3.1-8B into one shared 512-d latent with ~2-5B tokens (~$100k of GPU time). Compare RULER/LongBench at 32-128k against the MHA2MLA per-layer retrofit and YOCO-style half-depth sharing.
physics.prior_art: MLA (DeepSeek-V2, 2024); CLA (2024); YOCO (2024); LCKV (ACL 2024) single top-layer KV; MHA2MLA and xKV retrofits (2025). From memory.

innovation.key_insight: KV caches of different layers share aligned dominant singular vectors (xKV). One trained per-token latent with absorbed per-layer projections could cut KV capacity 10-40x, past xKV's training-free 8x.
innovation.killer_doubt: Retrofit is the doubt. Training-free xKV holds RULER only to ~8x, and beyond that single-cache designs (YOCO, LCKV) were pretrained. RoPE keys resist cross-layer sharing and weight absorption.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Distill Llama-3.1-8B into one shared 1-2k-dim latent per token with absorbed per-layer heads (~2-5B tokens, ~200 H100-hours). Measure RULER and needle accuracy at 32-128k against xKV-4 and MHA2MLA at 8x, 16x and 32x.
innovation.prior_art: xKV cross-layer SVD, 8x on Llama-3.1-8B (via search snippet); YOCO and LCKV single-cache designs; CLA; MLA (DeepSeek-V2); MHA2MLA and TransMLA retrofits.

title: 2050 engineer: KV cache stored as per-sequence implicit neural field
idea: A 2050 engineer stores functions, not tables. For each long sequence, a tiny sinusoidal MLP per layer is fitted online to map (position, head) to the K/V vector and refitted incrementally every few hundred tokens, and attention queries this field instead of a table. Exact KV is kept only for the recent window and for outlier tokens the field reconstructs poorly.

physics.key_insight: Decode leaves ~90% of tensor-core FLOPs idle, so online fitting of a compressed KV representation is nearly free in compute. The unknown is whether a field beats quantization in rate-distortion.
physics.killer_doubt: Post-RoPE keys and values are token-content signals, not smooth in position. 20-50x needs ~0.3-0.8 bits per element, against KIVI-class 2-bit (8x) that already loses accuracy on retrieval.
physics.decisive_experiment: Fit SIREN fields per layer and head to Llama-3-8B KV at 32k tokens with an exact recent window plus outliers. Compare against KIVI and low-rank at equal bits on RULER and needle tests. ~$30k of GPU time.
physics.prior_art: KIVI/KVQuant quantization, Palu/xKV low-rank, H2O/SnapKV eviction; trained-in neural memory (Titans, TTT layers) is the architectural workaround.

innovation.key_insight: Decode leaves ~90% of tensor-core FLOPs idle, so online fitting of a compact learned KV for old tokens is nearly free compute. Fitted latent tokens beat a position-indexed field.
innovation.killer_doubt: Post-RoPE K/V carry token content, not smooth position signals; 20-50x needs ~0.3-0.8 bit/element versus KIVI 2-bit (8x), and querying the field costs T MLP evaluations per step.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Fit SIREN fields and online Cartridges-style latent KV per layer/head to Llama-3-8B KV at 32k tokens (exact recent window plus outliers); compare with KIVI and low-rank at equal bits on RULER. ~$30k GPU.
innovation.prior_art: Cartridges (Stanford 2025, ~38x via offline self-study), KIVI, SnapKV/H2O eviction, Palu low-rank, DeepSeek MLA, Activation Beacon.

title: Bookshelf memory: dies stand on edge atop compute
idea: Eliminate both the interposer and TSVs: route top-metal lines to a polished, metallized die edge carrying ~2 um-pitch pads, stand dozens of DRAM dies vertically on the GPU's top surface and hybrid-bond their edges; the gaps between the standing dies become microfluidic coolant channels, so the memory doubles as a heat-sink fin array.

physics.key_insight: A polished laminated-die-block edge gives TSV-free, interposer-free memory-on-logic: ~5k pads per die ≈ 2.5 TB/s. The gaps form a microchannel heat sink (~5 K at 1 W/mm2).
physics.killer_doubt: Pads exist only in the ~3-5 um DRAM BEOL strip (~5-10k per 10 mm edge, not 250k). Thickness variation over 100 dies accumulates ~±10 um, against ~0.5 um bond overlay.
physics.decisive_experiment: Laminate 16-32 plasma-diced daisy-chain dies and CMP the block edge. Add an adaptive RDL (or the I-10449 slab). Bond to a logic test die at 10, then 3 um pitch. Measure yield and ΔT at 1 W/mm2 (~$600k).
physics.prior_art: Irvine Sensors / 3D-Plus edge-metallized die cubes (prior knowledge). Die-edge interconnect patents (US 12211799 family, via search snippet). Standing memory dies on logic: none found.

innovation.key_insight: Edge I/O on face-to-back die blocks removes TSVs and the interposer, so each die keeps DDR-class density while a 32-die block over a GPU gives ~100 GB at HBM-class width.
innovation.killer_doubt: Edge pads fit only the ~5-10 um BEOL band: ~25k contacts per die, not 250k. Diced cross-sections need <1 nm roughness to bond. Mm-long on-die paths give ~1 pJ/bit.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Bond 8 thinned dummy dies face-to-back into a block, CMP one edge to expose BEOL lines, and hybrid-bond it to a test wafer at 5 um pitch. Measure daisy-chain yield and shear after thermal cycling. About $400k.
innovation.prior_art: Irvine Sensors edge-metallized memory cubes, Vertical Circuits/Invensas sidewall-interconnect stacks, 3D-Plus; SK hynix VFO vertical wires. No 2 um edge hybrid bonding found.

title: Fan-deck ordering: codebook indices where one flip yields a similar shade
idea: Paint fan decks put similar shades on adjacent cards, so grabbing the wrong one still looks right. For vector-quantized weights and embeddings, codebook indices are assigned by simulated annealing so that codewords whose indices differ by one bit are nearest neighbors in vector space (a Gray-like assignment). Indices are stored raw in 1%-BER cells, and a flip swaps in a nearly identical codeword.

physics.key_insight: At 1% BER, protecting 64 B lines needs ~27-44% ECC overhead (finite-length bound). An annealed index map that makes flips nearly harmless could replace that overhead for VQ weights.
physics.killer_doubt: A 16-bit codebook index flips with 15% probability at 1% BER, and pseudo-Gray maps have historically given ~2-4 dB, not 5-10x. The cheap 1%-BER cell does not exist yet.
physics.decisive_experiment: Simulation (<$20k): AQLM 2-bit Llama-3-8B with 1% iid and row-clustered flips injected. Compare random, annealed and MSB-protected index maps on perplexity and MMLU.
physics.prior_art: Pseudo-Gray coding (Zeger-Gersho 1990); channel-optimized VQ (Farvardin 1990); EDEN approximate DRAM for DNNs (MICRO 2019). From memory.

innovation.key_insight: Codebook index assignment gives redundancy-free error protection: flips land on neighbouring codewords. Weights, the largest static inference tenant, can then sit ECC-free in relaxed-refresh or reject cells.
innovation.killer_doubt: At 1% BER, 15% of 16-bit AQLM indices flip, with only 16 Hamming neighbours per codeword. Distortion may fall 2-3x, not 5-10x. Real retention errors are asymmetric and clustered.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Anneal index orders for AQLM, VPTQ and QuIP# codebooks on Llama-8B/70B, then inject iid, asymmetric and row-clustered 1e-3 to 1e-2 flips. Compare perplexity and MMLU with random-order and int3-with-protected-scales baselines. GPU weeks, under $50k.
innovation.prior_art: Pseudo-Gray coding (Zeger-Gersho) and channel-optimized VQ (Farvardin) for speech; EDEN (MICRO 2019) approximate DRAM. No faulty-memory application to weight VQ found (via search snippet).

title: Mycologist's spores: hibernate idle AI agents as compressed snapshots
idea: Fungi survive lean times as tiny spores. Agent sessions spend most of their wall-clock time waiting on users or tools. After ~2 s idle, the session's KV cache, runtime heap and sandbox are snapshotted into a compressed, deduplicated spore on NVMe and rehydrated in tens of ms by lazily paging in only the pages touched first.

physics.key_insight: Agent sessions block on tools and users; snapshot KV, heap and sandbox together, and restore the heap and sandbox REAP-style from the recorded first-touch working set.
physics.killer_doubt: A 128k-token 70B GQA agent holds ~42 GB of KV; restore at ~50 GB/s PCIe takes ~0.85 s, not tens of ms; tool returns give no lead time.
physics.decisive_experiment: Log 10k real agent runs (SWE-bench harness): tool-wait distribution and predictability. Replay on vLLM+LMCache SSD tier with MLA/FP8 KV (~9 GB, ~0.2 s); measure resident-KV cut against added step latency.
physics.prior_art: InferCept (ICML'24: preserve/discard/swap KV during tool calls); REAP/FaaSnap lazy snapshot restore; Firecracker snapshots.

innovation.key_insight: An idle agent holds GPU KV and CPU sandbox DRAM, each idle while the other works. Co-hibernate both under one budget, waking on the LLM's tool-call tokens.
innovation.killer_doubt: A 32 GB GQA-70B KV restore at ~10 GB/s takes ~3 s, longer than a typical tool call. KV hibernation pays only on human waits: likely 2-4x, not 10-20x.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Run OpenHands/SWE-agent traces on vLLM+LMCache with Firecracker sandboxes. Measure the idle-gap distribution, resident GB per concurrent agent and added latency under joint hibernation. About $100k.
innovation.prior_art: InferCept (ICML 2024) handles KV during tool calls; E2B/Firecracker snapshot-restore; TVCache (ICML 2026) snapshots sandboxes. Joint KV+sandbox budgeting: none found (via search snippet).

title: Nanogap (vacuum/air) tunnel-barrier floating node: flash-like retention without oxide wear
idea: The floating metal node (TiN or W, anchored on dielectric on one side) faces a write electrode across a 2.5-4 nm gap. The gap is made by removing an ALD sacrificial layer (carbon or Al2O3) and then sealed, like BEOL air-gaps or NASA's nanoscale vacuum-channel transistors, which work in air because the gap is far below the ~70 nm mean free path. The node is the gate of an IGZO or Si read transistor (2T-like gain cell), so the read is non-destructive. Writing uses field emission at a few V/nm (field enhancement 2-3 at edges); holding relies on the exponential non-linearity of tunnelling. Charge never passes through a solid dielectric, so there are no trap generation, SILC or charge-to-breakdown limits, the mechanisms that cap flash endurance at ~1e5. Low-work-function coatings (LaB6-class, 2.7 eV) cut write voltage, but even plain TiN (4.5 eV) works at 8 V.

physics.key_insight: A vacuum barrier has no traps, SILC or charge-to-breakdown, so it is one of the few charge-write routes that could escape the charge-fluence endurance wall.
physics.killer_doubt: Retention changes ~5x per 0.1 nm of gap at 2.7 eV, and TiN roughness of ~0.3-0.5 nm rms lets asperities dominate. IGZO 2T0C already gives >200 s with unlimited endurance.
physics.decisive_experiment: Release 3 nm sacrificial-carbon gaps over amorphous-metal floating gates on ~1,000 MOSFETs at a university fab. Map the retention spread at 85 C and FN write cycling to 1e10. Go if 6-sigma spread <100x.
physics.prior_art: NASA Ames vacuum-channel transistors; ALD-spacer nanogaps from atomic layer lithography (Oh group, 2013); NAND inter-cell air gaps. Vacuum-barrier floating-gate memory: none known (no search).

innovation.key_insight: Vacuum is a barrier with no traps: write current through it cannot cause SILC or breakdown. That makes it one of the triage's four routes to DRAM-class write endurance.
innovation.killer_doubt: Write current shifts ~2x and retention ~9x per 0.1 nm of gap. ns writes need ~6 V/nm local fields (~160 MPa pressure), where field-driven atom migration may reshape gaps.
innovation.decisive_experiment: In a university nanofab, make lateral TiN/vacuum/TiN gaps of 2.5-4 nm by ALD Al2O3 sacrificial release and seal. Measure gap spread over 1e4 devices, FN I-V, and drift over 1e10 10-ns cycles. ~$400k.
innovation.prior_art: None found for vacuum-gap floating gates (via search snippet). Related: NASA Ames vacuum-channel transistors (prior logs); AIST/Funai nanogap resistive switches [training knowledge].

title: Decommissioned-server DRAM recertified by in-system retention retest
idea: Combine e-waste recycling with in-system profiling: retired DDR4/DDR5 modules pass through an automated rack that runs retention and hammer profiling, writes per-module weak-row maps into SPD and redeploys them behind stronger controller ECC as CXL-attached expansion.

physics.key_insight: Retired DDR4/DDR5 is existing silicon needing zero fab capital. Deep retention/hammer profiling plus SPD weak-row maps behind CXL ECC turns scrap into a graded capacity tier.
physics.killer_doubt: CXL adds ~70-170 ns, and DDR4-capable CXL controllers set the cost. If test plus controller exceeds ~$3-5/GB or the pass rate is <70%, it loses to new DRAM.
physics.decisive_experiment: Profile 5,000 retired server DIMMs on an automated rack (retention to 4 s at 85 C, hammer, VRT); write weak-row maps to SPD; run 200 in a CXL tier for 6 months logging CE/UE. ~$400k.
physics.prior_art: Microsoft GreenSKU (reused DDR4 behind CXL, ISCA 2024); Pond CXL pooling; ITAD used-server-RAM resellers.

innovation.key_insight: Retired DDR4/DDR5 is wafer-free capacity; in-system retention and hammer profiling with weak-row maps in SPD makes it a trusted CXL tier.
innovation.killer_doubt: Duplicate of canonical R16 I-00224 (HOLD). Microsoft GreenSKU and Marvell Structera X already run DDR4 behind CXL; supply caps at ~5-7 EB/yr of retirements.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Folded into the I-00224 pilot: retest and retention-profile 1,000 retired DDR4 RDIMMs at 85 C, run a CXL DDR4 expander in a tier-2 cloud, and report yield and landed $/GB. ~$300k.
innovation.prior_art: Microsoft GreenSKU (ISCA 2024); Marvell Structera X DDR4-reuse controller; ITRenew/Iron Mountain resale; REAPER retention profiling.

title: Tree-ring shells: coaxial gain cell in every tier-hole crossing
idea: Etch one array of vertical holes through a 100-layer wordline/oxide stack, then grow concentric shells like annual rings: an outer IGZO write-channel ring, a metal storage ring cut into per-tier segments by a selective recess, and an inner read-channel 'heartwood' that the storage ring gates. Each hole-tier crossing becomes a capacitorless 2T0C cell.

physics.key_insight: Names the enabling step: per-tier storage-ring segmentation by selective recess, which floating-gate 3D NAND already does at 100+ tiers. Merge into the I-10833 dossier.
physics.killer_doubt: Reading tier k through a series inner channel needs every other segment forced on, but those gates are floating stored rings; a plane-to-ring coupling below ~0.5 limits the override.
physics.decisive_experiment: TCAD plus a 4-tier test stack. Measure whether plane-to-ring coupling can force unselected read segments on (or switch to AND-type pillars), and the resulting per-tier read window. ~$300k.
physics.prior_art: Micron/Intel floating-gate 3D NAND recessed rings; IMECAS 4-tier IGZO 2T0C (VLSI 2026); Huawei vertical CAA IGZO (prior knowledge).

innovation.key_insight: One hole etch per 100 tiers, with per-tier recessed storage rings (like Micron's floating-gate recess), could give NAND layer economics to a transistor-written, capacitorless, high-endurance DRAM-class cell.
innovation.killer_doubt: Read and write paths are both series strings: ~100 IGZO segments give ~20-100 nA and ~0.5-5 us reads, and writing tier k rewrites every tier above it: NAND-like.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Use TCAD/SPICE to compare three topologies (series string, 3D-AND multi-pillar, two planes per tier) for read latency, density at 100 tiers and disturb. Then build a 4-tier IGZO coupon to measure string current and ring coupling. ~$400k.
innovation.prior_art: NEO 3D X-DRAM IGZO 1T1C/3T0C on a NAND-like process (2025, TCAD only; via search snippet); IMECAS vertical CAA 2T0C; Macronix 3D AND; Phase B N-43.

title: Origami memory stack: one thin membrane folded into N layers, wired through the folds [SPECULATIVE]
idea: Build N memory die images side by side as one continuous thin membrane (an oxide-cell array plus 3-4 metal levels, ~1.5-3 um thick) on a glass carrier with a laser-release layer, wiring neighbouring dies together across the gaps with ordinary BEOL lines. Release the membrane and fold it accordion-style into an N-layer stack bonded with thin adhesive, with fold radii of ~150-300 um. Vertical connectivity is the BEOL wiring that runs continuously around each fold, so there are no TSVs, no micro-bumps and no die-to-die alignment. The folded stack lands on a logic base die like HBM.

physics.key_insight: Continuous BEOL wires around folds replace TSVs, bumps and alignment; a dead die is bypassed by its pass-through wiring, so spare layers restore stack yield without known-good-die.
physics.killer_doubt: Layer pitch is ~2x fold radius (300-600 um at r=150-300 um), far above HBM's ~45 um; even 67 um pitch leaves 16 adhesive layers at ~30 K/W over 100 mm2.
physics.decisive_experiment: Cu/polyimide daisy-chain membrane of 4 die images (0.5-2 um lines) on glass; laser release, fold at r=33-300 um; measure line yield, resistance after 1,000 thermal cycles and stack thermal resistance with Si-foil interleaves.
physics.prior_art: Folded-flex stacked packages (Tessera micro-Z fold; Intel folded stacked CSP, ~2002). Monolithic BEOL fold-wired memory stack: none found. Unverified.

innovation.key_insight: BEOL wiring routed around folds replaces TSVs, micro-bumps and die alignment. ~20,000 wires cross a 10 mm fold edge, above HBM TSV counts, from one planar wafer flow.
innovation.killer_doubt: No known-good-die sort: 8 dies at 90% yield give 0.9^8 = 43% good stacks. 16 polymer interfaces give ~8 K/W, too hot above ~3 W; HBM tax is mainly die-area.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Fold a 2-3 um polyimide/Cu membrane carrying 8 die images, with <=1 um-pitch daisy chains through 33 um-radius hinges. Measure resistance and opens after 1,000 cycles at -40/125 C, plus spare-die bypass. ~$300k.
innovation.prior_art: EU ORIGENAL foil-TFT folding (3-layer interconnected stack) and 2000s folded-flex 3D packages (via search snippet); Illinois Si-nanomembrane stacking. No folded memory membrane found.

title: Capacitor-hole racetrack: electroplated domain-wall nanowires in DRAM's high-aspect-ratio mold
idea: Etch the standard honeycomb hole lattice (~20 nm diameter at 35-40 nm pitch) in oxide. Instead of conformal ALD electrodes, electroplate a magnetic nanowire up from a seed at the hole bottom, modulating composition (Co-rich/Ni-rich, or thin Cu spacers) every ~60 nm to make pinning notches. Bits are axial domains separated by Bloch-point domain walls, which cylindrical wires carry without the Walker breakdown that slows flat racetracks. A vertical select transistor under each hole (4F2/6F2 vertical-channel style) drives ~30 uA bipolar shift pulses through the wire.
