A 20 nm MTJ on the planarised top reads the top bit and writes it (STT, or SOT from a top heavy-metal line). Half of each track is shift buffer, giving 10 data bits per 1.3 um hole and 25 per 3 um hole.

physics.key_insight: Reuses DRAM's AR-65 hole as a bottom-up electroplating template for a 10-25-bit vertical shift register with wear-free magnetic writes and zero refresh.
physics.killer_doubt: Under ~40 nm diameter, walls are transverse, not Bloch-point. Fast shifting needs ~3e11-1e12 A/m2 (100-300 uA at 20 nm) versus ~30-60 uA of select drive. Errors <1e-12 unshown.
physics.decisive_experiment: Pulse-electroplate Co/Ni-modulated wires into 20-40 nm oxide holes and contact single wires. Count shift errors over 1e9 pulses by MR readout against current density. Go if <1e-9 at <=1e11 A/m2.
physics.prior_art: Parkin/IBM racetrack (2008); SPINTEC (Fruchart) and Vazquez-group modulated electroplated cylindrical wires; Bloch-point walls >600 m/s (Schobitz 2019). From memory.

innovation.key_insight: Reuses DRAM's 60:1 hole as a 10-25-bit magnetic shift register. Magnetic order has no write wear-out and needs no refresh, and modulated wires grow cheaply in AAO templates.
innovation.killer_doubt: Cylindrical-wire experiments show stochastic pinning, yet DRAM needs shift errors <1e-12 per shift at ~1e7 A/cm2. 20 nm MTJs at 35-40 nm pitch are ~2x tighter than production MRAM.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Electroplate Co/Ni-modulated 20-40 nm wires (60 nm period) in AAO templates. Contact single wires and measure the current-driven shift error rate over 1e8 pulses by magnetoresistance at 300-360 K. ~$350k.
innovation.prior_art: IBM Parkin vertical racetrack proposal (Science 2008); Schobitz et al. 2019 Bloch-point walls >600 m/s; Madrid modulated-wire pinning studies (prior logs).

title: SoftRAM 95 lesson: audited effective-GB rating for memory compression
idea: Syncronys' SoftRAM 95 sold 'RAM doubling' that did nothing, poisoning trust in memory compression for decades. Create an independent, FTC-backed certification that measures delivered effective GB on standard workload traces, so OEMs can sell and procurement can count 'certified 1.6x effective memory' with smaller physical DRAM.

physics.key_insight: Compression cuts DRAM per device only if buyers count compressed GB. An audited trace-based rating (like EPA mileage) turns zram's ~2.5-3x ratio into a number procurement can use.
physics.killer_doubt: Phones already ship zram and laptops ship OS compression. The real limit is CPU and latency on incompressible apps, so a certified 1.6x likely cuts DRAM 10-20%, not 25-40%.
physics.decisive_experiment: Build the benchmark (<$300k): replay 50 phone, laptop and server traces under zram/zswap on 8 GB versus 12 GB devices and publish effective GB at fixed p95 latency. Ask two OEMs whether they would down-spec.
physics.prior_art: Apple's '8 GB ~ 16 GB' claim; Samsung RAM Plus; Windows memory compression; SPEC/MLPerf-style benchmarks. Certification: none found. From memory.

innovation.key_insight: Platform floors (Copilot+ PC 16 GB) and phones' 'virtual RAM' claims already steer DRAM content unaudited. An audited effective-GB metric could let specs and procurement count OS compression.
innovation.killer_doubt: macOS, Windows and Android already compress memory silently (~1.2-1.5x effective), so certification adds no capacity. It saves bits only if spec owners lower floors, worth perhaps ~1% of world bits.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Build an open trace-replay suite (browser tabs, Office, Teams, IDE) scoring QoS at 8, 12 and 16 GB on three OSes, then pilot it with one large procurement buyer and one platform-spec owner. About $300k.
innovation.prior_art: None found for an audited effective-memory rating. Related: SPEC and BAPCo benchmarks, Apple's contested '8 GB Mac' claim, phone RAM-extension marketing [training knowledge].

title: CCD imager registers: vertical charge-shift strings replace capacitors
idea: Adapted from CCD image sensors: a 3D gate stack wrapped around a vertical silicon or oxide-semiconductor channel stores bits as charge packets in potential wells under each gate tier; a read clocks packets down the string to a floating-diffusion sense node at the base, like a CCD vertical register.

physics.key_insight: Binary data with regenerating readout tolerates ~0.99-0.997 CTE per 64-128-transfer pass, not imaging's 0.9999; IGZO's >3 eV gap removes dark charge. Capacitor-free, transistor-free 3D bit.
physics.killer_doubt: Plane-shared clocks shift every string in a block, so each needs its own sense path: per-row slits roughly halve density (4-8x to 2-4x 1b); 5 mm word-plane RC ~160 ns.
physics.decisive_experiment: Planar overlapping-gate IGZO/IGO CCD, 16-32 gates, university fab (~$300k): CTE vs clock (10 MHz-1 GHz), fat zero, 85 C hold. Kill if per-transfer loss exceeds 3e-3 at 100 MHz.
physics.prior_art: Phase B N-08 (same concept, ALIVE-SPEC); 1970s Si CCD memories; oxide-channel or vertical CCD memory: none found (via search snippet).

innovation.key_insight: A 32-tier oxide CCD string gives ~2-4x 1b density with no capacitor, no access transistor and no EUV, in NAND-like process. This is the density-optimised point of the CCD family.
innovation.killer_doubt: imec is already on this path. Demonstrated clocks are 4-6 MHz, but a 32-bit, 4-phase string needs ~1 GHz (128 transfers) for <=130 ns access, a ~200x gap.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Merge into the I-08879 dossier. Same planar IGZO CCD test chip, plus a 32-64-bit string to measure cumulative CTE at 100 MHz-1 GHz and 85 C with fat zero.
innovation.prior_art: imec: planar 142-bit 4-phase IGZO CCD (IEDM 2024) and vertical 3-word-line 3D CCD (IMW 2026) for CXL buffer memory (via search snippet).

title: Cross-finetune KV sharing below the first modified layer
idea: Imposed limit: a system prompt's KV may be stored once across all model variants. The platform requires finetunes to freeze the bottom k layers; those layers' KV is then bit-identical to the base model's, so every variant shares one prefix-KV store for the frozen layers and keeps private KV only for the layers it changed.

physics.key_insight: The sharing is exact, not approximate. Freeze layers 1..k and their K/V projections, and their prefix KV is identical by construction, so N variants store k+N(L-k) layers.
physics.killer_doubt: It helps only prefix KV shared across variants, capped at 2x on that slice when k=L/2. Activated LoRA already reuses base KV for the whole prefix at every layer.
physics.decisive_experiment: Fine-tune Llama-3-8B with LoRA on only the top 8, 16 or 24 of 32 layers for 5 tasks and measure quality loss. Replay a multi-LoRA trace to measure the shared-prefix KV fraction (<$30k).
physics.prior_art: IBM Activated LoRA (2025) base-KV reuse; DroidSpeak (2024) cross-fine-tune KV reuse with selective recompute; SGLang RadixAttention. From memory.

innovation.key_insight: If fine-tunes freeze the bottom k layers, those layers' prefix KV is bit-identical to the base model's, so it can be shared exactly across all variants.
innovation.killer_doubt: DroidSpeak (NSDI'26) already shares cross-variant KV without freezing, recomputing ~10% of layers, and Activated LoRA shares the whole prefix. Duplicated cross-variant prefix KV is small.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Train 10 LoRA variants of an 8B base, bottom-half frozen versus all layers. On multi-agent shared-prefix traces, compare quality and KV saved against DroidSpeak and aLoRA.
innovation.prior_art: DroidSpeak, Microsoft/UChicago, NSDI 2026 (via search snippet); IBM Activated LoRA (2025) [training knowledge]; vLLM prefix cache keyed per adapter.

title: Parametric charge pumping on common plate regenerates all cells continuously
idea: Effect: parametric amplification via a nonlinear C(V). Each storage node is a nonlinear MOS varactor plus a rectifying junction; a shared AC drive on the common plate pumps charge with a voltage-dependent sign, creating two stable fixed points, so every cell continuously restores itself toward its nearer rail with no row-by-row refresh. Reads compare node charge against a mid-level reference.

physics.key_insight: Bistability bought with pump power instead of capacitor size: a state-dependent varactor plus a rectifying diode. Holding 13 pA needs only ~130 Hz at 0.1 fC/cycle.
physics.killer_doubt: Separatrix is set by diode Vf and varactor flatband. BEOL sigma is ~50-100 mV against a ~200 mV window, so it fails at 6 sigma over 3e10 cells.
physics.decisive_experiment: Bench a discrete varactor+diode cell, then build 1,000 IGZO MOS-varactor/Schottky pairs in a university fab. Map the zero crossings of Ipump(V)-Ileak(V), the window, and its sigma at 85 C. <$300k.
physics.prior_art: Goto parametron (1954); TI RTD-based tunneling SRAM (van der Wagt/Seabaugh, late 1990s); triage N-07 tunnel-diode latch.

innovation.key_insight: Parametron-style bistability makes every cell self-restoring with no row-by-row refresh, which in principle frees leakage specs and removes refresh periphery.
innovation.killer_doubt: Common plate is ~17 uF per 16 Gb die; a 1 V, 100 kHz pump burns ~1.7 W versus ~12 mW for refresh today, before crosspoint sneak paths.
innovation.decisive_experiment: SPICE plus a 4x4 discrete varactor-diode array on a PCB: show two stable fixed points under plate AC drive and measure pump power per cell and noise margin versus frequency. ~$30k.
innovation.prior_art: Goto's parametron (1954); TI tunneling-based SRAM with RTD bistability and leakage-balanced standby (van der Wagt, 1999).

title: 3D-NAND toolset builds channel-hole gain cells with no EUV
idea: Ideal: density from tier count with tools already paid for. Closest: in a NAND-style oxide/word-plate stack, each channel hole holds two concentric ALD oxide-semiconductor devices per tier: an outer write channel charging an isolated metal ring, and an inner read channel gated by that ring, so every tier crossing is a capacitorless 2T gain cell built with the 3D NAND etch, ALD and staircase flow.

physics.key_insight: A transistor-written storage ring per tier (FG-NAND-style recess) gives semiconductor-channel endurance on 3D-NAND tools. It fills the untried >=16-tier single-etch 2T0C white space.
physics.killer_doubt: Topology: planes are the only per-tier lines, so a continuous outer write channel connects every ring above the target, disturbing up to ~100 tiers per write. Needs AND/NOR-style vertical pillars.
physics.decisive_experiment: Build an 8-tier W/SiO2 stack with one DUV hole, FG-NAND recess, ALD IGZO write shell, segmented metal ring and inner read shell. Measure per-tier write disturb, ring isolation, 85 C retention. University fab, ~$700k.
physics.prior_art: IMECAS 4-tier IGZO 2T0C (VLSI 2026); Huawei vertical CAA IGZO 2T0C; Micron FG 3D NAND recess rings; no coaxial in-hole 2T0C found (via search snippet).

innovation.key_insight: Same coaxial in-hole 2T0C as I-03474. Its extra value, reusing depreciated 3D-NAND etch, ALD and staircase tools for DRAM-class bits, is merged into I-03474's review.
innovation.killer_doubt: One word plane per tier leaves the inner read channel a 100-segment series string: ~20-100 nA of string current means ~0.5-5 us sensing, NAND latency rather than DRAM's 10-100 ns.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Covered by I-03474: TCAD of a 16-100 tier string, then a 4-tier university-fab coupon measuring string current, unselected-cell pass margin and write disturb.
innovation.prior_art: NEO 3D X-DRAM IGZO 1T1C/3T0C on a NAND-like process (2025, TCAD only; via search snippet); IMECAS vertical CAA 2T0C; Phase B N-43.

title: Recompute-as-correction for KV caches and activations
idea: Ideal: memory errors are free to fix because the data can be regenerated. Closest: AI KV-cache and activation buffers are stored in unprotected relaxed-refresh DRAM with only a 16-bit CRC per 1 KB block; on a CRC miss the runtime recomputes that block from upstream tokens or layers instead of correcting it.

physics.key_insight: Regeneration replaces correction: KV and activations can be re-derived, so a detect-only CRC is enough. Dense decode already activates every KV row each step, which refreshes it by access.
physics.killer_doubt: At 4x relaxation, unprofiled raw BER ~1e-6 gives ~8e-3 errors per 1 KB block. A 40 GB cache (4e7 blocks) then needs ~3e5 weight-bound recomputes/s.
physics.decisive_experiment: Inject DRAM-Bender-measured retention error maps (0.25-2 s, 45-85 C, including VRT) into vLLM KV blocks with CRC+recompute. Measure the tokens/s lost against the refresh energy saved. Software only.
physics.prior_art: Flikker (ASPLOS 2011) relaxed refresh for non-critical data; EDEN (MICRO 2019) approximate DRAM for DNNs; vLLM recompute-on-preemption; Smart Refresh.

innovation.key_insight: Regenerable AI data (KV/prefix caches) turns memory errors into cache misses: CRC-only blocks on non-ECC, recycled or relaxed-refresh DIMMs, with recompute as the repair path.
innovation.killer_doubt: Active KV rows are re-read every ~20-50 ms decode step, already self-refreshing; gains confine to idle prefix-cache tiers and ~12-25% ECC-chip savings.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Run vLLM+LMCache with a TB-scale CPU-DRAM prefix tier on non-ECC/recycled DIMMs at 4-8x tREFI plus fault injection; measure CRC hits, recompute overhead, output quality and $/GB versus ECC RDIMM. ~$150k.
innovation.prior_art: Kelle (2025) pairs relaxed eDRAM refresh with KV recomputation (via search snippet); EDEN (2019), Flikker (2011); parity-refetch L1 caches.

title: Garbage collector fused with a columnar compressor for old generation
idea: Combine the generational GC's copying/promotion phase with compression: objects promoted to the old generation are packed into per-class columnar blocks (field-transposed, delta- and dictionary-encoded), and a read barrier decompresses on access through a small decoded-object cache.

physics.key_insight: Promotion already copies every survivor and knows its class layout. So type-aware columnar packing (pointer deltas, enum dictionaries) can beat page-level LZ4 with no extra copy pass.
physics.killer_doubt: Old gen is hot in caches and services. A decoded-cache miss (~100-300 ns), re-encoding on field writes, and the existing 4-15% load-barrier tax together could erase the gain.
physics.decisive_experiment: MMTk/OpenJDK prototype (~$300k, two engineers): columnar promotion for the top classes. Measure old-gen ratio, decoded-cache hit rate, throughput and p99 on DaCapo, Renaissance, Cassandra and a Go service, against zswap.
physics.prior_art: Zippads (ASPLOS 2019) object-based compressed hierarchy (hardware); embedded-Java heap compression (OOPSLA 2003); V8 pointer compression. Columnar GC packing: none found.

innovation.key_insight: The GC already copies every promoted object. Packing old-gen objects into per-class columns (headers dropped, fields delta- or dictionary-coded) adds compression at near-zero extra copy cost.
innovation.killer_doubt: Old gen often holds hot caches. If the decoded working set exceeds ~30% of old gen, savings fall below 1.5x, before read-barrier costs (5-15% throughput) and write overlays.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Offline, take heap dumps and access samples from 15 Java services (Renaissance, Cassandra, Elasticsearch, Spark). Compute per-class columnar ratios and the decoded-cache size needed. ~$50k shows whether whole-heap saving clears 1.5x.
innovation.prior_art: Chen et al., heap compression during GC (OOPSLA 2003); Zippads/COCO object-based hardware compression (ASPLOS 2019); JDK compact headers (Lilliput) and string dedup.

title: Export idle host DRAM of GPU servers as far memory
idea: Inverts 'a server's DRAM serves only its own CPU': GPU servers carry 1-2 TB of host DRAM that sits mostly idle while the GPUs work from HBM. An RDMA far-memory daemon leases those idle bytes to neighboring CPU servers for swap and tiering over existing NICs.

physics.key_insight: AI servers size host DRAM to GPU count, not need (DGX H100: 2 TB per 640 GB HBM). Installed base ~1 EB (estimate); sub-5 us RDMA paging suits cold tiers.
physics.killer_doubt: The GPUs are claiming the idle bytes themselves: KV offload tiers (Mooncake, LMCache, Dynamo) and in-memory checkpoints. Above ~70% utilisation, harvestable supply drops below ~0.3 EB.
physics.decisive_experiment: Collect 30 days of host-memory telemetry (RSS, page cache, pinned, KV tier) on 2-3 GPU clusters. Then run an Infiniswap/Fastswap-style lease to CPU tenants and measure p99 slowdown on both sides (<$150k).
physics.prior_art: Infiniswap (NSDI 2017); Fastswap (<5 us, via search snippet); Memtrade harvesting marketplace (via search snippet); Harvest VMs. GPU-host-specific: none found.

innovation.key_insight: AI racks carry about as much host DRAM as HBM (GB300 NVL72 ~17 TB LPDDR5X vs ~21 TB HBM). Leasing the idle part frees already-installed bits with no new chips.
innovation.killer_doubt: No operator data shows how much is idle. Inference nodes now use host DRAM as the KV tier (Dynamo, LMCache), and a shared 200-400 Gb/s frontend NIC limits harvest bandwidth.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Collect 30 days of per-node host-memory telemetry (RSS, page cache, KV-tier use) from 2 GPU-cloud partners for training and inference. Then run a 16-node RDMA-harvest pilot that measures GPU-job interference. About $150k.
innovation.prior_art: Infiniswap (NSDI'17), Fastswap, Microsoft Pond, Kove SDM and MemVerge software pooling, Liqid/UnifabriX/SK hynix Niagara CXL pools. No idle-fraction data found (via search snippet).

title: Rotational molding: scramble stashed activations so flips average to zero
idea: Rotomolding spins the mold on two axes so material deposits evenly, with no bias. DRAM retention failures are one-directional (charged cells lose charge), which biases the value errors. Activations saved for backprop are therefore stored at 4 bits in 1%-BER cells, XORed with a PRNG mask whose per-block seed lets the mask be regenerated on read. A charge-loss flip then means +2^k or -2^k with equal probability, so the noise is zero-mean and gradients stay unbiased, only slightly noisier than SGD already is.

physics.key_insight: The activation stash lives <~2 s, so refresh-withheld banks suffice. The phase-B tail model gives raw BER ~1.4e-5 at 1 s, 85 C, far below the 1% budgeted.
physics.killer_doubt: E[err|bit] stays nonzero, so codes shrink toward the midpoint. Controller scramblers already randomize flip direction. Unrefreshed banks lose TRR while hot rows see ~1e6 activations/s against a ~1k hammer threshold.
physics.decisive_experiment: On an FPGA DDR5/HBM tester, measure the raw BER of refresh-withheld banks at 85-95 C over 0.2-2 s under training-like row activations, hammering included. Inject the measured error maps into 4-bit-stash training of a 1B model. ~$150k.
physics.prior_art: ActNN (ICML 2021) 2-bit activation stash; RANA (ISCA 2018) lifetime-aware eDRAM refresh; Flikker (ASPLOS 2011); Intel/AMD DDR data scramblers; Phase B B4-04.

innovation.key_insight: Per-step reseeded XOR masks turn one-way charge-loss flips into decorrelated +/-2^k errors, making quantized training stashes a natural customer for 4-level approximate DRAM (N-66).
innovation.killer_doubt: Alone it adds little: ActNN already gets ~12x with 2-bit stashes (via search snippet). At 1% BER error noise is ~10x 4-bit quantization noise; payoff needs N-66-class 2x-bit cells.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Train Llama-1B with 2-4-bit stashes under charge-loss and 4-level adjacent-drift error models at BER 1e-4 to 1e-2, masks on and off; compare loss curves. Then measure relaxed-refresh error direction on DRAM-Bender. ~$60k.
innovation.prior_art: ActNN (ICML'21) unbiased 2-bit activation compression; EDEN (MICRO'19); memory-controller data scrambling and DRAM true/anti cells [training knowledge]; Phase B N-66. Debiasing combination: none found.

title: Memory on window glass: multi-tier oxide TFT cells on display lines
idea: Inverts 'memory is made on 300 mm silicon wafers': run 1T1C cells on idle Gen-8.5 to Gen-10.5 LCD/OLED glass lines, stacking 10-20 tiers with KrF-class litho at ~0.3 um and oxide-TFT access whose ultralow leakage lets tiny capacitors skip refresh; dice panels into tiles bonded to a small CMOS controller.

physics.key_insight: Display fabs have idle Gen-8.5-10.5 area ~100x cheaper per m2; IGZO TFTs already run there and <1 aA leakage tolerates big, slow cells.
physics.killer_doubt: Production display litho resolves ~1-2 um, not 0.3 um: at F=1.5 um, 20 tiers give ~1.4 TB per Gen-10.5 panel, ~$1.4-5.7/GB, no better than DDR5's $1.48/GB.
physics.decisive_experiment: On a Gen-2/4 research glass line, pattern 0.5 um IGZO 1T1C arrays by NIL or high-res FPD stepper; measure killer-defect density per mask and 4-tier overlay. Break-even needs F<=0.7 um at 20 tiers.
physics.prior_art: SEL (a display company) CAAC-IGZO DOSRAM/NOSRAM, on Si BEOL; our N-36 BEOL cell line on glass carriers; none at Gen-10.5 scale.

innovation.key_insight: Idle Gen-8.5+ display lines cost ~100x less per area-tier than DRAM fabs and already run oxide TFTs. It is a capital-light capacity tier if sub-micron patterning on glass exists.
innovation.killer_doubt: Display litho resolves ~1.5-3 um, not 0.3 um. At F=1.5 um, 20 tiers need ~39 cm2 of glass per GB and cost ~$2-4/GB, no cheaper than DDR5 to make.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Build a cost/density model plus a 2-tier IGZO 1T1C array on a G2-G4.5 R&D glass line, with an NIL or interference-litho trial at 0.3-0.5 um. Measure retention and bitline signal. About $500k.
innovation.prior_art: SEL CAAC-IGZO DOSRAM/NOSRAM; Sharp/JDI memory-in-pixel LCDs; PragmatIC flexible IGZO ICs; Phase B N-36 glass-carrier cell line. Multi-tier glass DRAM: none found.

title: Librarian's catalog: signed lifetime passport on every DIMM
idea: Each module's SPD carries a signed lifetime log written by the host BMC: power-on hours, thermal history, corrected-error counts, row-hammer events. Second-hand buyers can grade modules the way a library tracks a book's condition, and a public registry prices reuse by verified health.

physics.key_insight: Buyer distrust of used DIMMs is real friction; a host-written lifetime log (hours, temperature, corrected errors, hammer events) holds grading data that one-shot bench tests miss.
physics.killer_doubt: SPD is a copyable ~1 KB EEPROM (~1e5-1e6 writes): a BMC-signed log can be cloned onto a worse DIMM unless bound to a die fingerprint such as its retention-failure map.
physics.decisive_experiment: Firmware pilot (~$150k): BMCs write signed logs to 1,000 DIMMs for a year; test whether logs predict post-retirement retention and error rates, and try cloning against a retention-map binding.
physics.prior_art: BMC and Redfish memory error logs; DDR5 SPD hub thermal sensor; Blancco-style ITAD certificates; stage-2 HOLD I-08260 (retention-map certificate).

innovation.key_insight: Field studies show past corrected errors strongly predict future failures; a signed per-DIMM log carries that signal, which a short burn-in cannot, into resale of reclaimed DDR5.
innovation.killer_doubt: For DDR4 the binding barrier is DDR5-only sockets, not trust. Seller-signed logs need operator keys; if history beats a 1-hour test by under 2x at predicting failures, drop.
innovation.decisive_experiment: From one partner fleet, take 2,000 DIMMs with 3+ years of BMC error logs, burn-in test them, then run 6 months in a CXL tier. Compare history versus burn-in as predictors of second-life UEs. ~$150k.
innovation.prior_art: Schroeder et al., DRAM errors in the wild (SIGMETRICS 2009); EU Digital Product Passport (ESPR); DDR5 SPD end-user bytes [training knowledge]. DIMM passport: none found.

title: Gist tokens replace old context; raw chunks re-expand from flash
idea: Box: summarize × agent runtime × document chunk × leaves recent window × raw tokens on SSD. Older chunks are replaced by a few learned gist tokens' KV; if attention to a gist crosses a threshold the runtime re-prefills the original chunk from flash (zoom-in).

physics.key_insight: Attention mass landing on a gist works as a free error detector that tells you when lossy KV compression failed, making compression recoverable rather than blind.
physics.killer_doubt: A chunk's true KV depends on every prior token, so isolated re-prefill is inexact. Each zoom re-prefill of 2k tokens on 70B (~3e14 FLOP) stalls decode 0.1-0.5 s.
physics.decisive_experiment: Fine-tune an 8B model with gist tokens and an attention-threshold zoom trigger. On RULER/LongBench-v2 at 128k, measure accuracy, zoom rate and KV bytes against full KV, Quest and InfLLM. ~$30k of GPU time.
physics.prior_art: Gist tokens (Mu et al. 2023), Activation Beacon, Landmark Attention, InfLLM block retrieval, CacheBlend partial recompute.

innovation.key_insight: Keep cheap raw tokens on flash and let attention mass on a gist trigger exact re-prefill. Lossy KV compression becomes a recoverable cache with fidelity on demand.
innovation.killer_doubt: Re-prefilling a 4k-token chunk on a 70B model is ~0.57 PFLOP, about a 1 s stall. Above one zoom per ~50 tokens, throughput collapses. Chunk-local re-prefill loses cross-chunk context.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Llama-3.1-8B with Activation-Beacon-style 16-32x gists on RULER, LongBench-v2 and agent traces. Log gist-attention triggers and compare accuracy recovered with zoom on and off against the zoom rate. Under $50k of GPU time.
innovation.prior_art: Gist tokens (Mu et al. 2023), Activation Beacon, ICAE, InfLLM block retrieval, CacheBlend selective recompute. The attention-triggered re-prefill from raw tokens is the new twist.

title: Vertical 3D charge-coupled shift-register memory with one regenerator per string
idea: Po: the bit is a rumor passed down a line. Store charge packets in potential wells along a tall vertical channel with dozens of stacked gate layers (3D NAND-like tiers clocked as a CCD); packets shift up and down and only the end-of-string regenerating sense amp restores them, so refresh is the shifting itself, with no per-bit capacitor or access transistor.

physics.key_insight: Per-string regeneration relaxes CTE need to ~0.999 (64 bits x 3 phases = 192 transfers, <20% loss), achievable by 1970s surface-channel CCDs; NAND tiers give 4-8x density without EUV.
physics.killer_doubt: Poly-Si grain-boundary traps and dark generation (~100 fA fills a 1,000 e- well in ~2 ms); IGZO tail-state deferred charge unmeasured; 100 ns-1 us serial access = capacity tier.
physics.decisive_experiment: University-fab 16-gate IGZO CCD (planar first, then 8-tier vertical): measure CTE versus clock rate, fat zero and 25-85 C, plus dark charge; go if CTE >=0.9995 at 10 MHz. ~$300k.
physics.prior_art: 1970s CCD main/bulk memories (Fairchild, Intel, ~64 kb); our own N-08 vertical oxide CCD (ALIVE-SPEC); no oxide-channel CTE data found in C0 searches.

innovation.key_insight: Clocked 3D-NAND-style tiers store bits with no per-bit transistor or capacitor; an oxide channel gives near-zero dark current; imec's planar IGZO CCD (>1e10 cycles, >200 s) supports the physics.
innovation.killer_doubt: Snippet CTE is only >98%. A 64-bit 4-phase vertical string needs per-transfer CTE >=0.9999 (256 transfers keep 97%). Serial 0.1-1 us access confines it to a buffer/capacity tier.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Build a 4-8-tier vertical IGZO CCD string (gate stack, hole etch, ALD IGZO) at a university fab. Measure per-transfer CTE vs clock rate and 85 C dark generation against imec planar data. About $400k.
innovation.prior_art: imec IGZO 3D CCD buffer memory: planar 142-bit, CTE>98%, >200 s, >1e10 cycles (via search snippet); 1970s CCD memories; overturns N-08 'open territory'.

title: Certified pre-owned DRAM: re-profiled hyperscaler memory with warranty
idea: Borrowed from certified pre-owned cars: a 10-person shop buys DIMMs from retired cloud servers by the ton, runs 48-hour retention, row-hammer and temperature profiling on FPGA test rigs, rewrites each DIMM's SPD with measured timing and refresh bins, swaps weak chips and sells warrantied modules for CXL memory expanders.

physics.key_insight: Per-DIMM measured retention, hammer and timing bins written into SPD turn anonymous used DIMMs into graded CXL capacity tiers for buyers who are not hyperscalers.
physics.killer_doubt: Feedstock. Hyperscalers (~half of server DRAM) now keep retired DDR4 internally (Meta Vistara), so open-market supply may be ~1-2 EB/yr against ~30+ EB/yr of new bits (estimate).
physics.decisive_experiment: Buy 500 retired RDIMMs at auction. FPGA-profile each for 48 h (85 C retention, hammer threshold, VRT), run 50 behind a Structera-X CXL server for 6 months logging CE/UE, and survey ITAD volumes. ~$250k.
physics.prior_art: Meta Vistara internal DDR4 reuse via CXL; Marvell Structera X 2404 (via search snippet); Microsoft GreenSKU (prior knowledge, unverified); refurbished-RDIMM resellers.

innovation.key_insight: Measured per-DIMM timing and refresh bins written into the SPD, plus a warranty, form the trust layer that makes grey-market DIMMs an enterprise product.
innovation.killer_doubt: ITAD resellers already sell tested hyperscale DIMMs. The supply is one-time (DDR4 is end-of-life) and needs DDR4-capable CXL controllers that add ~70-100 ns.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Profile 500 retired DIMMs on FPGA rigs and rewrite their SPD bins. Track corrected and uncorrected errors in a CXL pool for 6 months against unbinned controls. Under $150k.
innovation.prior_art: ITRenew/Iron Mountain recertified hyperscale hardware; R27 I-08260 signed-certificate tester (HOLD); REAPER retention profiling; Microsoft GreenSKU.

title: Urban-mined DRAM: re-binned retired DIMM dies in CXL expanders
idea: Box [existing DDR4 die | existing access | existing sense | CXL Type-3 expander | retired server DIMMs | test + retention re-binning]: route decommissioned hyperscale DIMMs to a test line that sorts dies by retention and bit-error rate, then a CXL controller with strong ECC and per-bin refresh tuning presents them as pooled far memory.

physics.key_insight: DRAM has no wear-out, so retired DIMMs are near-new; retention re-binning, per-bin refresh and CXL-side ECC turn scrap into far memory at ~$0.3-1/GB.
physics.killer_doubt: Supply ceiling: server DRAM shipped ~2021, now retiring, is ~6-10% of 2026 bit demand even if a third party captures 30-50%; hyperscalers already reuse it internally.
physics.decisive_experiment: Buy 1,000 retired DDR4 RDIMMs; profile retention, VRT and row-hammer at 85 C; build a CXL-card prototype; measure usable-GB yield and W/GB versus new DDR5.
physics.prior_art: Microsoft GreenSKU (ISCA 2024) reuses DDR4 behind CXL; secondary DIMM brokers. From memory.

innovation.key_insight: Retention/BER re-binning plus per-bin refresh tuning lets marginal retired dies serve as far memory. Same core mechanism as I-00224.
innovation.killer_doubt: Duplicate of I-00224. Microsoft already runs reused DDR4 behind CXL, and re-binning likely rescues only ~5-10% more dies than pass/fail retest (estimate).
innovation.decisive_experiment: Folded into I-00224: profile per-row retention of 1,000 retired DDR4 RDIMMs at 85 C, and count dies rescued by per-bin refresh versus plain pass/fail.
innovation.prior_art: Microsoft GreenSKU reused DDR4 via CXL (ISCA 2024); Marvell Structera X DDR4-capable CXL controller; ITAD resale (ITRenew/Iron Mountain).

title: Magnify DIMM lifespan 3x via a reclamation exchange
idea: Hyperscalers retire servers every 4-6 years with healthy DIMMs; robotic test-and-rebin centers grade them (retention, row-hammer threshold, speed) and repackage them into CXL Type-3 memory-expander sleds resold as a capacity tier with a 3-year warranty.

physics.key_insight: Grading retired DIMMs on retention, row-hammer threshold and speed, then binning them into CXL sleds with per-bin refresh and mitigation, makes marginal parts sellable under warranty.
physics.killer_doubt: Retiring server DRAM is ~6-10% of bit demand; hyperscalers reuse much internally. Full hammer screening is ~2M rows per die at ~10 ms each, hours per rank; sampling must suffice.
physics.decisive_experiment: Test 1,000 retired DDR4 RDIMMs on FPGA testers (~$300k): map retention and HCfirst per module, then show bin-tuned refresh gives zero uncorrected errors over 90 days in a CXL sled.
physics.prior_art: Microsoft GreenSKU; ITRenew/Sesame rack reuse; refurbished DIMM resellers; SAFARI DRAM Bender testers; stage-2 HOLD I-06172 (same mechanism).

innovation.key_insight: Grading retired DIMMs by retention and row-hammer threshold lets an exchange route weak parts to cold, single-tenant tiers and sell warranted capacity at ~20-30% of new.
innovation.killer_doubt: Hyperscalers reuse their own retirements (GreenSKU), leaving the exchange the leftovers; DDR4 prices rose after 2025 EOL notices [training knowledge], squeezing a ~20-30%-of-new price.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Grade 2,000 retired DDR4 RDIMMs for retention at 45-85 C, row-hammer threshold (DRAM Bender-style FPGA) and speed bin. Report yield per grade, test cost per GB and landed $/GB in a CXL sled. ~$250k.
innovation.prior_art: ITRenew/Iron Mountain Sesame resale; Microsoft GreenSKU (ISCA 2024); Marvell Structera X; DRAM Bender/SoftMC testers; study item I-00224 (HOLD).

title: Fifty-electron bit read by repeated non-destructive skipper sampling
idea: MINIFY the stored charge ~600x (from ~30,000 e- to ~50 e-): the storage node is a ~0.01 fF floating diffusion with no capacitor, and a per-subarray skipper-CCD-style floating-gate amplifier shuttles the packet under its sense gate N=16 times, averaging read noise below 1 e- rms before write-back.

physics.key_insight: At 0.01-0.02 fF one electron is ~8-16 mV, so 50 e- give ~0.4-0.8 V: read noise vanishes and skipper averaging is unnecessary. The real question is minimum charge per bit.
physics.killer_doubt: Holding 50 e- within 10 e- for 1 s needs <=1.6 aA at the 1e-6 tail; one Si midgap trap emits ~1e3 e-/s at 85 C; skipper samples ~10 us.
physics.decisive_experiment: IGZO 2T0C array with a minimal ~0.02 fF node on a university BEOL line (~$300k): map per-cell charge loss in electrons over 1e4 cells at 85 C, plus 1e6 neighbour-wordline toggles.
physics.prior_art: Skipper CCDs (Tiffenberg et al., PRL 2017) reach 0.068 e- rms over ms (training knowledge); imec IGZO 2T0C and IGZO CCD memory store sub-1,000 e-.

innovation.key_insight: With an IGZO node (~1 aA), transfer-path noise, not leakage, limits the electron count. A capacitor-free 1T node at ~200-300 e- on short bitlines would be 3D-ready.
innovation.killer_doubt: Frozen kTC on a 35 fF bitline is ~82 e- rms; 50 e- at 8 sigma needs a <=0.06 fF path (CCD or in-cell gain). Skipper cannot average pre-transfer noise.
innovation.decisive_experiment: A ~$400k test: a BEOL-IGZO MPW array with 0.02-0.1 fF 1T nodes on 8-, 16- and 64-cell bitlines, read by charge-transfer pre-sense plus CDS. Measure BER against electrons per bit (50-1,000) and the 85 C retention tail.
innovation.prior_art: Hitachi PLEDM few-electron gain cell (1990s); Fermilab skipper CCD (Tiffenberg 2017); Fossum/Gigajot QIS jots; triage N-04, N-84, N-08 [training knowledge].

title: One global clock restores every cell: gated-diode charge-pump bistables
idea: Inverts 'refresh is done row by row by sense amps': each cell is a gated diode (large capacitance when inverted, small when depleted) tied to a shared plate clock and a diode to the supply; a stored '1' couples the clock strongly and is topped up each cycle while a '0' couples weakly and stays below the diode threshold, so one global clock refreshes billions of cells at once.

physics.key_insight: Effectively a parametron memory: one global pump sustains bistable states in nonlinear accumulation/depletion capacitors, removing refresh controllers and tRFC bandwidth loss.
physics.killer_doubt: Clock energy CV2f: 0.6 fF x (2 V)^2 x 1 kHz = 2.4 pW/cell, ~3x today's refresh (~0.7 pW/bit) unless resonant drive recovers >70%; 6-sigma margin across 1e10 cells.
physics.decisive_experiment: 1-kb IGZO or SKY130 array with off-chip LC-resonant plate drive: map both stable points versus clock amplitude, frequency and temperature; measure hold power per cell and error rate. ~$250k.
physics.prior_art: Goto parametron (1954) global-pump bistables; IBM gated-diode eDRAM cells (~2006); TI tunnel-diode SRAM (~1999) (from memory). Global-clock DRAM self-refresh not verified.

innovation.key_insight: A nonlinear (gated-diode) capacitance makes one broadcast plate clock a parametric charge pump. Stored 1s are restored in place, with no row refresh, tRFC stalls or refresh controller.
innovation.killer_doubt: Leakage spans ~1e3x across 1e9 cells, yet one pump amplitude must serve all. A 1 kHz, 1 fF, 1 V plate clock costs ~9 mW/GB, about refresh's ~6 mW/GB.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Build a 1 kb open-PDK (SKY130/IHP) array of gated-diode, diode and access cells with an on-chip plate clock. Map bistable margin against Vt spread, 85 C leakage and clock energy, with and without resonant clocking. About $80k.
innovation.prior_art: IBM gated-diode 2T1D gain cells (Luk, Dennard, mid-2000s); Goto parametron pumped bistable (1954); Phase B N-03 gated-diode strip. Broadcast self-refresh: none found.

title: Correlated double sampling sense amps read 0.2 fF cells
idea: Sample the bitline before and after charge sharing onto two capacitors in a logic-process sense amp and amplify the difference, cancelling offset and 1/f noise so the required signal approaches the sqrt(kT/C) floor instead of a 6-sigma mismatch margin.

physics.key_insight: CDS cancels sense-amp offset and frozen bitline kTC (0.41 mV rms on 30 fF, 85 C). A 0.5 fF cell gives 8 mV (~14 sigma): 10x less capacitor.
physics.killer_doubt: At 0.2 fF, 64 ms allows ~250 e- loss: <=0.6 fA, ~20x below the 13 fA Si tail, so it needs an IGZO access device. WL kickback adds ~2 mV.
physics.decisive_experiment: A 28 nm MPW (~$300k): MIM cells of 0.2/0.5/1 fF on 30 fF bitlines with a CDS versus a latch sense amp, plus dummy-WL coupling compensation. Measure BER vs Cs and temperature to 1e-9.
physics.prior_art: Samsung and Hynix offset-cancellation sense amps in production DDR4/5; Hitachi charge-transfer pre-sensing; triage N-04, N-27 auto-zero [training knowledge].

innovation.key_insight: Sampling the bitline before and after charge sharing cancels offset, 1/f noise and precharge kTC together, a ~3-10 mV floor. Best as a logic-process sense amp under bonded cells.
innovation.killer_doubt: Offset-cancelling SAs already ship. Data-dependent BL-BL and WL coupling arise during sharing, which CDS cannot cancel. A 0.5 fF cell on a 13 fA leakage tail needs ~10 ms refresh.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Add a CDS arm to the N-04/I-11588 28-65 nm MPW. Use emulated 30 fF bitlines with 0.2-2 fF MIM cells and measure BER versus Cs under checkerboard and all-0 patterns at 85 C. ~+$50k.
innovation.prior_art: Samsung/SK hynix offset-cancellation sense amps (OCSA) in production; CIS CDS readout; Phase B N-04 charge-transfer pre-sense; advanced I-11588 neutralised bitline (training knowledge).

title: Two-hundred-variant bit-cell zoo on every shuttle run
idea: MAGNIFY variants and MINIFY cost per experiment: tile 200 bit-cell variants (gain cells, varactor caps, bootstrapped switches, leakage latches) with on-die retention/endurance BIST on each $10-20k MPW shuttle, publish an open retention-tail database and license the winners.

physics.key_insight: Parallel cell iteration with on-die retention BIST is the right test method; fold it into each dossier's test plan rather than treating it as an invention.
physics.killer_doubt: Logic MPWs lack the IGZO, high-k MIM and HAR modules where the open unknowns live; 200 variants on ~10 mm2 give ~1e4 cells each, blind to 1e-6 retention tails.
physics.decisive_experiment: One GF180 shuttle: 20 variants x 64 kb with BIST plus a 1 Mb reference array; check whether lognormal fits from 1e4 cells predict the measured 1e-5 tail. ~$40k.
physics.prior_art: Gain-cell eDRAM MPW test chips (Bar-Ilan, EPFL groups); foundry retention test vehicles; open-PDK shuttle supply fragile since Efabless closed in 2025.

innovation.key_insight: Reframed: on-die BIST cycling is the only cheap way to reach the 7e13-cycle hot-row endurance target in days. That measurement decides ~15 of 31 speculative triage verdicts.
innovation.killer_doubt: 200 variants share a ~10 mm2 slot, ~10k cells each, so tails resolve only to ~1e-4, not ppm. Logic MPWs cannot host the oxide or ferroic cells that matter.
innovation.decisive_experiment: One ~$150k shuttle: 10-20 variants x 1e5 cells, plus ZrO2/HZO MIM coupons post-deposited on top metal at <=400 C. Run on-die cycling to 1e13 and 85 C retention maps against an external pulse tester.
innovation.prior_art: Foundry/imec test vehicles and TEGs; RRAM-on-foundry-CMOS array chips (e.g., NeuRRAM 2022); Si gain-cell retention studies (Bar-Ilan, EPFL) [training knowledge].

title: Fiber-drawn salami capacitor arrays sliced into wafers
idea: Imposed scarcity: no lithography and no high-AR etch. Assemble a glass preform of millimetre metal-cored, glass-clad coaxial rods, thermally draw and restack-redraw it (as photonic-crystal fiber makers do) until cores reach ~50 nm pitch, then slice the fused bundle into 5 um discs and hybrid-bond them to a CMOS access-transistor wafer.

physics.key_insight: No-etch capacitor mold: etchable-core nanochannel glass with 30-50 nm pores, sliced 1-5 um and ALD-lined TiN/ZrO2/TiN, gives ~3-5 fF per um. CMOS keeps the switches.
physics.killer_doubt: Molten metal cores break up (Rayleigh-Plateau, ~ms at 25 nm radius), forcing etchable cores. Then ~1% draw-pitch disorder misregisters 50 nm-pitch pores against transistors within ~100 cells.
physics.decisive_experiment: Draw etchable-core nanochannel glass to 50 nm pores (~$200k), slice 2 um discs, ALD MIM-fill, and bond to a pad wafer with pads wider than pitch for registration-free contact. Measure fF/pad, leakage, shorts and open-pore yield.
physics.prior_art: NRL nanochannel glass (Tonucci et al., Science 1992, ~33 nm channels); photonic-crystal-fiber stack-and-draw; Phase B AAO-Cap B2-01; R16 DROP I-01820. From memory.

innovation.key_insight: Draw-redraw gives billions of AR~100 coaxes with no etch: a 5 um slice with 20 nm core and 5 nm k~7 glass holds ~5 fF per coax.
innovation.killer_doubt: Cell-level bonding at DRAM pitch (~40-50 nm) is ~10x finer than today's ~0.4-1 um hybrid-bond pitch, draw disorder defeats registration, and molten metal cores bead up below ~100 nm.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Draw-redraw an etchable-core glass bundle to 50-100 nm pores, slice 5 um, ALD TiN/ZrO2/TiN, then measure fF/um2, leakage and pore-position disorder versus an ideal lattice. ~$250k.
innovation.prior_art: NRL nanochannel glass (Tonucci et al., Science 1992, ~33 nm channels by draw-redraw); microchannel plates; Phase B N-21 anodic-alumina capacitor template, which is cheaper.

title: Retention-DLTS fingerprints the defect species behind the leakage tail
idea: Treat a commodity DRAM as a billion-pixel deep-level transient spectrometer. Measure each weak cell's retention time against temperature (the Arrhenius slope gives trap energy) and against wordline/plate bias (the field-enhancement factor separates Poole-Frenkel, phonon-assisted tunneling and GIDL). Cluster the signatures across vendors and lots to name the dominant defect species (Fe-B, vacancy-oxygen, interface Pb centers).

physics.key_insight: One retention atlas versus temperature and bias measures the tail's activation energy and field mechanism, which decides N-42 (3x or 18x from cooling), N-63 and this batch's refresh ideas.
physics.killer_doubt: Standalone payoff is small: vendors already do internal failure analysis, and if tail Ea is ~0.2-0.3 eV (GIDL/TAT), cooling 85 to 35 C buys only ~3-5x.
physics.decisive_experiment: FPGA testers and thermal chambers on ~100 DDR4/DDR5/LPDDR5 dies from three vendors (~$300k): per-cell retention at 25-95 C and three wordline-low biases; extract Ea and field-enhancement histograms across the 1e-9 to 1e-5 tail.
physics.prior_art: Hamamoto 1998 retention activation energies; Umeda et al. 2006 EDMR linked VRT to a vacancy-oxygen defect; SAFARI retention studies (Liu 2013, REAPER 2017).

innovation.key_insight: Per-cell Arrhenius slope plus bias dependence separates Poole-Frenkel, trap-assisted tunnelling and GIDL. Useful only as calibration data for refresh-relaxation models such as I-07888 and I-11108.
innovation.killer_doubt: No step change: refresh is 16-33% of idle power, so even halving the tail saves <=15%. Outsiders cannot act on it; vendors run deeper in-house EFA.
innovation.decisive_experiment: The study itself (~$300k): retention versus 45-95 C and wordline-off bias on ~1e5 weak cells from three vendors' DDR5 using DRAM Bender. Pass if signatures cluster into <=3 classes. Even a pass settles little.
innovation.prior_art: Hamamoto, IEEE TED 1998, retention distribution; Restle 1992 and Mori 2005 on VRT; Liu ISCA 2013 and REAPER 2017 on temperature (training knowledge).

title: Vertical charge-coupled memory: no switch per bit, just moving charge
idea: Inverts 'every bit needs its own access transistor': deposit a 200-layer gate/oxide stack (NAND-style, one hole etch), line each hole with a poly-Si or oxide channel, and clock the layer gates in 3 phases so charge packets march along the hole like a vertical CCD. Each hole holds ~60 bits and one sense/regeneration stage at the top restores packets as they circulate, so refresh is continuous and free.

physics.key_insight: One hole etch and no per-bit transistor or capacitor: CCD-clocked NAND word planes give ~1.8-3.7 Gb/mm2 (4-8x 1-beta) at single-exposure ArF, with channel-written charge and unlimited endurance.
physics.killer_doubt: 180 transfers per circulation needs CTE >=0.99994; ~250 e- packets against ~10-90 traps per gate leave poly or amorphous channels near 0.999. Cost is ~2-3x below DRAM, not 100x.
physics.decisive_experiment: University-fab planar overlapping-gate IGZO CCD, plus a buried-channel bilayer variant, with 16-32 gates (~$300k): CTE versus clock (1-100 MHz), fat zero and temperature to 85 C; build vertical stacks only if >=0.9999.
physics.prior_art: 1970s serial CCD memories (Intel, Fairchild); our Phase B N-08 vertical oxide CCD; no vertical-CCD memory patent found (via search snippet).

innovation.key_insight: Clocked word planes shift packets through a semiconductor channel. Writes avoid the tunnel-oxide endurance wall, with no per-bit transistor, capacitor or staircase and one regenerator per hole.
innovation.killer_doubt: 60 bits x 3 phases = 180 transfers: at CTE 0.999, 16% of charge is lost. Far bit ~1-5 us away (NAND-class); poly-Si dark current forces constant clocking.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Merge into I-10793's test: a 16-32-tier IGZO vertical CCD in a university fab (~$400k) measuring per-transfer CTE, 85 C dark charge and gate cycling to 1e12. Drop the poly-Si variant.
innovation.prior_art: imec IGZO CCD buffer memory (IEDM 2024 planar, IMW 2026 vertical; per R16/R06 search logs); 1970s Intel/Fairchild CCD memories; Phase B N-08; I-10793.

title: Vertical codewords across tiers break 3D DRAM yield compounding
idea: Combine 3D NAND-style tier stacking with tier-orthogonal coding: each codeword takes one symbol from each of ~32 tiers along the vertical bitline, so a defective tier (lateral-transistor shorts, capacitor voids) costs only one symbol per codeword. Per-tier yield can then be 99% rather than 99.99%.

physics.key_insight: Diagonal tier-to-mat interleaving makes a dead tier one erasure per codeword. Tier-yield compounding becomes a ~6-12% parity overhead, which helps every 3D DRAM cell.
physics.killer_doubt: WL-WL and WL-BL shorts load drivers and vertical bitlines shared by 32 tiers, so failures are not tier-confined. Erasure coding fixes 0.99^32 = 72% only if shorts are isolated.
physics.decisive_experiment: Run a Monte Carlo of 3D NAND-style defect maps (opens, shorts, voids) on a rotated tier-to-mat address map with RS(36,32) erasure decoding, and write decoder RTL to get latency and area. Software plus FPGA, ~$100k.
physics.prior_art: Chipkill (IBM 1997); SSD RAIN and die-RAID across NAND planes; no 3D-DRAM tier-orthogonal code found (prior knowledge).

innovation.key_insight: In 3D DRAM, defects cluster by tier (plane shorts, voids). Coding orthogonal to tiers turns a dead tier into one erasure per codeword rather than a dead block.
innovation.killer_doubt: Two spare tiers per 32 already tolerate 1% tier-defect rates (block yield ~99.5%); vertical-bitline arrays cannot read 32 tiers in one activation without bitline collisions.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Run a Monte Carlo of tier-, line- and cell-level defect maps for a 32-128 tier array, comparing die yield and area for tier sparing, row/column redundancy plus ECC, and cross-tier codes. Software, under $30k.
innovation.prior_art: Micron RAIN parity across NAND planes and dies; Chipkill symbol codes; HBM on-die ECC; 3D NAND bad-block management with spare blocks (training knowledge).

title: Mail carrier's local post offices: a sense amp every 32 cells
idea: Mail goes out from local post offices, not one central depot. Hybrid-bond a sense-amp wafer under the array so every 32 cells get their own sense amp on a ~0.05 fF micro-bitline, which cuts the charge a cell needs from ~5 fF to ~0.3 fF. The capacitor becomes a shallow planar MIM, the array shrinks to 4F^2, and 6 array decks share one sense wafer.

physics.key_insight: Concrete form of the solved-read thesis: 32-cell bitline (~1-1.5 fF real, not 0.05) lets a 0.2-0.3 fF stub replace the 1.3 um AR-60 pillar and VARY drop toward 0.4 V.
physics.killer_doubt: Sense amp in ~0.04 um2: sigma-Vt ~40-60 mV vs ~100 mV signal; 6 decks need per-32-cell vias through 5 wafers; 0.3 fF needs IGZO (<1 fA tail).
physics.decisive_experiment: 22/28 nm MPW (~$250k): arrays of offset-compensated micro-SAs in a 0.04-0.08 um2 footprint sensing 0.2-0.3 fF MIM cells on 1-1.5 fF bitlines; map offset and BER to 1e-6 at 85 C.
physics.prior_art: IBM POWER7 eDRAM micro-SA (~32 cells/local bitline); Samsung 4F2 VCT periphery-under-cell via bonding; imec/EVG 200 nm W2W bond pitch (ECTC 2026, via search snippet).

innovation.key_insight: Sensing every ~32 cells drops bitline capacitance to ~2-3 fF, so ~0.3 fF still gives ~50 mV: the capacitor shrinks ~15x and the 60-75:1 etch disappears.
innovation.killer_doubt: Planar MIM in 4F2 at F=12 nm gives ~0.04 fF, not 0.3; and one bond per 32 cells, even shared over 6 decks, needs ~330 nm pitch, beyond hybrid-bonding practice.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Tape out a 28 nm MPW test chip with 32-cell micro-bitlines, 0.1-0.5 fF short-pillar or MIM cells and offset-cancelled sense amps; measure signal-margin distribution over 1e5 cells versus Cs.
innovation.prior_art: Samsung/SK hynix 4F2 VCT with periphery-under-cell bonding; Phase B N-40 (64-cell bitlines, 8:1 mux, ~1 um bonds) is the feasible-pitch version.

title: Vacuum pack with crash foam: compress pages, fill freed space with ECC
idea: Packers shrink-wrap a product and fill the leftover box space with foam. Each 4 KB page in the compressed tier is compressed, and the freed bytes hold a long LDPC/BCH code sized to the space left over. At page scale, 1% raw BER needs about 15-23% parity, so any page that compresses 1.3x or better carries its own armor at no capacity cost. Incompressible pages go to a small protected tier.

physics.key_insight: Page-scale codes make 1% raw BER usable: channel capacity needs ~8% parity and BCH ~23%. A compressed far tier becomes a home for weak dies and low-charge cells.
physics.killer_doubt: Beyond N-62 (1e-4, line BCH), going from 3.7 to 2.3 sigma buys only ~1.6x less charge but costs microsecond page decode and 4 KB read-modify-write; VRT drift breaks fixed parity.
physics.decisive_experiment: DRAM-Bender on 20 DDR4/DDR5 DIMMs: map BER against refresh interval (1-16 s) and temperature, and VRT stability over weeks. Run an FPGA compress-plus-BCH controller on real page traces (~$150k).
physics.prior_art: COP (ISCA 2015) and Frugal ECC (SC 2015) compression-funded line ECC; CREAM (HPCA 2017); NAND LDPC controllers. Page-scale 1%-BER DRAM tier: none found.

innovation.key_insight: At 4 KB, 1% raw BER needs only ~8% parity at Shannon (~15-23% practical). Pages compressing >=1.3x carry free LDPC, giving immature cells a 1e-2 landing zone.
innovation.killer_doubt: DRAM errors cluster by row, column and chip, not iid: one dead x8 chip garbles 1/8 of a page. Each random 64 B write becomes a 4 KB read-modify-write (64x).
innovation.decisive_experiment: On an FPGA CXL board, run DDR4 rejects and DIMMs at 8-64x tREFI and 85 C, and log error maps. Replay real page traces through LZ4 plus page LDPC. Report net capacity, decode latency and uncorrectable rate.
innovation.prior_art: COP (Palframan et al., ISCA 2015); Frugal ECC (SC15) and US 8458568, compression for weak pages (via search snippet); NAND LDPC; fold into R21 I-01312.

title: Wafer-scale DRAM bonded under a wafer-scale accelerator replaces HBM
idea: Substitute HBM stacks plus interposer with one full DRAM wafer hybrid-bonded face-to-face to a wafer-scale processor: each compute tile gets the DRAM directly beneath it through ~2 um-pitch bonds, and defective DRAM tiles are routed around by the processor's existing redundancy fabric.

physics.key_insight: A face-to-face DRAM wafer under a wafer-scale engine gives ~3.9 TB at <0.3 pJ/bit with no TSV signal path; the processor's tile redundancy already absorbs DRAM tile defects.
physics.killer_doubt: Power and cooling need opposite faces: ~20 kW at 0.8 V is ~25 kA through DRAM TSVs; W2W voids at ~0.1/cm2 (estimate) leave ~70 dead regions per wafer pair.
physics.decisive_experiment: D2W hybrid-bond a DRAM test die face-to-face onto a 28 nm logic die at 2-6 um pitch, thinned (~$350k); measure bond yield, pJ/bit and 105 C retention under a 0.5 W/mm2 heater.
physics.prior_art: Phase B N-41 carrier-is-memory (includes wafer-scale variant); Cerebras WSE (SRAM only); Graphcore Bow WoW (power wafer, not DRAM); imec/EVG W2W bonding.

innovation.key_insight: A whole DRAM wafer bonded under a wafer-scale processor adds ~2-3 TB at <0.3 pJ/bit. The processor's redundancy fabric absorbs the wafer-to-wafer compound-yield risk.
innovation.killer_doubt: Wafer-scale compute dissipates ~0.5 W/mm² (estimate), so the DRAM runs at >=85-95 C with 2-4x refresh. The market is one or two vendors, and $1M cannot build a wafer-scale demo.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Die-to-wafer hybrid-bond a DRAM test die onto a heater-equipped logic die at 2-6 um pitch (~$300k). Measure bond yield, pJ/bit and retention tails at 85-110 C under 0.5 W/mm².
innovation.prior_art: Xi'an UniIC SeDRAM hybrid-bonded DRAM-on-logic (IEDM 2020) [training knowledge]; DRAM-wafer-to-processor patents (US 11,430,766); study's N-41 carrier-is-memory.

title: Substitute harvested second-life DRAM for newly fabricated bits
idea: Industrialize take-back of retired server DIMMs: robotic desoldering, at-speed retest with per-row retention profiling, and re-binning into CXL memory-expander cards for tier-2 memory, with controller ECC and adaptive refresh hiding weak cells.

physics.key_insight: Water claim checks out: ~8 m3 per wafer over 3,068 GB is ~2.6 L/GB (~0.33 L/Gb), so a reused bit avoids almost all fab water.
physics.killer_doubt: Duplicate of I-06172; robotic desoldering and reballing adds rework loss and cost versus reusing whole DIMMs, which are already socketed.
physics.decisive_experiment: Folded into I-06172's test; add a 500-package desolder, reball and retest run to price rework yield loss.
physics.prior_art: Same as I-06172: GreenSKU, used-DIMM brokers.

innovation.key_insight: The fastest supply lever in the batch: an estimated ~5-7 EB/yr of DDR4 retires (~15% of 2026 bit output) and can return as CXL far memory with zero wafers.
innovation.killer_doubt: Value capture. DDR4 secondary prices rise with the 4x spike. CXL card and controller add ~$0.3-0.8/GB and 70-150 ns, and hyperscalers already reuse their own retirements.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Buy 1,000 retired DDR4 RDIMMs, then retest and retention-profile them. Run a commercial CXL Type-3 DDR4 expander in a tier-2 cloud pilot. Report yield, landed $/GB and tiered-workload slowdown. ~$300k.
innovation.prior_art: Microsoft GreenSKU (ISCA 2024) reuses DDR4 via CXL; Marvell Structera X supports DDR4 reuse; ITRenew/Iron Mountain resell decommissioned hyperscale hardware.

title: Antiferroelectric latent-charge buffer holds stored-1 voltage on a plateau
idea: Reverse the capacitor dielectric's role from passive to defending its charge: use ZrO2-rich antiferroelectric HZO and bias the plate so a stored '1' sits just above the AFE back-switching voltage. As leakage drains the node, AFE domains switch back and release bound polarization charge (~10-20 uC/cm2), pinning the voltage on a plateau the way latent heat holds ice water at 0 C.

physics.key_insight: AFE back-switching releases 10-20 uC/cm2 at a fixed voltage versus ~2 uC/cm2 linear charge (k=40, 5 nm) in a 0.3 V droop: ~5-10x hold charge without taller pillars.
physics.killer_doubt: Every write of a '1' must exceed the forward switching field, so one full AFE transition per write; need 3e8-7e13 cycles, best AFE ZrO2 seen ~5e9.
physics.decisive_experiment: TiN/ZrO2-rich HZO/TiN MIM coupons (5-8 nm ALD): unipolar cycling to 1e11 at 85 C, measuring plateau hold charge and leakage each decade. ~$150k with university ALD.
physics.prior_art: Our N-01 AFE-reservoir ZrO2 stub (same endurance decision); morphotropic-phase-boundary HZO high-k DRAM dielectric work; AFE hafnia/zirconia energy-storage capacitor literature.

innovation.key_insight: AFE back-switching releases ~10-20 uC/cm2 at a fixed voltage, a latent-charge plateau worth ~2-3 V of linear ZrO2 charge. That could give ~5x hold time with no taller pillar.
innovation.killer_doubt: Each decay and rewrite is a full AFE transition: best endurance ~5e9 vs >=1e13 for hot rows. ~10 nm grains make a 20 nm capacitor's plateau a staircase.
innovation.decisive_experiment: On TiN/ZrO2/TiN MIM coupons (50 nm-10 um), bias at the back-switch plateau and drain through a calibrated fA-pA leak to measure the hold-time multiplier. Cycle 10 ns full transitions to 1e12 at 85 C. About $150k.
innovation.prior_art: NaMLab (Pesic et al.) biased-AFE ZrO2 memory and energy storage; SNU and others' MPB-HZO high-k DRAM capacitors; Phase B N-01 (same endurance blocker).

title: Shallow 1 fF pillars rescued by soft-decision sensing and LDPC
idea: Invert 'every cell must read correctly on its own' -> let cells be weak and the code be smart. Etch only 1 fF, AR ~15 pillars; sense amps emit 2-bit soft information (strong/weak 0/1) to an on-die LDPC decoder over 512-bit codewords, tolerating raw BER ~1e-3 that would kill a hard-decision chip.

physics.key_insight: Soft information turns small-margin reads into erasures, and latch resolution time supplies it almost free. Charge-transfer sensing and offset cancellation carry most of any 5x Cs cut.
physics.killer_doubt: Gaussian tails: raw BER 1e-4 to 1e-3 buys only 1.2x Cs (3.72 to 3.09 sigma). A 1 fF cell gives 14 mV on 35 fF; on-die LDPC adds ~10-20 ns.
physics.decisive_experiment: FPGA rig on commercial DDR4/DDR5 (~$80k): sweep tRCD and VARY per read to get per-cell margin as soft data, log error clustering per 512 b codeword, replay through soft LDPC versus BCH t=8.
physics.prior_art: Phase B N-62; in-study I-11559 and I-11148 (ADVANCE, same family); Hi-ECC (ISCA 2010); NAND soft-sensing LDPC; static weak-cell erasure maps (US 8,898,544).

innovation.key_insight: 2-bit soft sensing turns marginal reads into erasures. Its real value is as the aggressive operating-point knob of the N-62 ECC-paid-capacitor family, cheapest if a logic-process periphery hosts the decoder.
innovation.killer_doubt: Signal needed scales with Q^-1(BER): raw 1e-3 vs BCH-t8's 1e-4 is 3.09 vs 3.72 sigma, only 1.2x Cs. 1 fF gives ~14 mV on 35 fF.
innovation.decisive_experiment: FPGA rig on commercial DDR5 (~$80k): sweep VARY/tRCD to emulate 1-1.5 fF margins, log 2-bit SA-timing soft data per 512 b codeword, replay through soft LDPC vs BCH t=8; synthesize the decoder in 28 nm for ns/pJ.
innovation.prior_art: Phase B N-62; in-study I-11559, I-11148, I-07888 (ADVANCE); NAND soft-sense LDPC in SSD controllers; Hi-ECC (ISCA 2010). On-die soft LDPC DRAM: none found.

title: Bit-plane progressive fetch stops when precision suffices
idea: Eliminate low-order bits from the bus: store tensors transposed into bit-planes and fetch sign/exponent/MSB planes first; the consumer's datapath signals 'enough' as soon as the result (e.g., top-k ordering or a dot-product bound) can no longer change, and the remaining planes are never sent.

physics.key_insight: Exact interval bounds let an MSB-first plane fetch stop with no accuracy loss wherever a top-k or argmax consumes the result: LM-head sampling, MoE routing, vector retrieval.
physics.killer_doubt: With 4 of 16 planes, worst-case slack (sum|x|*max|w|/16) is ~40 logits, above ~10-20 logit gaps. Linear layers have no exact stop; the LM head is ~1.5% of 70B weights.
physics.decisive_experiment: GPU emulation (<$30k): interval-bound early termination on a Llama-70B LM head, KV key scoring and a FAISS-scale kNN index at batch 1-64. Report the fraction of planes skipped and the share of total decode bytes saved.
physics.prior_art: BitWeaving/V bit-sliced scans with early pruning (SIGMOD 2013); SpAtten progressive quantization; Energon multi-round mixed-precision filtering; SnaPEA early termination (ISCA 2018).

innovation.key_insight: Interval bounds from fetched MSB planes make termination exact: skipped planes cost no accuracy or retraining. Best fit is K-cache scoring for top-k attention, where ordering, not values, matters.
innovation.killer_doubt: LeOPArd (ISCA 2022) already terminates bit-serially and exactly, ~1.8x energy, on chip. In DRAM each extra plane round trip adds ~100 ns, and only comparison-fed operations qualify.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Dump INT8 K caches from an open 70B model on LongBench at 32k context; compute exact per-plane bounds for top-2% selection; measure K bytes skipped. Kill below 40%. About $20k GPU time.
innovation.prior_art: LeOPArd (ISCA 2022) exact bit-serial early termination (via search snippet); SpAtten progressive MSB fetch (HPCA 2021); SnaPEA; in-study I-02063 (HOLD).

title: Hadamard-spread embedding storage turns bit flips into faint Gaussian noise
idea: Shift the unit of meaning from bits to whole vectors: embeddings are stored after a fixed Hadamard rotation and spread-spectrum quantization, so any 1% of flipped bits perturb every coordinate slightly instead of wrecking a few; the inverse transform runs in the near-memory logic die as data streams out.

physics.key_insight: Rotation turns rare catastrophic flips into dense small noise. That helps outlier-sensitive nonlinear steps (softmax, top-k, max-inner-product) and could let ECC-paid arrays (N-62) relax margin for AI tensors.
physics.killer_doubt: Rotation conserves error energy. At 1% BER on int8, spread noise σ≈15 LSB vs ~30 LSB signal (SNR ≈6 dB). Only ~1e-3 works, and no high-BER DRAM SKU exists.
physics.decisive_experiment: Software only (<$20k GPU): inject 1e-4 to 1e-2 BER into int8 KV caches, embedding tables and ANN indexes. Compare plain, Hadamard-spread and MSB-only-ECC. Report the accuracy-vs-BER knee and the refresh or capacitor relaxation each knee allows.
physics.prior_art: EDEN approximate DRAM for DNNs (MICRO 2019). Flikker (ASPLOS 2011). QuaRot/SpinQuant Hadamard rotations (2024). Bit-error spreading for stored embeddings: none found.

innovation.key_insight: Rotating vectors before integer quantization bounds worst-case bit-flip damage and flattens outliers, so AI tensors degrade gracefully instead of catastrophically, as FP16 exponent flips do.
innovation.killer_doubt: Orthonormal transforms preserve error energy. At 1% BER a 128-d int8 vector takes ~10 flips (SNR ~6 dB). At a realistic 1e-4 BER, dropping ECC saves only ~12% capacity.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Software fault injection into FAISS, DLRM and KV tensors, with and without Hadamard spreading, at BER 1e-5 to 1e-2. Measure recall@10 and perplexity. About a week of GPU time, under $20k.
innovation.prior_art: EDEN (MICRO 2019) error-tolerant DNNs on approximate DRAM; QuaRot, QuIP# and SpinQuant Hadamard rotations; Flikker critical-data partitioning.

title: Open-hardware DRAM tester kits that issue signed grade certificates
idea: Learning from ham-radio networks, a 10-person company sells ~$300 FPGA tester kits with secure elements to e-waste recyclers worldwide. Each run produces a cryptographically signed certificate (pattern suite, retention, speed bin) bound to the module serial, so remote buyers can trust second-hand memory.

physics.key_insight: Bind the certificate to the module's DRAM retention-failure map, a physical unclonable fingerprint, instead of the rewritable SPD serial, so certificates cannot move to counterfeits.
physics.killer_doubt: A $300 FPGA tops out near DDR4-2400, so DDR5-4800+ speed bins need ~$5k+ parts; VRT cells make one-shot retention maps drift; the certificate price premium is unproven.
physics.decisive_experiment: Test 500 used DDR4 modules on DRAM Bender/SoftMC (~$100k): repeat retention maps over 30 days to measure fingerprint stability and VRT churn; sell 200 certified vs uncertified lots and compare prices.
physics.prior_art: ETH SAFARI SoftMC/DRAM Bender open FPGA testers; CST and RAMCHECK commercial testers; Blancco-style signed ITAD certificates; academic DRAM retention PUFs.

innovation.key_insight: A secure-element tester signs what it measured itself. Binding the certificate to a retention-error PUF, not the SPD serial, makes it uncopyable and enables reuse supply.
innovation.killer_doubt: SPD serials can be rewritten, so a certificate can move to a worse module. ITAD firms already sell tested DIMMs with warranty, so the premium may be <5%.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Build 10 FPGA kits ($30k). Fingerprint 1,000 used DIMMs by retention-failure map, re-identify them blind after 6 months and 85 C, and survey 20 brokers on the price premium for signed versus vendor-tested modules.
innovation.prior_art: CST and ITAD DIMM testers; MemTest86 Pro reports; Iron Mountain/ITRenew recertified hyperscale hardware; DRAM retention and latency PUFs (Keller 2014; Kim, HPCA 2018).

title: Rank/select engines enabling succinct trees and graphs in DRAM
idea: Information theory says an n-node tree needs only ~2n bits, yet pointer trees spend ~128n. Add rank/select and balanced-parentheses navigation units next to the memory controller so succinct encodings (LOUDS, BP, Elias-Fano adjacency lists) traverse in O(1) per hop at near-pointer speed.

physics.key_insight: Tree topology at ~2n bits versus ~128n for pointers is a large cut; an engine that chains rank-directory and bitvector reads inside the controller attacks succinctness's real cost, dependent misses.
physics.killer_doubt: x86 POPCNT/PDEP already do in-word rank/select in ~3 cycles; cost is 2-4 dependent ~100 ns DRAM misses per hop, and the controller saves only ~30-50 ns of fabric each.
physics.decisive_experiment: Build a rank/select/balanced-parentheses unit on an FPGA CXL memory expander (~$20k board); run LOUDS trie, BP tree and Elias-Fano graph BFS against pointer and SDSL-software versions. Continue only if within 1.5x pointer latency at 5x less memory.
physics.prior_art: SDSL-lite and Succinct (NSDI 2015) in software; SpZip (ISCA 2021) near-core graph decompression; FM-index rank accelerators and PIM for genomics, e.g. MEDAL (from memory).

innovation.key_insight: Succinct structures lose to pointers on dependent cache misses, not on space. A controller-side rank/select/BP unit that fuses the 2-3 misses per hop could run ~2n-bit trees at pointer speed.
innovation.killer_doubt: Large read-mostly indexes are already compressed (Lucene FST/postings, delta CSR graphs, GBWT), so against today the footprint gain is ~1.5-2x on a few-percent share of DRAM (estimate).
innovation.decisive_experiment: Build an FPGA or CXL-expander rank/select/BP unit. Run a LOUDS trie, Elias-Fano graph BFS and FM-index on 50-100 GB datasets against SDSL on Xeon and pointer baselines; report ns/hop and bytes/node. ~$300k.
innovation.prior_art: SDSL/sux software rank/select, SWAR/BMI2 select; FM-index FPGA accelerators in genomics [training knowledge]. No general near-memory rank/select unit found (via search snippet).

title: Eliminate low-order bits until needed: MSB-first bit-plane fetch
idea: Store tensors bit-plane transposed across sub-rows so the controller fetches the top 2-4 bit planes first; attention screening or early-exit logic requests the lower planes only for the ~5-10% of values that matter.

physics.key_insight: Attention scores tolerate low precision, so an MSB-first bit-plane layout screens most KV values with a fraction of the bits fetched.
physics.killer_doubt: Real gain ~2-3x, not 8-12x: INT8 with 4 MSB planes plus 10% low-plane refetch moves 55% of bits (1.8x); FP16 ~3x. SpAtten already does this.
physics.decisive_experiment: Software trace study: replay LLM attention over real KV caches with MSB-plane screening; measure bits fetched per token at iso-accuracy. About a GPU-week.
physics.prior_art: SpAtten (HPCA 2021) progressive quantization fetches MSBs first and LSBs on demand; bit-serial accelerators (Stripes, Bit-Pragmatic). From memory.

innovation.key_insight: A bit-plane layout makes precision a fetch knob: score keys from the top planes, then fetch low planes only for top-k tokens, with no new silicon.
innovation.killer_doubt: Realistic KV saving is ~3-4x, not 8-12x. Every key still needs its 4 MSB planes (25-50% of K bits), and diffuse attention heads push top-k past 10%.
innovation.decisive_experiment: GPU prototype at 32-128k context: bit-plane KV layout, MSB scoring and top-k fetch. Measure bytes moved and RULER/LongBench accuracy against Quest and SparQ baselines. ~$50k compute.
innovation.prior_art: Phase B N-70 (MSB-plane sketch top-k); Quest, SparQ and Double Sparsity approximate-score KV fetch; Any-Precision LLM bit-plane weights.

title: Swap fixed GC heap sizing for cluster memory-price-driven heaps
idea: Substitute DRAM headroom with CPU cycles when DRAM is dear. The scheduler publishes a live per-GB memory price, and the JVM, Go, .NET and V8 runtimes read it to retune their heap targets: they collect more often and return pages when memory is expensive and grow when it is cheap. Unchanged hardware.

physics.key_insight: At 4x DRAM prices, GC CPU is cheaper than idle heap headroom. A cross-runtime live price signal turns existing heap knobs into a fleet-wide market-clearing control.
physics.killer_doubt: GC CPU scales as live/(heap-live), so cutting headroom from 2.0x to 1.5x live doubles GC load (5-10% CPU becomes 10-20%). Freed GB count only if the scheduler repacks them.
physics.decisive_experiment: On a ~200-node Kubernetes testbed running JVM and Go services (DeathStarBench, Renaissance), have an agent drive SoftMaxHeapSize/GOMEMLIMIT from a price signal. Measure reclaimed GB that become extra scheduled pods, against CPU and p99. ~$150k.
physics.prior_art: Go GOMEMLIMIT, JVM SoftMaxHeapSize and the OpenJDK ZGC automatic-heap-sizing proposal, .NET DATAS adaptive heaps. A cross-runtime price signal was not found.

innovation.key_insight: GC headroom (1.5-3x live set) is DRAM bought to save CPU; one cluster-published memory-time exchange rate lets every runtime re-trade it as DRAM prices swing.
innovation.killer_doubt: MemBalancer's square-root rule cut memory ~16% at equal GC time (via search snippet); fleet gain is managed-heap share x ~16-30%, likely ~5-10% of server DRAM, with knobs already shipped.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Kubernetes pilot on ~200 JVM and Go services: map a published $/GB-hour to MemBalancer's constant via SoftMaxHeapSize/GOMEMLIMIT; compare RSS and CPU against static settings for 4 weeks, and measure fleet managed-heap share. ~$100k.
innovation.prior_art: Alonso & Appel 1990 heap 'advice server'; MemBalancer (OOPSLA'22) single tradeoff constant across heaps; US 9471225/9836394 multi-GC memory optimisation (via search snippet); Meta TMO.

title: Plated-pillar memory: circumferential magnetization lining 3D NAND-style holes
idea: Revive Univac/Bell plated-wire memory vertically: etch high-AR holes through a stack of word-strap tiers, ALD a soft magnetic shell, spacer and reference layer down each hole, and store bits as circumferentially magnetized ring segments under each strap, sensed non-destructively by the magnetoresistance of an axial read current. Closed-flux rings have no stray field, so hole pitch can be tight.

physics.key_insight: Heavy-metal core gives circumferential spin-Hall polarisation (z x r = phi), collinear with ring bits: field-free SOT writes, unlimited endurance. Workaround read: radial TMR to the word plane.
physics.killer_doubt: A 125x50x5 nm ring segment (3e-23 m3) needs Hk >=~160 Oe for 50 kT; axial read sees ~0.4 ohm GMR per bit on a ~1 kohm string: microvolt signals.
physics.decisive_experiment: Plate or ALD CoFeB/Cu/CoFe shells in AAO pores around W cores (~$200k): measure circumferential switching current, Hk and thermal stability versus thickness, and axial versus radial MR per segment.
physics.prior_art: Plated-wire memory (UNIVAC, 1960s); Parkin racetrack; cylindrical nanotube domain walls; Phase B N-82; sibling I-08865 dropped on its AMR read.

innovation.key_insight: Closed-flux circumferential rings have no stray field and read non-destructively. A magnetic write sidesteps the charge-fluence endurance wall, one of triage's four safe write routes.
innovation.killer_doubt: A 2% MR segment on a ~1.5 kohm pillar gives ~24 uV at 50 uA, below ~50 uV Johnson noise at 100 MHz. Oersted writes need ~5-10 mA.
innovation.decisive_experiment: ALD a NiFe/Cu/CoFe shell into 40 nm holes through a 4-strap stack. Measure per-segment delta-R and the half-select write margin (~$200k). Stop if delta-R is under 1 ohm per segment.
innovation.prior_art: UNIVAC/Bell plated-wire memory (1960s); IBM racetrack (Parkin); Phase B N-82 racetrack-in-hole; I-08865 (another batch) dropped an inductive variant (training knowledge).

title: Oxygen: porous-silicon oxidation carves many SOI tiers from one epi stack
idea: Grow an epi stack alternating p+ (~1e19) and lightly doped Si, open slits, anodize in HF so only the p+ layers become mesoporous, then oxidize them at ~850 C into buried oxide (FIPOS); the lightly doped layers remain single-crystal device tiers.

physics.key_insight: At ~55% porosity, oxidised porous Si fills its own volume (no net expansion), and B at 1e19 adds only ~5e-5 lattice strain: tier count escapes the SiGe strain limit.
physics.killer_doubt: Mesopores in p+ Si are ~10-20 nm, comparable to 20-30 nm sacrificial layers; boron-rich oxide dopes 30 nm device layers (sqrt(Dt) ~9 nm per hour at 850 C).
physics.decisive_experiment: Epi 8-16 Si/Si:B bilayers at 30-60 nm (~$150k, university epi plus anodisation): lateral porosification reach and selectivity from slits, post-oxidation SIMS boron profiles, device-layer mobility.
physics.prior_art: FIPOS (Imai, NTT, 1981) and Canon ELTRAN porous-Si SOI; Phase B N-45 Si/Si:B superlattice; imec and Samsung Si/SiGe 3D DRAM stacks.

innovation.key_insight: Doping-selective porosification turns a low-strain Si/Si:B epi stack into many single-crystal tiers. Boron at 1e19 strains ~150x less than Si0.8Ge0.2, so tier count escapes the SiGe relaxation limit.
innovation.killer_doubt: Holes injected from deeper p+ layers destroy selectivity (a 1990s patent anodizes top-first), and n- tiers block current at reverse junctions. No data beyond a few levels; 50-100 needed.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Buy a 20-period p+ (1e19) / lightly doped RPCVD epi stack (~$30k). Etch slits and anodize laterally at several current densities. Use TEM/EBSD on every tier for selectivity, pore-front uniformity and crystal survival (~$150k).
innovation.prior_art: US5023200 multi-level porous-Si buried insulators; NTT FIPOS (1980s); Canon ELTRAN; imec/Samsung Si/SiGe stacks; no 3D DRAM use found (via search snippet).

title: Diversified-portfolio DIMMs mixing vendors inside each codeword
idea: Portfolio theory cuts risk by holding uncorrelated assets. Build ECC modules in which the chips of each codeword come from 2-3 vendors or process lots. Systematic weaknesses (TRR bypass patterns, temperature-dependent retention) then stay uncorrelated, and chipkill absorbs one vendor's failure mode. Module design, qualification and a pilot run fit in $1M.

physics.key_insight: Works as a one-chip-per-codeword onramp: put at most one unproven second-source chip (e.g. from a U.S. entrant) in each chipkill codeword, so its systematic flaws are always correctable.
physics.killer_doubt: As written it fails. Every chip sees the same ACT, so a vendor-systematic flaw hits 3-5 chips of a 10-chip DDR5 x4 codeword. Chipkill corrects one.
physics.decisive_experiment: Build 20 RDIMMs with 9 incumbent chips plus 1 'risky' chip per subchannel. Run TRRespass-style hammer and 2 s retention stress, and show zero UEs against single-vendor controls. ~$200k.
physics.prior_art: Chipkill/SDDC (IBM, AMD); vendor/lot mixing in RAID disk arrays. Vendor-mixed DIMM codewords: none found.

innovation.key_insight: Decorrelating vendor-systematic failure modes across a codeword's chips is the right instinct for qualifying new second-source and U.S. dies.
innovation.killer_doubt: All chips in a rank get identical commands; a vendor-specific TRR bypass hits that vendor's 3-5 chips of a 10-chip codeword at once, beyond chipkill's 1-chip correction.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Build mixed-vendor DDR5 RDIMMs; run TRRespass/U-TRR patterns on an FPGA tester and count codewords with >1 failing chip versus single-vendor modules. ~$150k.
innovation.prior_art: Chipkill (IBM, 1997); vendor-specific TRR bypass patterns (TRRespass 2020, U-TRR 2021); field studies showing vendor-correlated faults.

title: Partial-charge sip read makes DRAM sensing non-destructive
idea: A tightly controlled subthreshold wordline pulse lets only ~3% of the cell charge (~450 e-) leak into a 0.2 fF local sense node; kT/C charge noise there is ~6 e-, so 450 e- is a >20 sigma signal (~0.36 V). The cell keeps 97% of its charge, so nothing is restored and only the addressed 64 B is sensed; normal refresh tops cells up.

physics.key_insight: Self-limited charge sharing onto a ~0.2 fF node takes only Cn/(Cs+Cn)~4% of the charge but gives a ~0.48 V swing: near-non-destructive 64 B reads with no restore.
physics.killer_doubt: Subthreshold sip: sigma Vt ~40-50 mV at ~90 mV/dec gives ~50x charge spread. The self-limited fix needs a local amplifier every ~3-8 cells. WL toggling still hammers.
physics.decisive_experiment: 65-28 nm MPW: 5 fF MIM 1T1C cells on 0.2-1 fF local nodes with source-follower readout. Measure swing, charge loss per read, reads before restore and spread over 10k cells at 25-85 C. ~$400k.
physics.prior_art: Hierarchical and local-bitline sensing; selective bitline activation (Udipi, ISCA 2010); gain cells (inherently non-destructive); Phase B N-40 MSB-DRAM.

innovation.key_insight: A 0.2 fF local node gets a >20 sigma signal from ~3% of the cell charge, so 64 B could be read without restoring a whole 8 KB row.
