title: Logic-die decoupling capacitors double as on-demand scratch memory
idea: Invert 'storage elements must be dedicated memory cells' -> reuse the capacitors already on every logic die. An accelerator's deep-trench/MIM decap is split into ~50 fF segments with access switches, so idle decap banks act as eDRAM-like scratch when the supply-noise budget allows and revert to decoupling during load surges.

physics.key_insight: Accelerators carry tens of uF of on-die and interposer capacitance; seeing it as idle charge storage is clever framing.
physics.killer_doubt: A cap holding data cannot decouple: droops arrive in ns, evicting 150 MB takes ms. 50 fF cells plus a transistor each give only SRAM-class density.
physics.decisive_experiment: GPU power-trace study: fraction of time half the decap can be removed with droop under 20 mV, versus scratch demand at those moments; drop if anti-correlated. ~$50k.
physics.prior_art: IBM deep-trench eDRAM and trench decaps share one module (POWER7-9); Intel Crystalwell MIM eDRAM; TSMC eDTC capacitors in CoWoS interposers.

innovation.key_insight: Logic dies carry large, mostly idle capacitance. Making it addressable reuses area already paid for, a new framing of eDRAM.
innovation.killer_doubt: Decap is needed most during compute bursts, when scratch is busy. At on-die MIM density (~20-50 fF/um2), a 50 fF bit takes ~1 um2, ~50x an N3 SRAM cell.
innovation.decisive_experiment: PDN simulation (~$50k) of an accelerator under real di/dt traces, with 30% of decap switched out and switch ESR added. Kill if droop exceeds budget at any useful scratch size.
innovation.prior_art: IBM deep-trench eDRAM (POWER7-POWER9); Intel Crystalwell 128 MB MIM-cap eDRAM (22 nm); no dual-use decap memory found [training knowledge].

title: Multilayer optical-disc focus addressing via threshold-coded tiers
idea: Like BD-XL picking a layer by focus depth, give each of 32 storage tiers on one shared vertical wordline a distinct access threshold set by deposited channel thickness; address tier k by stepping wordline voltage and differencing successive bitline reads, and write each column in descending-threshold order.

physics.key_insight: Selecting tiers by voltage instead of wiring would delete staircases and select lines; it works for ~4 tiers spaced ~0.5 V (5-7 decades apart), not 32.
physics.killer_doubt: 32 levels in ~3 V sit ~90 mV apart; at SS 70 mV/dec adjacent tiers differ ~1.3 decades, so tier k+1 leaks during reads; any write rewrites all lower tiers.
physics.decisive_experiment: 4-8 stacked IGZO TFTs on one gate with thickness-set Vt at a university fab (~$150k): measure per-tier Vt sigma and differential-read error versus level spacing at 85 C.
physics.prior_art: NAND multi-level reads step wordline voltage to sort Vt levels; Vt-coded tier selection for 3D DRAM: none found.

innovation.key_insight: Voltage-coded tier selection would delete staircases and select lines. It is viable for ~4 tiers at ~0.5 V spacing; the CCD family already avoids staircases by phase-tying tiers.
innovation.killer_doubt: 32 Vt levels in ~3 V sit ~94 mV apart: 4-sigma separation needs sigma-Vt <=12 mV, under the study's 20 mV oxide drift budget. Every write rewrites the column.
innovation.decisive_experiment: 4-8 stacked IGZO TFTs on one gate with thickness-set Vt at a university fab (~$150k): per-tier Vt sigma and drift after 85 C bias stress; kill if sigma exceeds 25 mV.
innovation.prior_art: Macronix 3D vertical-gate NAND layer selection by Vt-programmed select gates (~2010) [training knowledge]; NAND wordline-stepped multi-level reads. Vt-coded 3D DRAM tiers: none found.

title: Kovio's liquid-silicon ink printed into 32 cheap gain-cell tiers
idea: Kovio printed silicon RFID from liquid cyclopentasilane and folded in 2014 on a tiny market and hard-to-handle pyrophoric ink. Inside a sealed inert coater module, spin 20 nm silicon films from ink, crystallize only the top film with a nanosecond laser, and stack 32 tiers of poly-Si 2T gain cells, each tier patterned by one imprint.

physics.key_insight: Spin-on cyclopentasilane plus nanosecond laser crystallization makes a silicon tier from one coat and one scan, with no epitaxy or layer transfer.
physics.killer_doubt: Laser poly-Si write FETs leak ~1e-13 to 1e-12 A: a 0.5 fF node with 0.2 V margin holds 0.1-1 ms, less in 85 C tails. IGZO leaks <1e-18 A/um.
physics.decisive_experiment: Spin CPS films in a glovebox coater, laser-crystallize them and build 2T gain cells on two tiers. Map the 85 C Ioff tail and the lower-tier TFT shift after the upper-tier laser. ~$400k.
physics.prior_art: Kovio printed-Si RFID (to 2014); Shimoda et al. solution-processed silicon TFTs (Nature 2006); CEA-Leti laser-annealed sequential 3D (prior knowledge).

innovation.key_insight: Spin-on cyclopentasilane plus ns-laser crystallization makes a ~$5-10/wafer silicon tier with no epitaxy or layer transfer. It is a genuinely cheap semiconductor tier.
innovation.killer_doubt: Laser-crystallized poly-Si TFTs leak ~1e-13 A/um, so a 1 fF gain-cell node lasts ~1-10 ms. IGZO leaks aA-level at equally low temperature. Laser heat damages the tiers below.
innovation.decisive_experiment: In a glovebox, spin cyclopentasilane and ELA-crystallize 20 nm films, then build 2T gain cells. Measure off-current and 85 C retention, plus damage to underlying tiers after stacking 3. ~$250k.
innovation.prior_art: Kovio printed-Si RFID (closed 2014); Shimoda et al., Nature 2006 (Seiko Epson/JSR) solution-processed Si TFTs; Phase B N-37/N-38 oxide tiers [training knowledge].

title: Charge-injection-device cells: two-gate X-Y charge storage with non-destructive reads
idea: Failure mined: GE's charge-injection device (CID) imager lost to CCDs, yet it had an X-Y addressed, transistor-free pixel of two coupled MOS gates, read non-destructively by moving charge between the gates and sensing the column. Fix: use CID pairs as memory cells, with the row gate and column gate overlapping one storage well. A write injects charge; a read shifts it under the column gate and back, so the charge never leaves the well and can be re-read for multi-level sensing.

physics.key_insight: Small wells make dark charge minor: 1,600 nm2 at 1 nA/cm2 gives ~0.1 e/s. CID column reads move charge without destroying it.
physics.killer_doubt: A 40x40 nm MOS well holds ~230 e: ~1 mV on a 35 fF column versus ~20 e read noise. 3 bits needs ~100x averaging; writing needs an injecting junction.
physics.decisive_experiment: University-fab 32x32 CID array at 0.5-1 um with TCAD scaling. Measure electrical (non-optical) write selectivity, half-select disturb and correlated-double-sampled column SNR. ~$150k.
physics.prior_art: GE charge-injection-device imagers (Michon and Burke, 1970s); 1970s planar MOS-capacitor DRAM cells; CCD memories.

innovation.key_insight: Shifting charge between two coupled MOS gates and back reads a well non-destructively, allowing averaged multi-sample sensing with no restore and X-Y select without a per-cell transistor.
innovation.killer_doubt: A 4F2 surface well (F=20 nm) holds ~110 e-: ~0.2 mV on a 100 fF column; 85 C surface generation fills it in under 0.5 s; writes need a diffusion.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Build CID gate-pair arrays with 16-cell column segments on a 180 nm CIS shuttle; measure controlled-injection write accuracy, column signal and dark fill time at 85 C. ~$150k.
innovation.prior_art: GE CID imagers (1970s); Fossum QIS jots; 1970s CCD memories [training knowledge]; no CID-as-RAM found.

title: Snapback counting reads N stacked threshold cells per crosspoint
idea: Failure mined: Optane died partly because each extra deck needed its own lithography and decoders, so cost never scaled past two decks. Fix: deposit 8 chalcogenide threshold-switching memory layers in series at every crosspoint, pattern them with one etch, and engineer a different threshold window for each layer. One voltage ramp per pillar is read by counting and timing the snapback current spikes, whose pattern encodes all 8 states.

physics.key_insight: One etch and one decoder set shared by N layers is the right answer to Optane's per-deck mask cost, if layers could be addressed independently.
physics.killer_doubt: Series layers cascade: one snapback (~1 V drop) overdrives the rest, so they fire together. Eight windows need ~16-24 V ramps; per-layer writes cannot be isolated; OTS endurance ~1e8-1e11.
physics.decisive_experiment: Two- and three-layer OTS series stacks on 100 nm crosspoints (university fab, ~$200k): test whether snapbacks resolve as separate current spikes, window overlap over 1,000 devices, and per-layer write selectivity.
physics.prior_art: Intel/Micron 3D XPoint (two decks, per-deck masks); selector-only / self-selecting chalcogenide memory work at Micron and SK hynix.

innovation.key_insight: One etch and one decoder serving N stacked memory layers per crosspoint attacks the masks-per-deck cost that kept Optane from scaling.
innovation.killer_doubt: With one current through all 8 series layers, layer k cannot be written alone. GeSe OTS loses nonlinearity near 1e6 cycles, versus ~1e13 for DRAM (via search snippet).
innovation.decisive_experiment: On a university line, deposit a 2-layer OTS/self-selecting stack with distinct thresholds. Test whether either layer programs alone, measure Vth sigma against window spacing, and read disturb over 1e6 ramp reads. ~$250k.
innovation.prior_art: Intel/Micron 3D XPoint; Micron and SK hynix self-selecting / selector-only chalcogenide memory; multi-level PCM [training knowledge]. No stacked multi-window OTS found.

title: Crested-barrier capacitor: the capacitor is its own access switch
idea: Inverts 'storage and switch are separate devices': each crossbar node is a floating metal nanolayer between two crested tunnel barriers (e.g., nitride/AlN/nitride trilayers) whose peak collapses at high field, giving ~10^12 current change between the ~3 V write and ~1 V hold; charge on the floating layer is the bit, written in ns by tunneling and read capacitively, from one blanket deposition per deck.

physics.key_insight: Crested barriers do raise the write/hold current ratio enough on paper (~1e10-1e12 between 3 V and 1 V) for a transistor-free floating-node cell.
physics.killer_doubt: A 20x20 nm floating node holds ~0.005 fF, ~30 e- at 1 V; on a 100 fF crossbar line that is ~50 uV signal under ~200 uV kTC noise.
physics.decisive_experiment: Epitaxial nitride/AlN crested-trilayer coupons: J-V ratio at 3 V vs 1 V and charge-to-breakdown under ns pulses; if >1e8 C/cm2 survives, re-scope as gated floating-node cell (N-10/N-85).
physics.prior_art: Likharev crested/layered tunnel barriers for fast nonvolatile memory (APL ~1998); our N-85 crystalline crested-barrier 1S1C crosspoint.

innovation.key_insight: Field-collapsing crested barriers give large write/hold current contrast with no transistor. It is worth it only as a selector with a real capacitor (N-85), not as the storage node.
innovation.killer_doubt: A 20 nm floating node is ~6 aF (~40 e-), under the ~82 e- kTC noise of a 35 fF line. 1e12 tunnelling writes break the charge-fluence rule (1e2-1e5 cycles).
innovation.decisive_experiment: Fabricate a 1 um2 TiN/AlN/TiN crested-barrier floating node read by an integrated FET. Measure the 3 V/1 V current ratio, 85 C retention and cycles to failure. Under $150k.
innovation.prior_art: Likharev crested barriers (APL 1998); imec/Govoreanu VARIOT barrier-engineered flash; nanocrystal floating-gate memories; Phase B N-85 crystalline crested-barrier 1S1C.

title: Image-sensor 4T pixel gain cell reads 1,000-electron packets
idea: Box: buried-channel storage well (~1-2k e-) x transfer gate + floating-diffusion source follower borrowed from 4T image pixels x correlated-double-sampling column sensing x planar CMOS x Si x CIS fab flow. Full charge transfer onto a tiny floating diffusion gives ~100 uV/e- gain, so a small well replaces the 5 fF capacitor and is written back after read.

physics.key_insight: Full transfer onto a ~1.6 fF floating diffusion plus CDS reads ~1,000-electron packets cleanly; writes go through a transistor channel, so endurance is unlimited.
physics.killer_doubt: Duplicate of I-00973. Planar pinned well holds ~6,000 e-/um2: 1,000 e- plus 3-4T is ~0.2 um2, ~50-90x a 1-beta bit; 85 C hot-pixel tails give ~10 ms.
physics.decisive_experiment: None separate: settled by the I-00973 CIS-MPW test chip (fill-and-spill electrical write, 25 ns CDS read, dark-current tails at 25-85 C).
physics.prior_art: Global-shutter CIS pinned in-pixel storage nodes; Fossum/Ma pump-gate jots; our Phase B N-84 Jot-RAM; 1970s CCD memories.

innovation.key_insight: Floating-diffusion gain (~100 uV/e-) plus CDS reads ~1k-electron packets reliably. The transferable part is FD/CDS sensing for CCD strings and gain cells, not the pixel as a cell.
innovation.killer_doubt: The smallest shared CIS pixels are ~0.56 um pitch (~0.3 um2/bit) against DRAM's ~0.0017 um2: ~180x less dense. A 3 nm 6T SRAM bit (~0.021 um2) is 15x denser.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Free paper check: lay out a 2x2-shared 4T cell in a 65 nm CIS PDK and stop if it exceeds 0.05 um2/bit. Only then one CIS MPW (~$150k) measuring fill-and-spill write noise and 85 C dark charge.
innovation.prior_art: Near-duplicate of I-00973. Global-shutter CIS in-pixel pinned storage diodes (Sony, onsemi); Fossum pinned-photodiode/QIS jots; Phase B N-84 Jot-RAM (training knowledge).

title: Coaxial gallium-oxide 2T0C cell grown inside one vertical hole
idea: TRIZ #7 Nesting: in a 3D-NAND-like stack of word planes, one DUV-printed hole receives nested ALD shells at each tier recess - an outer amorphous Ga2O3 write channel gated by the plane, a metal storage-node ring, a thin dielectric, and an inner Ga2O3 read channel gated by that ring.

physics.key_insight: Same coaxial in-hole 2T0C as I-10833. A wider-gap channel could cut off-current further, but only if contacts and mobility allow it.
physics.killer_doubt: Even 1e-21 A on a 0.2 fF node with a 0.3 V margin gives ~17 h, not years. Amorphous ALD Ga2O3 is near-insulating (<1 cm2/Vs), with high contact resistance.
physics.decisive_experiment: Fold into I-10833: make planar ALD a-Ga2O3 and IGZO 2T0C cells on one wafer. Compare Ion at 1 V overdrive, contact resistance and 85 C retention. ~$150k.
physics.prior_art: IGZO already shows Ioff <1 aA (Kioxia OCTRAM) and >30,000 s (SJTU IGO 2T0C); Ga2O3 devices are mostly crystalline power FETs (prior knowledge).

innovation.key_insight: Wide-gap channels push off-current toward retention of hours. The coaxial in-hole geometry duplicates I-03474, so only the Ga2O3 channel choice is new.
innovation.killer_doubt: Oxide 2T0C already reaches >1,000 s (~30,000 s passivated), limited by traps and gate leakage, not bandgap; amorphous ALD Ga2O3 mobility is likely <1 cm2/Vs, slowing writes.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Fabricate planar ALD amorphous Ga2O3 and IGZO TFTs side by side at <=400 C; compare mobility, the Ioff floor via 2T0C retention at 85 C, and PBTI. University fab, ~$150k.
innovation.prior_art: Coaxial family: NEO 3D X-DRAM IGZO 3T0C (TCAD; via search snippet), IMECAS vertical CAA 2T0C, Phase B N-43; university Ga2O3 TFT research.

title: DRAM as lossy mirror of flash: refetch instead of protect
idea: Reverse which copy is authoritative: for clean (read-mostly) pages such as model weights and file cache, a cheap checksum detects errors on reject-grade 1%-BER dies and the line is refetched from the SSD copy.

physics.key_insight: Clean pages have an authoritative flash copy, so DRAM needs only detection, not correction: a CRC plus refetch turns uncorrectable errors into latency instead of data loss.
physics.killer_doubt: At 1% BER only 0.99^512 = 0.6% of 64 B lines read clean, so nearly every access pays a ~50 us SSD refetch. With SECDED it works only below ~3e-4.
physics.decisive_experiment: Fold into I-05038/I-01312: bitmap 200 reject-bin dies at 85 C, classify random versus clustered faults, then replay weight and page-cache traces with SECDED plus CRC-refetch to measure mean and p99 added latency against raw BER.
physics.prior_art: Linux hwpoison already drops and re-reads clean page-cache pages on uncorrectable errors (2009); Micron SpecTek off-spec bins; EDEN approximate DRAM (MICRO 2019). From memory.

innovation.key_insight: Clean pages have an authoritative copy elsewhere, so detect-and-refetch can replace correction; Linux already drops poisoned clean page-cache pages and rereads them.
innovation.killer_doubt: At 1% BER a 64-byte line is clean with probability 0.99^512 = 0.6%, so nearly every access refetches from SSD (~50-100 us). Works only below ~1e-7 BER.
innovation.decisive_experiment: DRAM-Bender characterization of ~100 reject or downbinned DDR4/DDR5 dies: are failures clustered (map-out-able rows/columns) or diffuse, and what share of wafer starts they are; plus a refetch-latency model. ~$80k.
innovation.prior_art: Heterogeneous-Reliability Memory (Luo et al., DSN 2014: parity plus recovery of clean pages from storage); Linux hwpoison clean-page handling; downbinned DRAM resale.

title: Vertical CCD charge-shift columns with one floating-diffusion sense node
idea: Box: potential-well storage in poly-Si/IGZO channel x CCD transfer gates x floating-diffusion source follower x 3D vertical stack x Si x CMOS image-sensor fab. Bits are charge packets that shift up one tier per clock to a single sense node at the top, like an image sensor's vertical register, so tiers need no individual wordline decoders or staircase contacts.

physics.key_insight: Floating-diffusion readout gives ~0.3 mV per electron at ~0.5 fF, so ~500-1,000 e- packets suffice and per-tier decoders and staircases disappear.
physics.killer_doubt: imec IGZO CCDs clock at ~4-6 MHz: a 64-tier shift takes ~10-16 us, ~100x the claimed 100 ns. Poly-Si grain-boundary dark charge (~100 fA) fills 1,000 e- in ~2 ms.
physics.decisive_experiment: Fold into the I-01064 test chip: planar then 8-tier IGZO CCD with a floating-diffusion output; measure per-transfer CTE versus clock (4-200 MHz), conversion gain and 85 C dark charge. ~$300k.
physics.prior_art: imec IGZO CCD buffer memory (IEDM 2024 planar; IMW 2026 vertical 3D, via search snippet); CIS vertical CCD registers; Phase B N-08; I-01064.

innovation.key_insight: Charge packets shifting up the tiers to one floating-diffusion node remove per-tier decoders and staircase contacts, which are the line-end cost of 3D arrays.
innovation.killer_doubt: It duplicates imec's IGZO 3D CCD. CIS fabs lack 3D-NAND tier stacks, and a poly-Si channel has ~1e3-1e5x c-Si dark current, giving ms-class retention at 85 C (estimate).
innovation.decisive_experiment: No separate experiment; fold into I-10793. If pursued, compare poly-Si with IGZO 8-tier vertical CCD strings at 85 C, measuring dark generation and per-transfer CTE. ~$300k.
innovation.prior_art: imec IGZO CCD buffer memory: planar at IEDM 2024, 3D at IMW 2026 (via search snippet, prior logs); 1970s CCD memories; study N-08.

title: Soviet-style socialist competition: bounties for memory-footprint patches
idea: Like a five-year-plan competition, but paid. A $600k bounty pool pays per verified GB saved on standard benchmarks of the 50 most-deployed open-source infrastructure packages (Postgres, Redis, Kafka, Elasticsearch, PyTorch DataLoader, Chromium). A $400k CI harness measures peak and steady RSS before and after each merged patch.

physics.key_insight: The software multiplier is real: a byte saved in Redis or Chromium is saved on millions of machines, and a CI harness measuring RSS is cheap and objective.
physics.killer_doubt: Fleets provision DRAM by VM shape and configured buffer pools, not RSS, so a 10% benchmark cut frees ~0% until operators resize. Meta's TMO offload already saves ~20-32% (from memory).
physics.decisive_experiment: Before funding bounties, merge 3 known memory-saving patches in each of 5 packages. At 2 partner operators, track over 6 months whether instance sizing or GB purchased changes (<$100k).
physics.prior_art: Google Patch Rewards; Sovereign Tech Fund; Valkey 8 per-key overhead cuts; Meta TMO and Google zswap far memory. From memory.

innovation.key_insight: A CI harness that measures RSS before and after each patch to widely deployed infrastructure would make memory savings a measured quantity rather than a claimed one.
innovation.killer_doubt: Postgres, Redis and Kafka RSS is mostly operator-sized buffers and data (shared_buffers, maxmemory, page cache), not code overhead. Patchable slack is likely <5%, and benchmark-specific patches can game the bounty.
innovation.decisive_experiment: For 10 of the packages at default and production configs, split RSS into configured buffers or data versus allocator, metadata and fragmentation overhead. If overhead is <5%, drop. About $30k.
innovation.prior_art: Chrome PartitionAlloc and Memory Saver work, Gitcoin and bug-bounty funds; same family as R27 I-02295 (DROP) [training knowledge].

title: Millefiori glass-cane draw sliced into litho-free vertical access arrays
idea: Assemble a cm-scale preform holding ~10^4 coaxial access-transistor cross-sections (chalcogenide-glass semiconductor core, glass gate dielectric, low-melting metal gate). Thermally draw it 10^4x as Venetian millefiori cane or optical fiber is drawn, then slice 100 nm discs: each slice is a ready-made array of vertical gate-all-around access switches.

physics.key_insight: A 1e4x thermal draw shrinks a cm preform of coaxial gate stacks to nm pitch in one step; slicing makes vertical GAA arrays with no patterning tool.
physics.killer_doubt: Coaxial cylinders break up by Plateau-Rayleigh below ~100 nm (tau ~ eta*r/gamma ~0.1 s at r=10 nm); a 3 nm dielectric must hold ±0.3 nm over km.
physics.decisive_experiment: Two-stage draw of a 7-element coaxial As2Se3/glass/Sn preform to <=50 nm cores (~$200k); microtome 100 nm slices and probe gated I-V. Kill if gate continuity <99% or Ion/Ioff <1e6.
physics.prior_art: Fink lab in-fiber devices and capillary breakup; Yaman et al. iterative draw of ~15 nm chalcogenide nanowires; no sliced transistor arrays found.

innovation.key_insight: Stack-and-draw copies one preform cross-section into thousands of identical vertical devices per slice with no scanner. A litho-free transistor faceplate is a fresh, capital-light concept.
innovation.killer_doubt: Thin co-drawn layers break up by capillary instability; the best uniform drawn features are ~40 nm. A GAA access array needs ~3-5 nm dielectric at <=30 nm pitch.
innovation.decisive_experiment: In a Fink/Sorin-class draw tower (<$300k), co-draw a Ge- or Se-core, glass-clad, metal-gate coaxial preform. Measure dielectric continuity against thickness after 1e3-1e4x reduction, and Ion/Ioff of microtomed slices.
innovation.prior_art: Fink (MIT) 2010 in-fibre chalcogenide FET; EPFL ultimate drawn feature sizes, uniform down to ~40 nm (via search snippet); NRL nanochannel-glass stack-and-draw arrays.

title: Cookie-cutter procedural data regenerated from seeds instead of stored
idea: Like stamping cookies from a cutter instead of storing them, replace stored tensors that are pseudo-random or structured (random projections, initializations, LoRA bases, positional tables, dropout masks) with seeds plus near-memory generators. These recreate each line at access time.

physics.key_insight: Never storing regenerable data is the cheapest memory: a seeded generator near memory trades a few pJ of compute for capacity and bandwidth.
physics.killer_doubt: Seed-regenerable tensors are <1% of AI memory; trained weights and KV are not. FlashAttention already regenerates dropout masks; VeRA and NOLA already seed LoRA bases.
physics.decisive_experiment: Audit peak memory of five production training and inference jobs by tensor class (~$20k of compute); kill if seed-regenerable tensors are under 2% of peak bytes.
physics.prior_art: FlashAttention dropout regeneration from Philox state; VeRA, NOLA and PRANC seeded random bases; RoPE computed on the fly.

innovation.key_insight: Anything pseudo-random need not be stored or refreshed. Dropout masks and random projection bases are already regenerated from RNG state today.
innovation.killer_doubt: Trained weights and KV are not seed-generated. Pseudo-random tensors are likely <1% of accelerator memory, and N-76 shows rate-distortion caps seed-coded weights at ~1.07-1.22x.
innovation.decisive_experiment: An audit is enough: count the bytes of seed-regenerable tensors in Llama-class training and serving memory snapshots (<$20k). Expect <1%.
innovation.prior_art: FlashAttention regenerates dropout masks from saved RNG state; PRANC, NOLA, VeRA seed-generated bases; RoPE computed on the fly; Phase B N-76 (training knowledge).

title: Long-channel thick-oxide gain cell in open-source 130 nm
idea: MAGNIFY channel length ~10x and oxide thickness ~3x on the write device: a 3T gain cell in the open SKY130/GF180 PDKs uses the 5 V thick-oxide transistor as write switch (aA subthreshold leakage) and stores on the read transistor's gate; free or cheap shuttles allow monthly iterations.

physics.key_insight: A thick-oxide write device with negative hold bias reaches ~10 aA, giving ~1-10 s retention in U.S.-fabbed open PDKs: useful for chiplet test vehicles.
physics.killer_doubt: A 3T thick-oxide cell is ~3-5 um2/bit (~0.25 Mb/mm2), about 1,500x below 1-beta DRAM; junction leakage rises ~100x at 85 C, cutting retention to ~0.1 s.
physics.decisive_experiment: One GF180 or SKY130 shuttle: 64 kb 3T arrays, retention distribution at 25 and 85 C; a weeks-scale result, not a moonshot. ~$20k.
physics.prior_art: Intel 1103 three-transistor DRAM (1970); Bar-Ilan and EPFL long-retention gain-cell eDRAM in 180-65 nm; open-PDK gain-cell projects on SKY130.

innovation.key_insight: Thick-oxide long-channel write devices in open PDKs give seconds of retention in a U.S.-fabbed node at near-zero capital. It is a good teaching and test vehicle.
innovation.killer_doubt: A 5 V 3T cell in 130 nm is ~5-10 um2, ~10,000x DRAM's 864 nm2. Retention drops ~10-30x at 85 C, so it does not move DRAM supply.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Not needed as an invention. Include it as reference cells on the I-01420 shuttle (~$10-20k) to calibrate the retention-tail BIST.
innovation.prior_art: Si gain-cell eDRAM (Teman/Giterman, Bar-Ilan; Meinerzhagen/Burg, EPFL); OpenRAM on SKY130 (Guthaus, UCSC) [training knowledge].

title: Sell retention-fallout dies as permanent fast-refresh DDR5 SKUs
idea: Forced limit (DDR/HBM interface unchanged): standard controllers only. Dies that miss 64 ms retention because of a weak-cell tail are fused to always report the hot-temperature refresh-rate code (2x or 4x refresh) in the existing MR4 register, so stock controllers refresh them faster, and they sell at a discount into capacity-hungry, bandwidth-tolerant tiers such as CXL expanders and inference KV-cache.

physics.key_insight: MR4 refresh-rate reporting lets stock DDR5 controllers run a weak-retention die at 2x or 4x refresh with no host changes.
physics.killer_doubt: Post-repair, post-on-die-ECC retention fallout is ~1-3% of dies; at 32 Gb 4x refresh costs ~42% bandwidth (tRFC 410 ns, tREFI 0.98 us). Downgrade bins already sell.
physics.decisive_experiment: Partner with a module house holding downgrade dies: retention-map 1,000 fallout parts at 32 ms and 16 ms windows, 85 C; report the share passing at 2x refresh.
physics.prior_art: Micron SpecTek and other downgrade channels; DDR5 2x refresh above 85 C; review I-07481 (temperature-grade resale) dropped.

innovation.key_insight: A permanent 2x-refresh code in MR4 lets stock controllers absorb weak-tail dies with zero capex, much like B4-03's relaxed-retention HBM bin.
innovation.killer_doubt: After row/column repair and DDR5 on-die ECC, retention-only fallout is likely <1-3% of dies. Makers already sell such dies through temperature grades, downbins and UTT channels in a shortage.
innovation.decisive_experiment: A ~$100k test: buy 1,000 UTT/downbin DDR5 dies and screen their retention at 85 C with 32 and 16 ms refresh. Kill if <50% pass at 2x refresh or if the recoverable volume is <1% of supply.
innovation.prior_art: Industry downbinning, extended-temperature 2x refresh grades and UTT/eTT die sales; RAIDR multi-rate refresh (CMU 2012); triage N-64/B4-03 retention bin [training knowledge].

title: Seed-regenerated tensors replace stored bits with recomputation
idea: Time-shift storage into computation: store a 32-bit PRNG seed plus a few coefficients per weight block, and regenerate weights on the fly in a near-memory generator at read time, so the bit lives as an algorithm.

physics.key_insight: Trading stored bits for recomputed bits is sound where compute is cheap: a PRNG plus a few coefficients regenerates a weight block in a few cycles near memory.
physics.killer_doubt: SeedLM-style seeds reach ~3-4 bits/weight, the same as production 4-bit quantization (GPTQ, MXFP4), so the gain over today's baseline is ~1-1.3x, not 3-8x.
physics.decisive_experiment: Software only (~$20k GPU time): seed fitting versus GPTQ/AWQ at equal bits per weight on Llama-class models; report perplexity at 2-3 bits per weight.
physics.prior_art: SeedLM (Apple, 2024 preprint; PRNG-seed weight compression, training knowledge); GPTQ, AWQ, MXFP4/NVFP4 formats; AQLM vector-quantization codebooks.

innovation.key_insight: Recomputing instead of storing is sound where near-memory compute is cheap: a PRNG seed plus a few coefficients regenerates a weight block in a few cycles.
innovation.killer_doubt: SeedLM-style seeds reach ~3-4 bits/weight, the same as deployed 4-bit formats (GPTQ, MXFP4/NVFP4): ~1-1.3x over today's baseline, not 3-8x.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Software only (~$20k GPU time): seed fitting vs GPTQ/AQLM at 2-3 bits/weight on Llama-class models, reporting perplexity and decode bytes moved.
innovation.prior_art: SeedLM (Apple, 2024 preprint) [training knowledge]; GPTQ, AWQ, AQLM; MXFP4/NVFP4 formats.

title: Prior action: base-die gather engine packs sparse reads before PHY
idea: TRIZ #10 Preliminary action: the HBM base die runs a scatter-gather and transpose engine. The GPU sends index lists (KV-cache page tables, embedding IDs, MoE token routes), and the base die collects 32 B sectors across banks and packs them into dense full-width bursts before they cross the PHY.

physics.key_insight: For sub-32 B random words (graphs, sparse matrices) a base-die gather removes most wasted link bytes, and HBM4 custom logic base dies make it buildable.
physics.killer_doubt: Named workloads are already dense: KV pages 2 KB+, embedding rows 128-512 B, MoE tokens KBs, against 32 B granules; gain under ~10% of AI traffic. Row overfetch untouched.
physics.decisive_experiment: Trace study (~$30k): replay KV-cache, embedding and MoE address traces through a 32 B-sector HBM model and count PHY bytes saved by gather-pack versus controller sector coalescing.
physics.prior_art: Impulse memory controller (Utah, 1999); GS-DRAM (MICRO 2015); RecNMP (ISCA 2020); in-study I-10911 (DROP); HBM4 custom base dies.

innovation.key_insight: HBM4 custom base dies make memory-side gather buildable; worthwhile only for sub-32 B random words (graphs, sparse matrices).
innovation.killer_doubt: The named AI streams are already coarse: KV pages >=2 KB, embedding rows 128-512 B, MoE token blocks KBs vs 32 B sectors. Saving <~10% of HBM traffic (estimate).
innovation.decisive_experiment: Trace replay (~$30k): KV, embedding and MoE address traces through a 32 B-sector HBM model, counting PHY bytes saved versus controller-side coalescing.
innovation.prior_art: Impulse controller (Utah, 1999); GS-DRAM (MICRO 2015); RecNMP (ISCA 2020); Samsung AxDIMM; in-study I-10911 (DROP).

title: Myelin multilamellar self-assembly lays down twenty tiers in one coat
idea: Schwann cells wrap axons in dozens of uniform lamellae; spin a high-chi lamellar block copolymer that orders parallel to the substrate into 20+ layers (~12 nm period), then use sequential infiltration synthesis to turn one block into AlOx insulator and the other into In2O3 channel, creating a whole tier stack in one coat-anneal-infiltrate sequence below 200 C.

physics.key_insight: Self-assembly can set tier pitch without 100 depositions, and SIS turns polymer lamellae into AlOx stacks below 200 C.
physics.killer_doubt: A 12 nm period leaves a 6 nm channel, a 6 nm insulator and no wordline layer. SIS infiltrates only the polar block, so In2O3 cannot form in the other.
physics.decisive_experiment: Coat a 20-period PS-b-PMMA film, infiltrate TMA/water, and check layer continuity and terrace defects over 1 cm2 by TEM. Measure SIS In2O3 mobility in a test TFT. ~$100k.
physics.prior_art: Argonne sequential infiltration synthesis (Darling, Elam); SIS ZnO/In2O3 films; parallel-lamellar BCP multilayers (prior knowledge).

innovation.key_insight: Self-assembled parallel lamellae plus sequential infiltration synthesis could create many insulator/semiconductor tiers in one coat, replacing ~100 depositions with chemistry.
innovation.killer_doubt: A 12 nm period leaves ~6 nm per channel and no room for gate, dielectric and wordline (~30-60 nm per tier); per-layer staircase contacts at 12 nm pitch are unmanufacturable.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Coat a 20-period high-chi lamellar film, infiltrate In2O3 and AlOx, then TEM-check layer continuity and measure Hall mobility of buried infiltrated layers. ~$100k; stop if mobility is below 1 cm2/Vs.
innovation.prior_art: Argonne SIS (Darling, Elam); Brookhaven CFN SIS-derived ZnO transistors; parallel-lamella BCP films. No BCP-defined memory tiers found (training knowledge).

title: Keyword-spotter extreme: ternary weights stored as zero-skipping trit runs
idea: From always-on keyword spotters that run ternary networks: models are trained to {-1, 0, +1} weights stored as base-3 packed trits (5 per byte) with run-length skip lists for zeros, decoded by adder-only compute units that skip zero runs.

physics.key_insight: Zero-skipping saves compute energy on adder-only hardware; for memory, the only question is whether zero runs carry entropy below the 1.585-bit ternary bound.
physics.killer_doubt: At ~40% zeros ternary entropy is 1.57 bits per weight, so run-length coding saves ~2% over five-trit packing; zeros must exceed ~80% (H = 0.92) to matter.
physics.decisive_experiment: Histogram zero fraction and run lengths in BitNet b1.58 2B4T weights, then compute empirical entropy against 1.6 bpw. One day of scripting, <$1k.
physics.prior_art: Same packing as I-06286 (BitNet, TQ1_0); zero-skipping in EIE (ISCA 2016) and Cambricon-X; ternary keyword-spotting accelerators (from memory).

innovation.key_insight: Adder-only units can skip zero weights in compute, which helps always-on edge accelerators save energy.
innovation.killer_doubt: BitNet zeros are ~1/3 and scattered, so ternary entropy is ~1.58 bits. Run-length coding saves ~0-6% beyond 5-trit packing and breaks random access (estimate).
innovation.decisive_experiment: None needed. Compute the empirical entropy and zero-run-length histogram of released BitNet-b1.58 weights; kill if RLE beats 1.6 bpw by <10%. ~$1k.
innovation.prior_art: Same mechanism as I-06286; BitNet b1.58, llama.cpp TQ1_0, TerEffic and sparse ternary kernels [training knowledge].

title: ZettaCore's molecular redox storage repurposed as a charge-multiplying capacitor coating
idea: ZettaCore stored charge in porphyrin redox molecules on silicon but died on the 400C BEOL thermal budget. Graft thermally stable inorganic redox clusters (polyoxometalates) inside each 3D DRAM capacitor. Each cluster stores several electrons at a fixed potential, adding pseudocapacitance on top of the dielectric's.

physics.key_insight: A POM monolayer (~1e14/cm2, 2 e- each) holds ~32 uC/cm2 in a 0.3 V window, ~15x a 0.5 nm EOT dielectric. That is real only with electrolyte counter-ions.
physics.killer_doubt: Without mobile ions, redox charge images across the dielectric: C = series(C_diel, C_redox) < C_diel, no gain. Ionic electrolytes fail endurance (1e5-1e6 cycles) and ns kinetics.
physics.decisive_experiment: A MIM coupon, TiN/POM monolayer/ZrO2/TiN versus a no-POM control (~$50k): C-V at 1 kHz-100 MHz. Any charge above C_diel*V at 100 MHz would overturn the series argument.
physics.prior_art: ZettaCore porphyrin memory (Bocian/Lindsey); POM flash storage nodes (Busche et al., Nature 2014); triage N-17, N-25 (pseudocapacitive variant dead) [training knowledge].

innovation.key_insight: Redox sites store charge at a fixed potential, offering in principle multi-level plateaus and charge independent of dielectric thickness, aimed squarely at the capacitor charge wall.
innovation.killer_doubt: With no counter-ions, an electron hopping from electrode to cluster stays on one plate: terminal charge remains C_dielectric x V. Ionic compensation makes a pseudocapacitor: ~1e5 cycles versus 1e12+.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Graft Keggin POMs on TiN and cap with 5 nm ZrO2 and TiN. Measure charge versus frequency (1 kHz-100 MHz) and after 1e9 cycles. Stop if charge does not beat the bare MIM at 10 MHz. ~$100k.
innovation.prior_art: ZettaCore porphyrin memory (Lindsey/Bocian); Busche et al., Nature 2014, polyoxometalate flash cells (Glasgow); Phase B N-17 alive-speculative; N-25's pseudocapacitive variant failed on endurance.

title: Copying: passive optical splitters broadcast one weight read to many chips
idea: TRIZ #26 Copying: in data-parallel inference every accelerator holds an identical copy of the weights. Instead, one memory node reads each weight block once and broadcasts it in lockstep to all accelerators through cheap passive 1:16 PON fiber splitters (mass-produced telecom parts). (No new fab: only existing trailing-node capacity.)

physics.key_insight: Same insight as I-05406 at 1:16: one weight read can be broadcast to every data-parallel replica through mass-produced passive splitters.
physics.killer_doubt: PON optics run 10-50 Gb/s (<=6 GB/s) per port against ~2 TB/s of weight reads per accelerator, ~300x short. Moving to DWDM fixes bandwidth but turns this into I-05406.
physics.decisive_experiment: No separate experiment. I-05406's DWDM splitter testbed and receiver cost model settle this one, because telecom PON line rates are fixed.
physics.prior_art: Same as I-05406; telecom XGS-PON and 50G-PON splitter trees (prior knowledge).

innovation.key_insight: The same O(1)-weights insight as I-05406, using mass-produced telecom PON splitters as a cheap broadcast medium.
innovation.killer_doubt: PON optics carry 10-50 Gb/s per wavelength. One accelerator's weight reads (~2 TB/s, ~16 Tb/s) need ~300-1,600 PON lanes per leaf. It duplicates I-05406.
innovation.decisive_experiment: No separate test: fold it into I-05406's link-budget bench. A desk check of whether any PON-class part reaches >=400 Gb/s per fiber through a 1:16 split within budget. Under $10k.
innovation.prior_art: Same as I-05406: Fiber Memory preprint (arXiv 2607.08407), Cerebras SwarmX weight broadcast; Phase B N-80.

title: Plasma-display memory effect: global sustain waveform replaces refresh and transistors
idea: Failure mined: plasma displays held each pixel's state as wall charge under a global AC sustain waveform, with only row and column drivers and no per-pixel transistor, and lost to LCD and OLED on power. Fix: each crosspoint cell pairs a thin threshold switch with a small capacitor in a hysteresis loop. A global sustain clock re-pumps every 1 cell while 0 cells never fire, and coincident row/column pulses set or clear individual cells.

physics.key_insight: A threshold switch plus capacitor under a global AC sustain is a real transistor-free bistable latch, as AC plasma panels showed across ~6e6 subpixels.
physics.killer_doubt: OTS leakage ~0.1 nA drains 1 fF in ~5 us: ~200 kHz sustain at ~16 fJ/firing is ~14 W/GB (DDR5 refresh ~12 mW/GB), ~6e13 firings per decade.
physics.decisive_experiment: Fabricate 100 OTS-plus-1 fF MIM cells (university fab, ~$150k); measure the bistable sustain window versus Vth spread and drift, the minimum sustain frequency at 85 C, and firings to failure.
physics.prior_art: AC plasma display wall-charge memory effect; T-RAM thyristor bistable memory (2000s); OTS crosspoint selector arrays (3D XPoint).

innovation.key_insight: A hysteretic threshold-switch plus capacitor cell, latched by a global AC sustain, needs no access transistor or refresh controller: plasma-display wall-charge memory moved to crosspoints.
innovation.killer_doubt: Sustain re-fires every '1' each cycle. OTS off-current of 1 pA-1 nA (13 fA tail) drains 1 fF in 0.1-100 us, so sustain burns ~20 W-20 kW/Gb (estimate).
innovation.decisive_experiment: Single-cell bench test: an OTS in series with a 10-100 fF MIM capacitor under AC sustain. Measure the bistable window, hold time between pulses, and Ioff after 1e9 fires. ~$100k.
innovation.prior_art: AC plasma display panel memory effect (wall charge); selector-only chalcogenide memory [training knowledge]. A threshold-switch/capacitor sustain RAM was not found.

title: Magnify the draw ratio: fiber-drawn lithography-free memory arrays
idea: Build a centimeter-scale preform holding thousands of channels of semiconductor glass, metal and insulator, thermally draw it 10,000:1 into km fibers so features shrink to sub-micron, then fuse and slice fiber bundles into faceplates where each core is a vertical transistor-capacitor cell addressed by one coarse metallization.

physics.key_insight: Drawn coaxial metal/glass/metal cores yield ~1.5 fF/um, so a 100 um slice gives ~150 fF per core with no HAR etch. Capacitors are free; switches are not.
physics.killer_doubt: Drawn chalcogenide/poly-Si switches leak decades above the ~1e-14 A needed; distorted fused lattices still need aligned litho; 1 um pitch is ~440x below 1b density.
physics.decisive_experiment: $150k university draw tower: a fiber with a drawn semiconductor-core FET; measure Ion/Ioff and off-current at 85 C. Below 1e6 Ion/Ioff or above 1e-13 A off-current kills it.
physics.prior_art: MIT Fink/Abouraddy multimaterial fibers, fiber diodes (Rein et al., Nature 2018); iterative-draw nanowires (Yaman et al., 2011).

innovation.key_insight: Thermal drawing really does shrink cm-scale multi-material preforms to sub-micron features without lithography; fused fiber faceplates are a cheap large-area structuring method.
innovation.killer_doubt: Random access needs row/column lines at cell pitch, which coarse metallization cannot give; at 500 nm core pitch density is ~0.05 GB/cm2, ~100x below 1b DRAM's ~5.5 GB/cm2.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Draw a 100-core preform with semiconductor-glass cores and metal gate sheaths in a university draw tower; measure single-core transistor on/off ratio and storage-node retention at 85 C.
innovation.prior_art: Multimaterial fiber devices (Fink, MIT; Abouraddy, CREOL); silicon-core fibers (Ballato, Clemson); fused fiber-optic faceplates. Fiber memory arrays: none found.

title: Redox pseudocapacitor nanocell replaces 70:1 pillar with planar charge sponge
idea: Effect walk: Faradaic surface redox (pseudocapacitance). Replace the dielectric capacitor with a 5-nm hydrous RuO2 or Ti3C2 MXene film against a nanometre solid proton conductor; fast surface redox stores ~100-1000 uF/cm2 versus ~7 uF/cm2 for ZrO2, so a flat 30x30 nm pad holds ~4-5 fF at 0.5 V.

physics.key_insight: Areal capacitance, not aspect ratio, is the real lever: a 30x30 nm pad at ~500 uF/cm2 would hold ~4.5 fF and delete the 60:1 etch.
physics.killer_doubt: Proton diffusion (D ~1e-8 to 1e-10 cm2/s) across 5 nm takes ~25 us-2.5 ms, 1e3-1e5x too slow; Faradaic films survive ~1e5-1e6 cycles versus >=3e8 needed.
physics.decisive_experiment: Probe-station RuO2 or MXene micro-pads on a thin proton conductor (~$100k): capacitance versus frequency from 1 kHz to 100 MHz, then capacitance retained after 1e8 pulses at 0.5 V.
physics.prior_art: Hydrous RuO2 and MXene micro-supercapacitors; MIT nanosecond protonic programmable resistors (Science 2022) move far fewer ions per pulse at high field (training knowledge).

innovation.key_insight: Planar pseudocapacitance in principle gives ~4-5 fF on a 30 nm pad with no HAR etch. That would be the ideal answer to the capacitor wall.
innovation.killer_doubt: Faradaic redox endures ~1e5-1e6 cycles against the 1e13-1e15 needed. Pseudocapacitor knee frequencies are Hz-kHz, not the ~100 MHz a ns write needs. Hydrous RuO2 needs water in BEOL.
innovation.decisive_experiment: A ~$80k coupon test: ALD RuO2 or MXene on a Nafion-class or solid-acid film, 1 um2 pads, 10 ns pulses at 85 C. Kill if <50% of the charge moves in 10 ns or it fails before 1e9 cycles.
innovation.prior_art: Triage N-25 (pseudocapacitive variant dead on faradaic endurance) and N-17 (ZettaCore molecular redox memory); Gogotsi MXene micro-supercapacitors [training knowledge].

title: Ion-beam ripple self-patterning writes wafer-wide nanoline arrays without masks
idea: Ideal: line arrays that appear by themselves under a flood beam. Closest: off-normal low-energy Ar+ sputtering of an a-Si or metal hard-mask film spontaneously forms Bradley-Harper ripples at 20-40 nm wavelength, phase-locked by a coarse pre-pattern; transfer them as wordline/bitline gratings and repeat rotated 90 degrees for the crossing grid.

physics.key_insight: Bradley-Harper ripples self-organize 20-40 nm gratings in one broad-beam step, and coarse pre-patterns can phase-lock them: a cheap 1D grating source.
physics.killer_doubt: Ripple fields carry ~1-10 line merges per um2 (~1e8/cm2, estimate) versus DSA's still-unadopted ~1/cm2, and each merge shorts a wordline. SAQP already makes DUV gratings without EUV.
physics.decisive_experiment: Make templated Ar+ ripples on a-Si over a 1 cm2 coupon at 30 nm pitch. Count line terminations and merges by SEM over 1e4 um2 and measure LWR; proceed only below ~1e-4 defects/um2.
physics.prior_art: Bradley-Harper theory (1988); Facsko ion-sputtered dots (1999); Cuenat-Aziz templated ripples (2005); DSA as the better-ordered benchmark. From memory.

innovation.key_insight: A flood ion beam self-organizes 20-40 nm gratings in one cheap step; phase-locking to a coarse pre-pattern mirrors graphoepitaxy for block copolymers.
innovation.killer_doubt: Ripple order lengths of ~0.1-1 um imply ~1e8 dislocations/cm2 versus near-zero for DRAM lines; SAQP on ArF already makes array gratings without EUV, so the saving is small.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Broad-beam Ar+ on a-Si over 200 nm-period guide trenches; SEM defect counts over 1 mm2 versus guide period and fluence, against a block-copolymer DSA baseline. ~$80k.
innovation.prior_art: Bradley-Harper theory (1988); HZDR and IOM Leipzig ripple studies; directed self-assembly (IBM, imec, Merck) is the stronger self-patterning route and still unadopted.

title: Ten people, one kernel module: retire weak pages, run 4x tREFI
idea: 10-person constraint: ship software plus a BIOS setting. A kernel module runs a retention test at 4x the refresh interval and retires the ~0.01-0.1% of 4 KB pages that fail (BadRAM-style memmap exclusion). It stores the compressed failing-page list in the DIMM's user-writable SPD bytes so the list travels with the module, then sets tREFI 4x longer.

physics.key_insight: Zero-hardware refresh relief is real: 4x tREFI cuts refresh energy ~75% and recovers most of the 7.6-20% tRFC bandwidth loss if weak pages are mapped out.
physics.killer_doubt: VRT cells keep appearing after profiling; a 4x window gives hammer 4x more ACTs; 0.05% of 16M pages is ~8k entries (~25 KB), far beyond 384 B user SPD.
physics.decisive_experiment: On 20 ECC servers with exposed tREFI, profile at 4x, retire failing pages, then log corrected and uncorrected errors for 90 days at 45-85 C; kill if new weak pages exceed ~1e-6 per day.
physics.prior_art: RAIDR (2012), REAPER reach profiling (2017), AVATAR ECC-triggered row upgrade (2015), BadRAM; overclockers already run maximum tREFI.

innovation.key_insight: Refresh relief with zero hardware: storing the weak-page list in the SPD makes the profile travel with the DIMM. Deployable on any server that exposes a tREFI knob.
innovation.killer_doubt: VRT: Liu 2013 saw new failing cells appear for days, so one-shot profiling at 4x tREFI risks silent corruption. DDR5 on-die ECC hides weak cells. Saving ~3% server power.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Profile 20 DDR5 RDIMMs at 256 ms and retire failing pages, then run 30 days at 4x tREFI with ECC logging. Count new CE/UE per TB-day. Under $60k.
innovation.prior_art: RAPID (HPCA 2006) retention-aware OS placement; RAIDR 2012; REAPER 2017; BadRAM; HARP (on-die ECC profiling); Qimonda per-page refresh patent US7975170 (via search snippet).

title: 1970s CCD memory flipped vertical inside a 3D NAND stack
idea: CCD memories (Intel 2416, Fairchild) died because serial shifting lost to DRAM's random access. Turn a 3D NAND stack into vertical CCD shift registers: 2-phase clock its 300 word-line layers to push 4-level charge packets along an IGZO channel whose low generation current preserves packets for seconds, with one sense amp per string top and no storage transistor or capacitor per bit.

physics.key_insight: Same physics win as I-04377: charge shifts through an IGZO channel, so wear is gate stress only, and IGZO's low generation holds packets for >200 s.
physics.killer_doubt: 2-bit packets over ~300-600 transfers need CTE >=0.9999, but imec's IGZO CCD shows >98% (0.98^300 ~0.2%). 2-phase operation needs built-in barriers that a hole liner cannot implant.
physics.decisive_experiment: Measure 2-bit packet error after 50, 100 and 300 transfers on imec-style vertical IGZO CCD strings at 25-85 C with 1-50 MHz clocks. ~$400k.
physics.prior_art: imec IGZO 3D CCD buffer memory (IEDM 2024; 3D demo 2026; CTE >98%, >4 MHz); our N-08; Intel 2416 and Fairchild CCD memories.

innovation.key_insight: Reusing a 300-layer NAND stack as two-phase CCD strings adds multilevel packets to the no-per-bit-device CCD idea, and an IGZO channel holds packets for seconds.
innovation.killer_doubt: Up to ~300 transfers per read: at imec's >98% CTE ~0.2% survives, and 4-level packets need ~3x tighter loss. 150 ns implies ~1-2 GHz clocks versus 4-6 MHz shown.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Superseded by the I-08879/I-10793 CTE-versus-clock test chip. Revisit only if per-transfer CTE >=0.99999 at >=500 MHz; then measure 4-level packet error rates on a 64-gate string.
innovation.prior_art: imec IGZO CCD buffer memory (IEDM 2024 planar; IMW 2026 vertical, word lines as phase gates); 1970s Intel/Fairchild CCD; in-study I-10793, I-08879.

title: Ink-saver encoding keeps fewest cells in leaky charged state
idea: Like ink-saving fonts that print letters with holes, encode each burst with a low-weight code (e.g., 16b to 18b with per-group inversion) chosen using the die's true-cell/anti-cell map, so as few cells as possible sit in the charged state that leaks; retention failures are nearly all charged-to-discharged.

physics.key_insight: Retention failures are directional (charged to discharged), so true/anti-cell-aware low-weight coding shrinks the vulnerable population at near-zero circuit cost.
physics.killer_doubt: With a retention-tail slope of ~3-5 on log-log, cutting charged cells 35% stretches refresh only ~1.08-1.15x, not 1.5x, while 16b-to-18b costs 12.5% capacity. VRT cells are unaffected.
physics.decisive_experiment: On DRAM Bender with 20 DDR4/DDR5 chips, map true/anti cells, write low-weight versus random data, and sweep refresh from 64 ms to 4 s at 85 C; compare failing-bit counts and VRT share. ~$30k.
physics.prior_art: Liu et al. ISCA 2013 data-dependent retention; bus-invert coding (Stan and Burleson 1995); value-aware refresh-skipping proposals.

innovation.key_insight: Retention failures are almost all charged-to-discharged, so a cell-type-aware low-weight code shrinks the vulnerable population at zero process cost.
innovation.killer_doubt: 8-bit-group inversion cuts charged cells only ~27% (50% to 36%); on a steep retention tail that stretches tREF ~10-17%, below the 12.5% capacity cost of 16-to-18-bit coding.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Replay real traces through the code on DRAM-Bender using true/anti-cell maps of 20 DDR4/DDR5 dies; measure retention failures versus tREF with and without encoding. Kill below 1.3x tREF at equal failures. ~$40k.
innovation.prior_art: Liu et al. ISCA 2013 data-pattern dependence; DDR4/5 data-bus inversion; true/anti-cell characterization (Mutlu group); zero-aware refresh schemes [training knowledge].

title: Data-parallel training: model replicas become each other's ECC
idea: In a 10,000-GPU job, every data-parallel rank holds identical weights. Periodically checksum each 2 MB weight shard, compare checksums across replicas over NVLink or InfiniBand, and repair any mismatched shard by copying it from a majority peer. Local HBM errors are then corrected by replication that already exists.

physics.key_insight: Identical data-parallel replicas are a free majority-vote copy, and checksumming 2 MB shards costs negligible bandwidth while catching silent data corruption.
physics.killer_doubt: In mixed-precision Adam, bf16 weights are ~2 of ~16 bytes/param, and ZeRO shards the rest. One flipped weight pollutes gradients all-reduced to every replica within a step.
physics.decisive_experiment: Inject bit flips into weight HBM in a 64-GPU DDP job and measure steps until cross-replica checksums diverge versus loss corruption. Then test read-only inference replicas, where weights dominate HBM.
physics.prior_art: Fleet silent-data-corruption studies (Meta, Google); ABFT checksums; parameter-hash checks across DP replicas in Megatron-LM.

innovation.key_insight: Data-parallel replicas are a free majority vote: periodic cross-replica weight hashes detect and repair HBM or compute corruption in replicated weights.
innovation.killer_doubt: Already practiced for SDC detection. FSDP/ZeRO shard weights, so true replicas are few; HBM refresh is per-device, not per-region, so no weak-die or relaxed-refresh saving follows.
innovation.decisive_experiment: On a 64-GPU HSDP job, measure the replicated-weight share of HBM, then inject bit errors at 1e-9 to 1e-6 into one replica between hash checks and quantify loss divergence. ~$30k compute.
innovation.prior_art: Laguna M.1 report hashes weights across DP replicas; shadow-replica SDC detection (arXiv 2502.12340); AEGIS (OSDI'26) (via search snippet).

title: Epidemic contact tracing: ECC events trigger blast-radius refresh
idea: Epidemiologists trace and test the contacts of each case. When row r reports a corrected error, controller firmware treats it as a case. It immediately refreshes and scrubs r+-1..+-4 using the physical adjacency map. If more cases appear, it raises local refresh and asks the OS to quarantine (remap) the hot aggressor pages.

physics.key_insight: Corrected errors are free sensors of weak or hammered rows, and DDR5 DRFM can refresh an aggressor's victims on command, so a firmware-only response is feasible.
physics.killer_doubt: DDR5 on-die SEC hides single-bit flips and patrol scrub takes ~24 h per pass, while hammer flips occur within one 32 ms window. Host CEs come too few, too late.
physics.decisive_experiment: Replay published hammer and retention patterns on DRAM Bender with on-die ECC enabled; measure the fraction of rows where a host-visible CE precedes any UE within 32 ms. If <10%, stop.
physics.prior_art: rasdaemon/mcelog CE-threshold page offlining; Meza et al. DSN 2015 page retirement; DDR5 ECS and DRFM; Intel ADDDC.

innovation.key_insight: Every corrected error is a free, localized sensor: CE events plus the physical adjacency map and DDR5 directed refresh give a firmware-only second line of hammer defense.
innovation.killer_doubt: DDR5 on-die ECC hides single-bit flips, so the host's first CE is often already multi-bit; unread victim rows stay invisible until a ~24 h scrub. PRAC handles hammer in-DRAM.
innovation.decisive_experiment: On DRAM-Bender, run U-TRR hammer patterns against DDR5 dies with a host-side CE-triggered neighbor-refresh model; measure the share of campaigns caught before an uncorrectable error. ~$50k.
innovation.prior_art: JEDEC DDR5 DRFM and PRAC; Linux RAS CE-threshold page offlining; CE-pattern UE prediction in fleet studies; ECCploit (S&P 2019) [training knowledge].

title: Flight-recorder DIMM interposer capturing command history before each error
idea: An aircraft's black box records the minutes before an incident. An FPGA DIMM interposer (two board spins, about $250k) keeps a rolling 1-second ring buffer of ACT/REF commands and temperature. On any corrected or uncorrected ECC event it freezes and dumps the buffer. Deployed on ~200 partner servers within the $1M, it would build the first large dataset linking real flips to real access patterns.

physics.key_insight: Linking real field flips to real ACT/REF histories is the one dataset that could show hammer and retention margins are over-designed.
physics.killer_doubt: DDR5 on-die SEC hides single-bit flips. 3,200 DIMMs give ~30-150 CE DIMMs/yr, mostly permanent faults, so few hammer events. A 1 s ring needs ~1-2 GB/s per subchannel.
physics.decisive_experiment: Before building hardware, mine existing MCA/ECS CE logs from one partner fleet (10k+ servers) for row-adjacent clustering. If <1% of CEs look hammer-like, stop.
physics.prior_art: DDR5 protocol analyzers (Teledyne LeCroy/FuturePlus); ETH SAFARI DRAM Bender lab characterization; Meta fleet study (Meza, DSN 2015).

innovation.key_insight: Linking real field flips to their preceding access history would ground hammer and refresh margins in measured, workload-specific distributions instead of worst-case assumptions.
innovation.killer_doubt: DDR5 on-die ECC hides single-bit flips from host triggers; field errors (Google 2009: ~8% of DIMMs/year) are dominated by hard faults, so hammer/retention events stay sparse.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Before building interposers, mine 6 months of MCE/ECS logs plus PEBS access samples on ~200 partner servers; build the DDR5 interposer only if >100 non-hard-fault events appear. ~$100k.
innovation.prior_art: Field studies (Google 2009, Facebook 2015, AMD/LANL 2015); ETH DRAM Bender/SoftMC lab characterization; DDR protocol-analyzer interposers (FuturePlus, Nexus).

title: Eliminate software bloat: memory-footprint bounties for top open-source apps
idea: Eliminate wasted bytes: a $1M bounty fund pays per verified MB saved, times installed base, for merged patches that cut resident memory in Chromium, Electron, Firefox, Kubernetes components and JVM defaults, measured on a public benchmark.

physics.key_insight: Server-side defaults (JVM heap, Kubernetes requests running 2-3x over use) map directly to purchased DRAM; client resident memory does not.
physics.killer_doubt: $1M is tiny beside Chromium's existing memory teams (PartitionAlloc, Memory Saver); devices ship RAM in fixed tiers, so a 10% RSS cut moves ~0% of bits shipped.
physics.decisive_experiment: Measure the server case instead: audit requested vs resident memory for 1,000 Kubernetes pods at three cloud tenants (~$100k) and price the DRAM a right-sizing nudge would free.
physics.prior_art: Chromium PartitionAlloc and Memory Saver tab discarding; Electron footprint work; Google Patch Rewards; Kubernetes VPA right-sizing tools.

innovation.key_insight: Pricing memory savings by installed base is a clean metric for demand reduction, and it costs nothing in wafers.
innovation.killer_doubt: Devices ship in fixed 8/12/16 GB steps, so a 10% RSS cut crosses no step and bits bought fall ~0%. Per-MB bounties are gameable via lazy allocation.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Using 2024-26 telemetry, regress OEM DRAM configs on Chrome and Electron RSS changes such as Memory Saver ($50k). If a 10% RSS drop moves no SKU mix, stop.
innovation.prior_art: Chrome Memory Saver and PartitionAlloc, Edge sleeping tabs, Electron memory work; Gitcoin and bug-bounty funds.

title: Buffet-line broadcast: one DRAM read feeds every accelerator
idea: One buffet tray serves every diner. Likewise, a weight-streaming memory node reads each weight block once and puts it on a shared multidrop optical/SerDes broadcast bus. All N data-parallel accelerators in the pod latch it at the same moment, in a synchronized schedule.

physics.key_insight: Lock-stepped replicas can share one weight copy; the HBM freed for KV cache is real if the broadcast fabric can match each replica's weight-stream rate.
physics.killer_doubt: Memory-bound decode streams weights at HBM rate (~8 TB/s per GPU); scale-up ingress is ~0.9 TB/s per direction, so per-token latency rises ~9x.
physics.decisive_experiment: Simulate Llama-70B and DeepSeek-V3 serving with weights broadcast at 0.9-3.6 TB/s ingress versus local HBM; report tokens/s/user and the batch needed to recover throughput under a 50 ms TPOT SLO. Software, ~$30k.
physics.prior_art: Cerebras weight streaming (MemoryX plus SwarmX broadcast to many CS-2s, 2021); Phase B N-80 is the same idea (prior knowledge).

innovation.key_insight: Inference weights are read-only and identical across replicas, so O(1) copies per pod suffice; broadcasting could free replica HBM for KV cache.
innovation.killer_doubt: Each replica still ingests all weights every step (~2-8 TB/s each) over a bus far slower than local HBM; TP/EP sharding already keeps one weight copy per scale-up domain.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Model a 70B decode pod: per-GPU ingest bandwidth, tokens/s and KV capacity for 8-way broadcast versus TP=8 sharding at batch 1-256, with real NVLink/CPO link budgets. Spreadsheet plus simulator, under $20k.
innovation.prior_art: Phase B N-80; R12 reviews of I-05406, I-03120, I-00277; Cerebras MemoryX/SwarmX weight broadcast; NVLink SHARP multicast; Fiber Memory preprint (arXiv 2607.08407).

title: Float-glass style liquid-gallium printing of atomically thin Ga2O3 channels
idea: As float glass forms on molten tin, kiss the wafer against a liquid Ga/In alloy. Its self-limiting 1.5-3 nm oxide skin transfers at room temperature as a crystalline wide-gap 2D channel for BEOL access transistors.

physics.key_insight: Self-limiting 1.5-3 nm oxide skins print at room temperature with no ALD or epitaxy tool; liquid-metal In2O3/ITO variants make working TFTs.
physics.killer_doubt: Retention is already interface-limited: IGZO is <1 aA, 1e2-3e4 s. As-printed Ga2O3 skin is amorphous with poor mobility. Printing coats only planar tiers, and planar 2T0C never beats vertical density.
physics.decisive_experiment: Print Ga2O3 and In2O3 skins on 100 mm wafers (~$80k); map thickness and Vt sigma; build 2T0C cells and compare retention at 85 C with ALD IGZO. Kill if not >10x better.
physics.prior_art: Zavabeti/Kalantar-Zadeh (RMIT) liquid-metal printed 2D oxides, Science 2017; printed 2D In2O3/ITO transistors; ALD IGZO/IGO gain cells.

innovation.key_insight: Liquid-metal skin transfer lays down a 1.5-3 nm wide-gap oxide at room temperature, with no vacuum or hydrogen: a possible low-capex channel for planar BEOL tiers.
innovation.killer_doubt: imec IGZO 2T0C already retains >400 s, so lower leakage buys almost nothing. Planar transfer cannot coat the 3D holes or recesses where 3D DRAM channels live.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Print Ga2O3 and In2O3 skins onto 100 mm SiO2/Si, pattern 50 nm FETs, and map Vt and 85 C off-current uniformity against ALD IGZO controls. About $150k in a university lab.
innovation.prior_art: Zavabeti et al., Science 2017 (RMIT, Kalantar-Zadeh), liquid-metal printed 2D oxides; printed In2O3 TFTs (Daeneke group); Purdue's atomically thin ALD In2O3 FETs.

title: Display fabs build IGZO memory tiers on Gen-8.5 glass panels
idea: [Box: 2T0C gain charge | IGZO TFT | current sense | many-tier panel-level stack | 2.2 x 2.5 m glass | i-line/ArF dry steppers in existing LCD/OLED fabs] Use idle display-fab capacity to build IGZO gain-cell arrays at ~0.5 um F on huge glass panels, stack 8-16 tiers, and dice them into CXL capacity-tier memory modules.

physics.key_insight: Idle display lines bring depreciated capex, IGZO know-how and no EUV or crucibles; F=0.5 um at 8F2 does give ~62 GB/m2 per tier.
physics.killer_doubt: Display fabs have no ArF; panel steppers resolve ~1.2-1.5 um. At 1.5 um, 8F2 gives ~7 GB/m2 per tier, ~$20/GB at ~$150/m2. Duplicate of I-00145.
physics.decisive_experiment: Settled by I-00145's single-tier panel run, plus a vendor resolution and overlay demo of the best Gen-8.5 stepper at 0.5-0.8 um (~$50k).
physics.prior_art: SEL CAAC-IGZO DOSRAM/NOSRAM; Phase B N-38 panel oxide memory; siblings I-10785, I-04673, I-03879; ram-venture A1-03 killed display-glass memory at 2 um.

innovation.key_insight: Panel lines already run IGZO TFTs on ~5.5 m2 substrates with no EUV. A 2T0C gain cell needs no HAR capacitor, so the cell process matches their toolset.
innovation.killer_doubt: FPD steppers resolve ~1.2-1.5 um, not 0.5 um, and Gen-8.5 has no ArF tool. At F=1.5 um, 8F2 is 18 um2: ~7 GB/m2 per tier, 9x below claim.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Merge into I-00145's partner run. First, a free check: get actual Gen-8.5 stepper resolution and overlay specs from Canon/Nikon. Stop if F is above 0.8 um.
innovation.prior_art: Near-duplicate of I-00145. SEL CAAC-IGZO DOSRAM/NOSRAM; Sharp/JDI memory-in-pixel; Phase B N-36/N-38 glass and panel oxide memory (training knowledge).

title: Zettacore redox molecules: eight built-in reference levels per cell
idea: Failure mined: Zettacore's porphyrin molecular memory stored charge in discrete oxidation states but died on CMOS process heat and slow voltammetric reads. Fix: after the 400 C steps, graft thermally robust ferrocene/porphyrin mixtures with 7 redox couples onto a nanoporous TiN electrode. The sense amp's reference ladder is a reference electrode coated with the same molecules, so the potential plateaus self-calibrate and each cell stores 3 bits.

physics.key_insight: Redox plateaus are intrinsic, identical references. Coating the reference electrode with the same molecules is a clever self-calibration for multi-level sensing.
physics.killer_doubt: A 4F2 cell (F=20 nm) holds ~1,600 molecules, ~230 e- per level at 3 bits. 50 fF needs ~200x surface area. Solid counter-ions at >=1e8 redox/s are unshown.
physics.decisive_experiment: Graft a ferrocene/porphyrin mix on porous TiN under a solid or ionic-gel electrolyte. Measure redox completion at 10-100 ns pulses, 1e10 cycles, and level separation after 400 C. ~$300k.
physics.prior_art: ZettaCore (2000s); Liu et al., Science 2003, porphyrin memory surviving processing (training knowledge); Phase B N-17 (ALIVE-SPECULATIVE) is the re-scoped version.

innovation.key_insight: Coating the reference electrode with the same molecules makes the sense ladder track each redox plateau through temperature and ageing: a genuinely clever self-calibration.
innovation.killer_doubt: Ideal surface redox peaks are ~90 mV wide at 25 C, so seven plateaus need ~1.4 V; counter-ion motion through solid electrolyte has not shown 50 ns switching (N-17's test).
innovation.decisive_experiment: University electrochemistry: graft a 3-couple mixture on porous TiN under a solid polymer electrolyte; pulse 50 ns-1 us; measure charge per plateau, level overlap at 85 C and drift over 1e9 cycles. ~$200k.
innovation.prior_art: ZettaCore porphyrin memory, including multi-state sandwich molecules (Bocian, Lindsey, 2000s) [training knowledge]; study N-17 ZettaCore revival (ALIVE-SPECULATIVE).

title: Minify rank width: one-chip sub-rank access controller
idea: Build an FPGA DIMM controller that addresses each x4 DDR5 chip independently through per-chip command buffering, so a random access activates one chip's row instead of 8-16 chips' rows.

physics.key_insight: Per-chip activation cuts row-activation energy ~8-16x for random 8-64 B gathers (graph, KV); real value only with a custom DIMM/RCD routing per-chip CA.
physics.killer_doubt: Standard DIMMs share CA/CS per rank (PDA is MRS-only), so 'existing DIMMs' fails; a 64 B line from one x4 chip needs BL128 = 20 ns burst and breaks chipkill.
physics.decisive_experiment: Largely settled in literature. If pursued: FPGA board with 16 discrete x4 DDR5 parts on per-chip CA, replay graph/KV traces, measure pJ per useful bit vs a DDR5 subchannel baseline (~$150k).
physics.prior_art: Mini-rank (Zheng, MICRO 2008); MC-DIMM rank subsetting (Ahn); Rambus threaded module; SSA (Udipi, ISCA 2010); DDR5 32-bit subchannels.

innovation.key_insight: Activating one x4 chip per access cuts row-activation energy about 8x for random graph and KV traffic, using commodity DRAM dies with only controller changes.
innovation.killer_doubt: The RCD broadcasts CA to every chip, so custom DIMMs are needed; 64 B from one x4 chip takes 128 beats (~20 ns); total energy falls ~1.5x, not 8x (estimate).
innovation.decisive_experiment: Ramulator/DRAMPower trace study (~$20k) of per-chip activation on graph and KV-cache traces, reporting total energy and tail latency against DDR5 32-bit subchannels.
innovation.prior_art: Mini-rank (Zheng et al., MICRO 2008), HP MC-DIMM (Ahn et al., 2009), single-subarray access (Udipi, ISCA 2010); DDR5 subchannels, HBM pseudo-channels [training knowledge].

title: Endohedral ion-in-cage dipole: one molecule, one bit
idea: Scarcity rule: the bit gets one molecule of space. A metal ion inside an elongated fullerene or nitride-cluster cage (Li+@C70-type) sits in one of two off-center wells, a gate field flips it, and the dipole shifts the threshold of an underlying 2D transistor. No bond breaks, and the cage is chosen for a ~0.8 eV barrier giving ms-s retention.

physics.key_insight: Bond-free ion displacement inside a cage avoids the charge-fluence wear that kills tunnel-write cells, so endurance could genuinely be unlimited.
physics.killer_doubt: Flipping a 0.8 eV well over ~0.2 nm in ns needs ~4 V/nm local field, cage-screened further, above ~1 V/nm breakdown; one dipole moves a 100 nm2 FET ~10 mV.
physics.decisive_experiment: STM on a Li+@C60 or Sc3N@C80 monolayer at 300 K: measure dipole-flip barrier from telegraph lifetimes and the tip switching field; kill if barrier <0.5 eV or field >1 V/nm. ~$150k.
physics.prior_art: Li+@C60 isolated and structurally characterised (Aoyagi et al., Nature Chem 2010); ZettaCore molecular memory; no endohedral-dipole memory array found.

innovation.key_insight: A field-switched ion-in-cage dipole could make a bond-free, wear-free bit at ~1 nm2 with attojoule writes.
innovation.killer_doubt: Lowering a 0.8 eV barrier with dp~e*0.3 nm needs ~3 V/nm, 3x dielectric breakdown, before cage screening. Retention: ~27 s at 300 K, ~0.2 s at 85 C.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Low-temperature STM switching of single Li+@C60/C70 molecules on a gated substrate (~$200k, a university STM). Measure the switching field and barrier; kill if field exceeds 1 V/nm.
innovation.prior_art: Li+@C60 synthesized (Aoyagi et al., Nature Chem 2010); molecular charge memory (ZettaCore porphyrins, 2000s); N@C60 spin-qubit work [training knowledge].

title: Po: a wafer is a napkin — remote-epitaxy peel-and-stack floating-body tiers
idea: Po: a wafer is a napkin you can peel. Extracted: grow 50 nm single-crystal Si films by remote epitaxy through graphene on a reusable donor wafer, peel and laminate 64 of them; each membrane carries capacitor-less floating-body cells defined by one imprint step, and each donor is reused ~100 times.

physics.key_insight: Donor-wafer reuse decouples crystal cost from tier count, and pre-tested single-crystal membranes avoid the Si/SiGe superlattice defects of monolithic 3D DRAM.
physics.killer_doubt: Si remote epitaxy fails through graphene (covalent field is screened). Floating-body cells hold only tens of ms at 85 C; 64 bonds at 99.5% each give 73% stacks.
physics.decisive_experiment: CVD Si on graphene-coated Si(001), check registry by EBSD/XRD (~$80k); in parallel, measure 85 C retention tails on existing SOI floating-body test chips. Either failure kills it.
physics.prior_art: Kong et al., Nat. Mater. 2018: Si/Ge remote epitaxy fails through graphene (via search snippet); Soitec Smart Cut and Canon ELTRAN donor reuse; Z-RAM.

innovation.key_insight: Reusing the donor crystal while stacking single-crystal membranes attacks epi cost. Smart-Cut donor reuse already captures most of that value.
innovation.killer_doubt: Remote epitaxy is shown for polar crystals, not Si. 64 bond and imprint steps make cost linear in tiers (0.99^64 = 53% yield). Floating-body retention failed at Z-RAM.
innovation.decisive_experiment: A ~$300k test: grow Si through monolayer graphene on Si(001), peel it, and check XRD rocking width and DLTS defect density. Then measure floating-body retention at 85 C on 10 transferred films. Kill if >1e9 cm-2 dislocations or <64 ms.
innovation.prior_art: MIT Jeehwan Kim remote epitaxy (polar: GaAs, GaN, LiF); Soitec Smart-Cut donor reuse; NEO 3D X-DRAM and Unisantis DFM floating-body; Innovative Silicon Z-RAM [training knowledge].

title: Plated-wire memory rebuilt as vertical plated vias in 3D stacks
idea: Plated-wire memory (Voyager era) stored bits in the circumferential magnetization of permalloy plated on a wire and read them non-destructively by tilting it with a word strap. Make the wire a vertical copper pillar in a 3D-NAND-style hole lined with circumferentially anisotropic CoFeB, use the stacked tier planes as word straps, write by coincident pillar plus strap current, and read by a small strap pulse that tilts the film and induces a pillar voltage.

physics.key_insight: Circumferential magnetization round a vertical via is a closed-flux, stray-field-free bit; stacked planes as word straps would give 100+ tiers from one hole etch.
physics.killer_doubt: Faraday read fails: 5 nm CoFeB over a 40 nm tier links ~3e-16 Wb, ~0.1 uV per 1 ns tilt; writes need ~0.7 mA per 50 nm pillar (3.5e7 A/cm2).
physics.decisive_experiment: Drop inductive read: test TMR or AMR readout of circumferential domains in electroplated CoFeB/NiFe-lined 50-100 nm vias (~$200k), measuring switching current and thermal stability per tier.
physics.prior_art: Plated-wire memory (UNIVAC, 1960s); in-study I-08865 (DROP, same numbers); Phase B N-82 racetrack in capacitor hole; Parkin racetrack.

innovation.key_insight: Circumferential magnetization round a via is closed-flux and stray-field-free; tier planes as word straps would give 100+ magnetic tiers from one hole etch.
innovation.killer_doubt: Inductive read fails: 5 nm CoFeB on a 40 nm tier links ~3e-16 Wb, ~0.1 uV for a 1 ns partial tilt. Writes need ~0.6 mA per 50 nm pillar.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Not fundable as stated. If revived, drop inductive read: test TMR/AMR readout of circumferential domains in plated NiFe/CoFeB-lined 50-100 nm vias (~$200k), measuring switching current per tier.
innovation.prior_art: Plated-wire memory (UNIVAC, Voyager era); in-study I-08865 (DROP, same mechanism); Phase B N-82 racetrack-in-hole; Parkin racetrack [training knowledge].

title: Smoke detector: radioisotope micro-battery keeps low-leakage cells alive for decades
idea: Random stimulus 'smoke detector' (a tiny Am-241 source runs for decades) -> a Ni-63 or tritium betavoltaic cell in the module package supplies microwatts forever, refreshing an ultra-low-leakage gain-cell array whose retention is ~1000 s. Data survives loss of external power for ~decades with no new memory material.

physics.key_insight: At ~1000 s retention, refresh of a 16 Gb gain-cell array needs only ~0.2-0.7 uW, so retention-mode power is set by the periphery, not the cells.
physics.killer_doubt: A CR2032 (~2.4 kJ) runs 10 uW for ~7 years with no licence. 1 uW from Ni-63 needs ~0.3-1 Ci, against ~15 mCi in licensed ECD sources.
physics.decisive_experiment: Measure the retention-mode power of an IGZO gain-cell macro with gated periphery and negative hold bias. If it is <10 uW per 16 Gb, compare a coin cell with a betavoltaic over 10 years. ~$200k.
physics.prior_art: NVDIMM-N (supercap plus flash backup); Betavolt BV100 Ni-63 cell (~100 uW, 2024); City Labs tritium cells (prior knowledge).

innovation.key_insight: With ~1000 s gain-cell retention, refresh power for a 16 Gb array falls to ~1 uW, so a package-level isotope source could make volatile memory persistent.
innovation.killer_doubt: Periphery standby (charge pumps, references, oscillator) typically draws ~10-100 uW versus betavoltaic tens of nW to ~100 uW; persistence is niche, and NVDIMM supercap-to-NAND already provides it.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Power-gate a gain-cell test array with burst refresh every 300-1000 s; measure average standby power against a commercial tritium or Ni-63 cell's output over a week at 85 C. ~$100k.
innovation.prior_art: City Labs NanoTritium betavoltaics pitched for SRAM/RTC retention; Betavolt BV100 Ni-63 cell; NVDIMM-N supercap backup to NAND (training knowledge).

title: Cochlear amplifier: Hopf-poised sense amp hears sub-femtofarad cells
idea: Cochlear hair cells sit at a Hopf bifurcation, giving huge gain for faint sounds; bias each sense amplifier at the edge of oscillation with a calibrated negative-resistance loop so the tiny bitline perturbation of a ~1 fF cell tips it decisively, with per-amp calibration of the bifurcation point.

physics.key_insight: A latch is already a bifurcation amplifier; calibrating each amp's trip point is offset cancellation, which is the real lever for sub-fF sensing.
physics.killer_doubt: Hopf gain amplifies noise equally, so SNR stays input-referred: 1 fF on a 35 fF bitline gives ~14 mV against ~10-20 mV SA offset; the poise drifts with temperature.
physics.decisive_experiment: SPICE plus a 28 nm MPW: compare a Hopf-poised amp with an offset-cancelled latch on identical 1 fF/35 fF bitlines; measure BER at 85 C and energy per sense. Drop unless Hopf wins >2x.
physics.prior_art: Offset-cancellation sense amps in production DRAM; Hopf-bifurcation hearing models (Hudspeth, Magnasco); charge-transfer pre-sense (Phase B N-04) does this better.

innovation.key_insight: Poising a regenerative amplifier near instability is the right instinct, but the cross-coupled latch already is a saddle-node regenerator; offset cancellation, not bifurcation type, sets sensitivity.
innovation.killer_doubt: DRAM reads a DC step; Hopf gain favours periodic tones. A 1 fF cell on 35 fF gives ~14 mV, comparable to 5-10 mV sigma offset that poise amplifies.
innovation.decisive_experiment: Transient-noise SPICE plus Monte Carlo mismatch of a Hopf-biased versus offset-cancelled latch on a 35 fF bitline; compare BER for 1-2 fF cells. Build an MPW only if Hopf gives >2x margin. ~$20k.
innovation.prior_art: Offset-cancellation sense amps in production DRAM; charge-transfer presensing (study N-04); Hopf hair-cell amplifier circuits in silicon-cochlea work [training knowledge].

title: Blessing in disguise: Geiger-mode avalanche bitline sensing of 100-electron cells
idea: TRIZ #22 Blessing in disguise turns breakdown, normally a failure, into gain: each bitline segment ends in a SPAD-like junction biased just above avalanche breakdown, which a stored packet of ~100 electrons triggers into a full-swing self-quenched pulse, so storage nodes need only ~0.02 fF and can be plain planar diffusions.

physics.key_insight: Avalanche gain makes ~100 stored electrons an almost certain trigger: at PDP 0.5, 1-0.5^100 is ~1. Sensing is not the limit.
physics.killer_doubt: 100 e retained 64 ms needs leakage <=0.13 fA, ~100x below the 13 fA Si tail. Low-DCR SPADs need ~10+ V and um guard rings, not 30-40 nm pitch.
